content.content:
name: Build pgvector-embedded artifacts

# Rebuilds the prebuilt pgvector artifacts vendored in
# packages/pgvector-embedded/prebuilt/<platform>/ for every platform
# embedded-postgres supports. Run on demand (bump pgvector / PG major) or when
# build.sh changes on main. embedded-postgres ships vanilla PG 18 with no
# pgvector, so each cell compiles pgvector against a same-major PostgreSQL (the
# extension ABI is stable within a major) and uploads the result; a final job
# opens a PR with the regenerated artifacts.
#
# Windows (windows-x64) is intentionally NOT built yet — pgvector on Windows
# needs an MSVC/nmake build the bash script doesn't cover. Follow-up.

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      pgvector_version:
        description: pgvector git tag to build
        default: v0.8.1
  push:
    # Branch-scoped on purpose: a bare `paths` filter also matches tag pushes,
    # and GitHub can't diff a freshly-created ref so it ignores the filter and
    # runs anyway — which meant every release-please tag (`lobu-vX.Y.Z`) kicked
    # off a rebuild and opened a churn PR (the builds aren't byte-reproducible).
    # Restricting to `main` excludes tag refs. Only build.sh affects the
    # artifacts, so the workflow file itself is intentionally not a path here.
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - packages/pgvector-embedded/scripts/build.sh

permissions:
  contents: write
  pull-requests: write

env:
  PGVECTOR_VERSION: ${{ inputs.pgvector_version || 'v0.8.1' }}

jobs:
  build:
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - { platform: darwin-arm64, runner: macos-15 }
          # macos-15-intel is GitHub's x86_64 macOS runner. The old macos-13
          # (Intel) image was retired Dec 2025, so that label queues forever.
          # macos-15-intel runs Intel on macOS 15 (available until ~Aug 2027,
          # the last x86_64 macOS image GitHub will offer).
          - { platform: darwin-x64, runner: macos-15-intel }
          - { platform: linux-x64, runner: ubuntu-latest }
          - { platform: linux-arm64, runner: ubuntu-24.04-arm }
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: 22

      - name: Install PostgreSQL 18 dev (macOS)
        if: runner.os == 'macOS'

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Read-only look at the prod org via the existing CLI session. Never echoes the token.
set -uo pipefail
TOKEN=$(python3 -c "
import json,os
d=json.load(open(os.path.expanduser('~/.config/lobu/credentials.json')))
print(d['contexts']['prod']['accessToken'])
")
[ -z "$TOKEN" ] && { echo "NO_TOKEN"; exit 1; }
API="https://app.lobu.ai/api/v1"
ORG=buremba
H=(-H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json")

echo "########## session ##########"
curl -s "${H[@]}" "$API/whoami" | head -c 400; echo
echo
echo "########## agents in $ORG ##########"
curl -s "${H[@]}" "$API/$ORG/agents" | python3 -c "
import json,sys
try: d=json.load(sys.stdin)
except Exception as e: print('parse fail', e); raise SystemExit
ags = d.get('agents', d) if isinstance(d,dict) else d
for a in (ags if isinstance(ags,list) else []):
    print(' ', a.get('id'), '|', a.get('name'), '|', a.get('status',''))
" 2>&1 | head -20

echo
echo "########## chat connections in $ORG ##########"
curl -s "${H[@]}" "$API/$ORG/connections" | python3 -c "
import json,sys
d=json.load(sys.stdin)
cs = d.get('connections', d) if isinstance(d,dict) else d
for c in (cs if isinstance(cs,list) else []):
    print(' id=%s key=%s slug=%s agent=%s status=%s' % (c.get('id'), c.get('connector_key'), c.get('slug'), c.get('agent_id'), c.get('status')))
" 2>&1 | head -30

echo
echo "########## prod UI reachability ##########"
for u in https://app.lobu.ai/ https://app.lobu.ai/lobu https://app.lobu.ai/lobu/api/health https://lobu.ai/ https://lobu.ai/getting-started/; do
  echo "$u -> $(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' --max-time 15 "$u")"
done

content.text:
A lot has landed. Interim report while the last probes finish:

## The headline: `lobu run` is broken on most Linux self-hosts

Two independent blockers on the landing page's own quickstart (`npx @lobu/cli@latest run`), both reproduced against the published 14.7.1:

**1. As root** — `packages/server/src/embedded-runtime.ts:122`, `embeddedPgOptions()` never sets `createPostgresUser`, so `pg.initialise()` throws under uid 0. `git grep createPostgresUser origin/main` finds nothing outside tests. #2153's reporter was at a `root@sqlserver2025:/my-lobu#` prompt.

**2. As non-root — the worse one.** Getting past the root check just moves the failure later:

```
could not load library ".../@embedded-postgres/linux-x64/native/lib/postgresql/vector.so":
/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6: version `GLIBC_2.38' not found
```

Verified straight from the repo — the vendored prebuilt requires `__isoc23_strtol@GLIBC_2.38`, and **both** Linux platforms are affected:

| prebuilt | glibc floor |
|---|---|
| `linux-x64` | **2.38** |
| `linux-arm64` | **2.38** |
| `darwin-*` | n/a |

`build-pgvector-embedded.yml` builds `linux-x64` on `ubuntu-latest`, which is now 24.04 (glibc 2.39) — gcc 13 emits the `__isoc23_*` symbols and the floor got silently uplifted. Last rebuilt in #1106.

Blast radius — anything below glibc 2.38 cannot boot embedded Postgres at all: **Debian 12 bookworm (2.36), Ubuntu 22.04 LTS (2.35), RHEL/Rocky 9 (2.34), Amazon Linux 2023 (2.34)**. `node:22-slim`, the most obvious Docker base, is bookworm. macOS is unaffected, which is why it works on your Mac and why this never showed up locally.

## Chat: both platforms are genuinely live

**Slack — PASS.** I DM'd the hosted bot and got a real answer in 10s: *"Buradayım, çalışıyorum ✅ — CRM ajanı ayakta, ne lazım?"* The z.ai 429 that broke this at 00:41 today has cleared.

**Telegram — PASS.** 54 rows in `channel_messages`, both directions, most recent today 13:15. The #2305 fix is holding. I couldn't send a *new* inbound message myself — `secretToken` is correctly redacted so I can't replay a signed webhook, and the composer ignores synthetic events — so this is verified from real history, not a fresh send by me.

**A bug inside that Telegram history.** The agent told you your conversation URL was `https://app.lobu.ai/workspaces/personal-agent/telegram_6570514069/conversations/...`, you called it out, and it doubled down explaining its own container path. The real builder (`url-builder.ts:348`) produces `/<orgSlug>/agents/<agentId>/conversations/<id>`. The agent has no context carrying the real permalink, so it fabricates one from `/app/workspaces/...`. Those URLs return 200 only because the SPA is a catch-all.

## Still running

opencode is mid-flight on the real landing prompt (it scaffolded `hnwatch` and booted the stack on macOS). The image-boot probe for #2183 and the trixie control (the green half of the glibc red/green) are both in progress. I'll report those, then bring you the fixes and the CI gates.

5:For most users we recommend running Lobu via the [`lobu run`](../README.md) CLI (no Docker needed). Self-hosting in Docker is for operators who want a long-lived deployment without orchestrator overhead.

set -u
step() { echo; echo "########## $* ##########"; }
REPO="lobu-ai/lobu-app"
TAG="14.7.1"
ACCEPT='application/vnd.docker.distribution.manifest.v2+json,application/vnd.oci.image.manifest.v1+json,application/vnd.docker.distribution.manifest.list.v2+json,application/vnd.oci.image.index.v1+json'

apt-get update -qq >/dev/null 2>&1
DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get install -y -qq curl ca-certificates python3 postgresql postgresql-contrib >/dev/null 2>&1
echo "tools: curl=$(command -v curl) python3=$(command -v python3)"

step "pull ghcr layers anonymously (the self-hoster's docker pull path)"
TOKEN=$(curl -s "https://ghcr.io/token?scope=repository:${REPO}:pull&service=ghcr.io" | python3 -c 'import json,sys;print(json.load(sys.stdin)["token"])')
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Accept: $ACCEPT" "https://ghcr.io/v2/${REPO}/manifests/${TAG}" -o /tmp/index.json
AMD=$(python3 -c "import json;m=json.load(open('/tmp/index.json'));print(m['manifests'][0]['digest'] if 'manifests' in m else '')")
if [ -n "$AMD" ]; then
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Accept: $ACCEPT" "https://ghcr.io/v2/${REPO}/manifests/${AMD}" -o /tmp/man.json
else
  cp /tmp/index.json /tmp/man.json
fi
python3 -c "
import json
m=json.load(open('/tmp/man.json'))
ls=m['layers']
print('layers',len(ls),'MB',round(sum(l['size'] for l in ls)/1e6,1))
open('/tmp/layers.txt','w').write('\n'.join(l['digest'] for l in ls))
"

mkdir -p /rootfs
N=0
while read -r d; do
  N=$((N+1))
  curl -sL -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://ghcr.io/v2/${REPO}/blobs/$d" -o /tmp/l.tgz
  tar -xzf /tmp/l.tgz -C /rootfs 2>/dev/null
  printf '\r  extracted %s layers' "$N"
done < /tmp/layers.txt
echo
echo "ROOTFS_OK=$([ -f /rootfs/app/start.sh ] && echo YES || echo NO)"
ls -l /rootfs/usr/local/bin/lobu 2>&1
du -sh /rootfs 2>/dev/null | tail -1

step "mount pseudo-filesystems and enter the image"
mount -t proc proc /rootfs/proc 2>/dev/null || echo "proc mount failed"
mount --rbind /sys /rootfs/sys 2>/dev/null || echo "sys mount failed"
mount --rbind /dev /rootfs/dev 2>/dev/null || echo "dev mount failed"
cp /etc/resolv.conf /rootfs/etc/resolv.conf 2>/dev/null

step "issue #2231: lobu CLI inside the published image"
chroot /rootfs /bin/sh -lc 'command -v lobu; ls -l /usr/local/bin/lobu; node -v'
echo "--- lobu --version ---"
chroot /rootfs /bin/sh -lc 'lobu --version' 2>&1 | head -5
echo "--- lobu --help ---"
chroot /rootfs /bin/sh -lc 'lobu --help' 2>&1 | head -18

step "postgres + pgvector on the host side of the sandbox"
PGVER=$(ls /usr/lib/postgresql 2>/dev/null | head -1); echo "pg major: ${PGVER:-NONE}"
DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get install -y -qq "postgresql-${PGVER}-pgvector" >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo "pgvector OK" || echo "pgvector MISSING"
PGBIN="/usr/lib/postgresql/${PGVER}/bin"
mkdir -p /pgdata && chown postgres:postgres /pgdata
su postgres -c "$PGBIN/initdb -D /pgdata --locale=C --encoding=UTF8" >/dev/null 2>&1
su postgres -c "$PGBIN/pg_ctl -D /pgdata -l /tmp/pg.log -o '-p 5432 -c listen_addresses=127.0.0.1' start" >/dev/null 2>&1
sleep 5
su postgres -c "$PGBIN/psql -p 5432 -c \"ALTER USER postgres PASSWORD 'pw'\"" 2>&1 | head -2
su postgres -c "$PGBIN/psql -p 5432 -c 'CREATE DATABASE lobu'" 2>&1 | head -2
su postgres -c "$PGBIN/psql -p 5432 -d lobu -c 'CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS vector'" 2>&1 | head -3
echo "PG_READY=$(su postgres -c "$PGBIN/psql -p 5432 -d lobu -tAc 'select 1'" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ')"

step "boot the image's own start.sh (migrations + server), inside the chroot"
cat > /rootfs/boot.sh <<'BOOT'
export DATABASE_URL="REDACTED"
export ENCRYPTION_KEY="aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa="
export BETTER_AUTH_SECRET="bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb="
export PUBLIC_GATEWAY_URL="http://localhost:8787/lobu"
export NODE_ENV=production
export LOG_LEVEL=INFO
cd /app && exec bash /app/start.sh
BOOT
nohup chroot /rootfs /bin/bash /boot.sh > /tmp/app.log 2>&1 &

HEALTH=MISS
for i in $(seq 1 100); do
  sleep 5
  code=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' --max-time 5 http://localhost:8787/lobu/api/health 2>/dev/null || echo 000)
  if [ "$code" = "200" ]; then echo "HEALTH_OK after $((i*5))s"; HEALTH=OK; break; fi
  if [ $((i % 10)) -eq 0 ]; then echo "  ...waiting $((i*5))s (http=$code)"; fi
done
echo "IMAGE_HEALTH=$HEALTH"

step "issue #2183: endpoint matrix"
for p in / /lobu /lobu/ /lobu/api/health /api/health /lobu/api/docs /lobu/api/openapi.json /lobu/login /lobu/auth/login; do
  echo "$p -> $(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' --max-time 8 "http://localhost:8787$p" 2>/dev/null)"
done

step "does the ADMIN UI render (not a white screen)?"
curl -s --max-time 10 http://localhost:8787/lobu | head -c 900; echo
echo "--- asset tags ---"
curl -s --max-time 10 http://localhost:8787/lobu | grep -oE '(src|href)="[^"]+\.(js|css)"' | head -8
ASSET=$(curl -s --max-time 10 http://localhost:8787/lobu | grep -oE 'src="[^"]+\.js"' | head -1 | sed 's/src="//;s/"$//')
echo "asset: ${ASSET:-none}"
if [ -n "${ASSET:-}" ]; then
  case "$ASSET" in http*) U="$ASSET";; /*) U="http://localhost:8787$ASSET";; *) U="http://localhost:8787/lobu/$ASSET";; esac
  echo "status: $(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' --max-time 10 "$U")  ctype: $(curl -sI --max-time 10 "$U" | grep -i '^content-type' | tr -d '\r')"
  echo "first bytes: $(curl -s --max-time 10 "$U" | head -c 100)"
fi

step "docker exec <container> lobu providers list (#2231 payoff)"
chroot /rootfs /bin/sh -lc 'DATABASE_URL="REDACTED" lobu providers list' 2>&1 | head -25

step "app log (tail 90)"
tail -90 /tmp/app.log

step "done"

Mechanism nailed:

```
node /tmp/t.mjs  →  ReferenceError: __filename is not defined
bun  /tmp/t.mjs  →  __filename = /private/tmp/t.mjs
```

content.text: I've hit the limit of what's worth chasing before reporting. Let me persist the two critical findings.

input.content:
---
name: project_cli_worker_filename_bun_vs_node
description: 2026-07-30 — EVERY agent turn via `lobu run`/`lobu chat` fails with `__filename is not defined`; published @lobu/worker bundle is bun-targeted, CLI users run it under node. Repros on Node 22 AND 26.
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
---

**`lobu chat` / any agent turn under `lobu run` is broken for every CLI user**, on the
published `@lobu/cli@14.7.1`. Not Node-version-specific — reproduced identically on
**Node 22.22.2 and Node 26.5.0** on macOS (`filename-repro.sh`, both booted OK, both
crashed on the turn).

```
💥 Worker crashed (ReferenceError): __filename is not defined
[worker] Worker execution failed: {"name":"ReferenceError","message":"__filename is not defined"}
```

**Root cause.** `packages/agent-worker/src/embedded/egress-fetch.ts:270` (on `origin/main`):
```ts
undiciPath: createRequire(__filename).resolve("undici"),
```
The file imports `createRequire` from `node:module` but **never defines `__filename`** and
never imports `fileURLToPath`. Compare `packages/server/src/gateway/config/index.ts:21`,
which does it correctly (`const __filename = fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)`).

**Why it was invisible in dev.** The published `@lobu/worker/dist/index.bundle.mjs` (line
3117 carries the same expression) begins:
```
#!/usr/bin/env bun
import { createRequire as __createRequire } from 'module'; const require = __createRequire(import.meta.url);
```
The bundler injected a `require` shim but **not** `__filename`. Verified directly:
`bun t.mjs` → `__filename = /private/tmp/t.mjs`; `node t.mjs` → ReferenceError. The repo runs
everything under bun, so it is green in dev; `npx @lobu/cli` runs it under **node**.
This is the canonical "works from source/bun, broken from the artifact/node" class.

**Trigger path.** `buildEgressFetch()` (`egress-fetch.ts:357`) calls `ensureWorker()` eagerly
`if (httpProxy || httpsProxy)`. A scaffolded project sets `WORKER_ALLOWED_DOMAINS` (allowlist
mode) → gateway sets HTTP_PROXY for the worker → `ensureWorker()` → ReferenceError. So it
fires on the FIRST agent turn of a default `lobu init` project.

**Fix**: one line — `createRequire(import.meta.url)` (accepts a URL directly), or define
`__filename` from `import.meta.url` as the server module does. Then grep the class: any
other bare `__filename`/`__dirname` in ESM-bundled packages.

**UNRESOLVED — why CI is green.** `scripts/cli-smoke.sh:319` DOES run a real worker turn
under `node` (`node "$LOBU_BIN" chat "say the safe word"`), and `:230` DOES set
`WORKER_ALLOWED_DOMAINS=127.0.0.1,localhost`. So the proxy branch should be live there too.
I did not determine the divergence (would need an actual cli-smoke run / full build).
Resolve this BEFORE trusting any new gate — the existing gate looks like it should already
catch this and does not. See [[project_published_artifact_has_no_gate]].

Prod chat is UNAFFECTED (Slack + Telegram both verified replying 2026-07-30) — prod uses the
non-embedded worker deployment, not this embedded egress path.

**Root cause.** `packages/agent-worker/src/embedded/egress-fetch.ts:270` (on `origin/main`):
```ts
undiciPath: createRequire(__filename).resolve("undici"),
```
The file imports `createRequire` from `node:module` but **never defines `__filename`** and
never imports `fileURLToPath`. Compare `packages/server/src/gateway/config/index.ts:21`,
which does it correctly (`const __filename = fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)`).

**Why it was invisible in dev.** The published `@lobu/worker/dist/index.bundle.mjs` (line
3117 carries the same expression) begins:
```
#!/usr/bin/env bun
import { createRequire as __createRequire } from 'module'; const require = __createRequire(import.meta.url);
```
The bundler injected a `require` shim but **not** `__filename`. Verified directly:
`bun t.mjs` → `__filename = /private/tmp/t.mjs`; `node t.mjs` → ReferenceError. The repo runs
everything under bun, so it is green in dev; `npx @lobu/cli` runs it under **node**.
This is the canonical "works from source/bun, broken from the artifact/node" class.

**Trigger path.** `buildEgressFetch()` (`egress-fetch.ts:357`) calls `ensureWorker()` eagerly
`if (httpProxy || httpsProxy)`. A scaffolded project sets `WORKER_ALLOWED_DOMAINS` (allowlist
mode) → gateway sets HTTP_PROXY for the worker → `ensureWorker()` → ReferenceError. So it
fires on the FIRST agent turn of a default `lobu init` project.

**Fix**: one line — `createRequire(import.meta.url)` (accepts a URL directly), or define
`__filename` from `import.meta.url` as the server module does. Then grep the class: any
other bare `__filename`/`__dirname` in ESM-bundled packages.

**UNRESOLVED — why CI is green.** `scripts/cli-smoke.sh:319` DOES run a real worker turn
under `node` (`node "$LOBU_BIN" chat "say the safe word"`), and `:230` DOES set
`WORKER_ALLOWED_DOMAINS=127.0.0.1,localhost`. So the proxy branch should be live there too.
I did not determine the divergence (would need an actual cli-smoke run / full build).
Resolve this BEFORE trusting any new gate — the existing gate looks like it should already
catch this and does not. See [[project_published_artifact_has_no_gate]].

Prod chat is UNAFFECTED (Slack + Telegram both verified replying 2026-07-30) — prod uses the
non-embedded worker deployment, not this embedded egress path.

description: 2026-07-30 — vendored pgvector prebuilts (both Linux arches) require GLIBC_2.38, so `lobu run` cannot boot embedded Postgres on Debian 12 / Ubuntu 22.04 / RHEL 9 / AL2023. Plus a separate uid-0 failure.
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
---

`npx @lobu/cli@latest run` — the landing page's own quickstart — **cannot boot on most
Linux self-hosts**. Two independent blockers, both reproduced against published 14.7.1.

## 1. glibc floor (the big one)

```
could not load library ".../@embedded-postgres/linux-x64/native/lib/postgresql/vector.so":
/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6: version `GLIBC_2.38' not found
```

Verified straight from the repo, no runtime needed:
```
strings packages/pgvector-embedded/prebuilt/linux-x64/vector.so | grep -oE 'GLIBC_[0-9.]+' | sort -V
→ GLIBC_2.2, 2.4, 2.14, GLIBC_2.38
```
The forcing symbol is **`__isoc23_strtol@GLIBC_2.38`** — the classic gcc-13-on-glibc-2.38
accidental uplift. **Both** Linux arches are affected (`linux-x64` AND `linux-arm64`);
`darwin-*` are `.dylib` and unaffected (which is why it always works on the Mac).

Cause: `.github/workflows/build-pgvector-embedded.yml` builds `linux-x64` on
`ubuntu-latest`, which is now 24.04 (glibc 2.39). Artifacts last rebuilt in PR #1106.

Broken everywhere glibc < 2.38: **Debian 12 bookworm (2.36) — including `node:22-slim`,
the most obvious Docker base — Ubuntu 22.04 LTS (2.35), RHEL/Rocky 9 (2.34),
Amazon Linux 2023 (2.34)**. Works on Debian trixie (2.41) / Ubuntu 24.04 (2.39).

Fix: build the Linux prebuilts on an OLD glibc base (pin `ubuntu-22.04`, or build in a
`debian:bullseye` container), not `ubuntu-latest`. Then gate it: assert the max GLIBC
symbol version in the artifact is <= the declared floor, as a step in that workflow —
a `strings | sort -V | tail -1` check is enough and costs nothing.

## 2. uid 0 (root) — separate, earlier failure

```
You are running this script as root. Postgres does not support running as root.
... set the `createPostgresUser` option to true.
```
`embeddedPgOptions()` (`packages/server/src/embedded-runtime.ts:122`) never sets
`createPostgresUser`. `git grep createPostgresUser origin/main` → nothing outside tests.
Root shells are the default on VPS/WSL/LXC/containers; #2153's reporter was at
`root@sqlserver2025:/my-lobu#`. As root you fail here; as non-root you get past it and
fail on the glibc issue above.

Both are invisible to CI because `cli-smoke` runs on a modern-glibc GitHub runner as a
non-root user. See [[project_published_artifact_has_no_gate]] and
[[project_cli_worker_filename_bun_vs_node]].

description: The whole "works from source, broken from the artifact" bug class (#2153, #2186, __filename, glibc) is ungated — cli-smoke runs the monorepo, publish-packages never installs what it published.

- `build-images.yml` self-checks the **worker** image (`docker run --network=none
  lobu-worker:parity-smoke`) but never the **app** image — which is how #2231 (no `lobu`
  on PATH) shipped.

Each of those four axes hides a real, currently-shipping bug:
| axis cli-smoke pins | bug it hides |
|---|---|
| source tree, not tarball | #2186 unpublished private dep; [[project_cli_worker_filename_bun_vs_node]] |
| runs under bun in dev | `__filename` (bun defines it in ESM, node does not) |
| non-root runner | uid-0 embedded-postgres refusal |

`npx @lobu/cli@latest` → `init --yes` → `validate` → `run` → poll `/api/health` → **one real
agent turn** (the turn is what catches `__filename`), run **as root and as non-root**, on an

self-check mirroring the worker one.

`cli-smoke.sh:319` already runs a real worker turn under node with
`WORKER_ALLOWED_DOMAINS` set (`:230`), which should already trip `__filename`. That
divergence is unexplained; see [[project_cli_worker_filename_bun_vs_node]]. A new gate built
on the same assumption may be equally blind.

Already covered, do not rebuild: `release-image-audit.yml` (hourly, green) catches the
`latest`-tag drift of #2184; `message-handler-bridge.test.ts` has 4 tests for #2230.

## Sandbox harness notes (isorun, 2026-07-30)
- `isorun` is an **npm** package (`npx isorun-mcp`), NOT PyPI — `uv tool install isorun` 404s.
- SDK `exec()` dies at a 120s HTTP/2 stream timeout — detach with nohup+setsid and poll.
- It rejects `:latest` tags ("Ambiguous tag"); pin a version.

  anonymously and `chroot` into the reconstituted rootfs — that worked.
- docker-in-docker kills the guest agent even with `--iptables=false`; don't bother.
- Beware `pkill -f "lobu.*run"` — it matches the repo path and killed my own drivers.

All sandboxes torn down (16 total, $0.62). Here's the full picture.

## The answer to "is the CLI working in prod properly"

No. The last released version is broken in two ways that no closed issue covers, and the second one hits **everyone**.

### 1. Every agent turn via the CLI fails — all platforms, all Node versions

```
💥 Worker crashed (ReferenceError): __filename is not defined
```

`packages/agent-worker/src/embedded/egress-fetch.ts:270` on `origin/main`:

```ts
undiciPath: createRequire(__filename).resolve("undici"),
```

It imports `createRequire` but never defines `__filename` — unlike `server/src/gateway/config/index.ts:21`, which derives it from `import.meta.url` correctly.

Why it's invisible in dev — the published `@lobu/worker/dist/index.bundle.mjs` starts:

```
#!/usr/bin/env bun
import { createRequire as __createRequire } from 'module'; const require = __createRequire(import.meta.url);
```

The bundler shimmed `require` but not `__filename`. Verified: `bun t.mjs` → prints the path; `node t.mjs` → ReferenceError. The repo runs under bun; `npx @lobu/cli` runs under Node.

I tested opencode's hypothesis that this was Node 26-specific. It isn't:

| Node | boot | `lobu chat` |
|---|---|---|
| 22.22.2 | OK | ReferenceError |
| 26.5.0 | OK | ReferenceError |

It fires on the first turn of a default `lobu init` project, because the scaffold sets `WORKER_ALLOWED_DOMAINS` → gateway sets `HTTP_PROXY` → `buildEgressFetch` eagerly calls `ensureWorker()` (`egress-fetch.ts:357`). Fix is one line: `createRequire(import.meta.url)`.

### 2. `lobu run` can't boot on most Linux hosts

Two separate blockers. As **root**: `embeddedPgOptions()` (`embedded-runtime.ts:122`) never sets `createPostgresUser`, so Postgres refuses. As **non-root** you get further and hit the real one:

```
strings prebuilt/linux-x64/vector.so | grep GLIBC → GLIBC_2.38   (__isoc23_strtol@GLIBC_2.38)
```

Both Linux arches. `build-pgvector-embedded.yml` builds on `ubuntu-latest`, now 24.04. Dead on **Debian 12 (incl. `node:22-slim`), Ubuntu 22.04 LTS, RHEL 9, Amazon Linux 2023**. macOS unaffected — which is why it works on your machine.

## What is genuinely fine

- **Slack** — DM'd the hosted bot, real answer in 10s: *"Buradayım, çalışıyorum ✅"*. The z.ai 429 has cleared.
- **Telegram** — 54 messages both directions, latest today 13:15. #2305 holds.
- **#2186** — `npx @lobu/cli@latest --version` → 14.7.1 clean on Node 22 and 24.
- **#2184** — ghcr `latest` and `14.7.1` are the same digest; hourly audit green.
- **#2231** — `lobu --version` → 14.7.1 *inside* the published image (I reconstituted its rootfs from ghcr layers and chrooted in).
- **#2230** — 4 regression tests.
- **opencode drove the whole landing prompt to a working project** — init, validate, boot, admin UI, 157 HN stories ingested, 206 events. Only the LLM turn failed.

## The uncomfortable part about "won't break again"

I was going to hand you a post-publish smoke gate. Then I found `cli-smoke.sh:319` **already** runs a real worker turn under `node`, and `:230` **already** sets `WORKER_ALLOWED_DOMAINS`. By my reading it should already trip `__filename` — and CI is green. I could not explain that divergence without a full build, so I stopped rather than guess.

That matters: a new gate built on the same assumption may be equally blind. **Resolving why cli-smoke passes is the prerequisite**, not the gate itself.

Three findings and the harness notes are saved to memory.

**Confidence** — `__filename` and glibc bugs: **95**, reproduced against published 14.7.1 with symbol-level and runtime evidence on two Node majors. Slack/Telegram: **90**, real round trip for Slack, real history for Telegram (I couldn't send fresh inbound — `secretToken` is correctly redacted). Image endpoint matrix for #2183: **25** — never completed, my harness lacked pgvector and the retries died.

**Next, pick from:**
1. Resolve why `cli-smoke` is green despite exercising the crashing path — everything else depends on it.
2. One-line `__filename` fix + grep the class for other bare `__filename`/`__dirname` in ESM-bundled packages.
3. Repin `build-pgvector-embedded.yml` to `ubuntu-22.04` and add a max-GLIBC-symbol assertion on the artifact.
4. Finish the #2183 endpoint matrix against the real image.

Context given: "recently somebody said both docker and cli was broken, telegram was not working in github issues, we fixed them and merged all of them. can we make sure it won't break again?" They supplied isorun sandbox credentials and asked me to "create asndboxes to try lobu in there both in docker and cli and our prompt in the landing page end to end to test it out."

   Second request (scope expansion): "ok you do all extensive testing and even create different projects and run the opencode in there so we can test end to end"

   Mid-turn refinements: use the **locally installed** opencode rather than shipping a key to a sandbox; the testing "should even mind slack code and we should talking to generated slack bot"; "and same with telegram"; "and confirm the ui exists etc".

   Net intent: (a) verify the shipped 14.7.1 CLI + Docker image against the specific closed issues, (b) drive the real landing-page setup prompt end-to-end with a coding agent, (c) actually converse with live Slack and Telegram bots, (d) confirm the UI exists, and (e) design regression gates so these classes of breakage cannot recur.

2. **Key Technical Concepts:**
   - isorun — Firecracker microVM sandboxes; **npm** package (`npx isorun-mcp`), NOT PyPI
   - ESM vs CJS: `__filename` is ambient in CJS and in **bun**'s ESM, but undefined in **Node**'s ESM
   - glibc symbol versioning; `__isoc23_*` symbols introduced by gcc 13 / glibc 2.38
   - OCI/ghcr anonymous pull: token endpoint, manifest index → per-arch manifest → layer blobs; chroot rootfs reconstitution
   - embedded-postgres + vendored pgvector prebuilts; `createPostgresUser` option
   - Lobu egress proxy (`HTTP_PROXY`) gating `ensureWorker()`
   - Lobu hosted chat bot flow: `credentialMode: "hosted"` → `/api/{org}/preview/claims` → `/lobu link <code>`
   - Astro island bundles / minified export-alias tracing to recover the landing prompt
   - Slack MCP, Lobu MCP (`query_sql` with `org_slug`)

3. **Files and Code Sections:**

   - **`packages/agent-worker/src/embedded/egress-fetch.ts`** (THE critical bug, line 270, confirmed on `origin/main`):
     ```ts
     function ensureWorker(): Worker {
       if (egressWorker) return egressWorker;
       const worker = new Worker(WORKER_SOURCE, {
         eval: true,
         workerData: {
           undiciPath: createRequire(__filename).resolve("undici"),
         },
       });
     ```
     Line 43 imports `createRequire` from `node:module`; the file never defines `__filename` nor imports `fileURLToPath`. Trigger at line 357:
     ```ts
     const httpProxy = process.env.HTTP_PROXY || process.env.http_proxy;
     const httpsProxy = process.env.HTTPS_PROXY || process.env.https_proxy || httpProxy;
     // Spawn the shared worker eagerly...
     if (httpProxy || httpsProxy) ensureWorker();
     ```
     Fix: use `createRequire(import.meta.url)` or define `__filename` from `import.meta.url`.

   - **`packages/server/src/gateway/config/index.ts:21`** — the correct pattern for contrast: `const __filename = fileURLToPath(import.meta.url);`

   - **`packages/server/src/embedded-runtime.ts:122`** — root-user bug:
     ```ts
     export function embeddedPgOptions(databaseDir: string, port: number) {
       return {
         databaseDir, user: "postgres", password: "postgres", port,
         persistent: true,
         initdbFlags: ["--locale=C", "--encoding=UTF8"],
       };
     }
     ```
     Missing `createPostgresUser: true` for uid 0. Used at line 211 `const pg = new EmbeddedPostgres(embeddedPgOptions(pgDataDir, pgPort));`

   - **`packages/pgvector-embedded/prebuilt/linux-x64/vector.so`** and `linux-arm64/vector.so` — both require `GLIBC_2.38` via `__isoc23_strtol@GLIBC_2.38`. Built by `.github/workflows/build-pgvector-embedded.yml` on `ubuntu-latest` for `linux-x64`, `ubuntu-24.04-arm` for arm64.

   - **`scripts/cli-smoke.sh`** — the gate that should have caught this. Line 32 `LOBU_BIN="$WT/packages/cli/bin/lobu.js"` (source tree, not tarball); line 230 `echo "WORKER_ALLOWED_DOMAINS=127.0.0.1,localhost"`; line 319 `( cd "$PROJ" && timeout 90 node "$LOBU_BIN" chat "say the safe word" -c local --json )`.

   - **`packages/cli/bin/lobu.js`** — node-version gate only rejects `major < 22`; Node 25 is allowed to boot (documented: "25 boots but has no isolated-vm build"). `packages/cli/src/internal/node-version.ts` has `MIN_NODE_MAJOR = 22`, `SANDBOX_GAP_NODE_MAJOR = 25`, `sandboxAvailableForNode()`, surfaced in `commands/dev.ts:142` and `commands/doctor.ts:41`.

   - **`packages/server/src/utils/url-builder.ts:348`** — the real permalink shape the Telegram agent failed to use:

6. **All user messages:**

7. **Pending Tasks:**

Before the opening turn ended I had said I'd "bring you the fixes and the CI gates", and earlier flagged an open question I deliberately did not decide alone: "whether the root fix and the CI gate go up as two PRs now, or whether you want to see the gate design first."

Specifically: confirmed the published `@lobu/worker/dist/index.bundle.mjs:3117` carries `undiciPath: createRequire(__filename).resolve("undici")` with a `#!/usr/bin/env bun` shebang and a `require` shim but no `__filename` shim; proved the mechanism with `node /tmp/t.mjs` → ReferenceError vs `bun /tmp/t.mjs` → `__filename = /private/tmp/t.mjs`; read the repro results showing identical failure on Node 22 and 26; traced the trigger to `egress-fetch.ts:357`; and discovered that `cli-smoke.sh` already does the seemingly-sufficient thing (real worker turn under node at `:319`, `WORKER_ALLOWED_DOMAINS` at `:230`) yet stays green — which I left explicitly unexplained.

description: "The whole \"works from source, broken from the artifact\" bug class (#2153, #2186, __filename, glibc) is ungated — cli-smoke runs the monorepo, publish-packages never installs what it published."

Every "can't get started" issue shares ONE shape: **works from the monorepo, broken from
the published artifact.** Nothing in CI installs and boots what was actually shipped.

- `scripts/cli-smoke.sh` sets `LOBU_BIN="$WT/packages/cli/bin/lobu.js"` — it walks the whole
  command surface, but against the **source tree**, on the runner's pinned Node 22, as a
  **non-root** user, on a **modern-glibc** GitHub runner.
- `.github/workflows/publish-packages.yml` publishes and never installs the result.
- `build-images.yml` self-checks the **worker** image (`docker run --network=none
  lobu-worker:parity-smoke`) but never the **app** image — which is how #2231 (no `lobu`
  on PATH) shipped.

Each of those four axes hides a real, currently-shipping bug:
| axis cli-smoke pins | bug it hides |
|---|---|
| source tree, not tarball | #2186 unpublished private dep; [[project_cli_worker_filename_bun_vs_node]] |
| runs under bun in dev | `__filename` (bun defines it in ESM, node does not) |
| non-root runner | uid-0 embedded-postgres refusal |
| modern-glibc runner | [[project_pgvector_prebuilt_glibc_238_floor]] |

**Gate worth adding** — a post-publish smoke that, in a clean container, does
`npx @lobu/cli@latest` → `init --yes` → `validate` → `run` → poll `/api/health` → **one real
agent turn** (the turn is what catches `__filename`), run **as root and as non-root**, on an
**old-glibc base** (`node:22-bookworm-slim`) as well as a new one. Plus an app-image
self-check mirroring the worker one.

**Do not build that gate until you know why the EXISTING gate is green** —
`cli-smoke.sh:319` already runs a real worker turn under node with
`WORKER_ALLOWED_DOMAINS` set (`:230`), which should already trip `__filename`. That
divergence is unexplained; see [[project_cli_worker_filename_bun_vs_node]]. A new gate built
on the same assumption may be equally blind.

Already covered, do not rebuild: `release-image-audit.yml` (hourly, green) catches the
`latest`-tag drift of #2184; `message-handler-bridge.test.ts` has 4 tests for #2230.

## Sandbox harness notes (isorun, 2026-07-30)
- `isorun` is an **npm** package (`npx isorun-mcp`), NOT PyPI — `uv tool install isorun` 404s.
- SDK `exec()` dies at a 120s HTTP/2 stream timeout — detach with nohup+setsid and poll.

name: project_pgvector_prebuilt_glibc_238_floor
description: "2026-07-30 — vendored pgvector prebuilts (both Linux arches) require GLIBC_2.38, so `lobu run` cannot boot embedded Postgres on Debian 12 / Ubuntu 22.04 / RHEL 9 / AL2023. Plus a separate uid-0 failure."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 82368b87-6555-4432-bce4-6459714348f7
  modified: 2026-07-30T23:15:53.973Z
---

`npx @lobu/cli@latest run` — the landing page's own quickstart — **cannot boot on most
Linux self-hosts**. Two independent blockers, both reproduced against published 14.7.1.

## 1. glibc floor (the big one)

```
could not load library ".../@embedded-postgres/linux-x64/native/lib/postgresql/vector.so":
/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6: version `GLIBC_2.38' not found
```

Verified straight from the repo, no runtime needed:
```
strings packages/pgvector-embedded/prebuilt/linux-x64/vector.so | grep -oE 'GLIBC_[0-9.]+' | sort -V
→ GLIBC_2.2, 2.4, 2.14, GLIBC_2.38
```
The forcing symbol is **`__isoc23_strtol@GLIBC_2.38`** — the classic gcc-13-on-glibc-2.38
accidental uplift. **Both** Linux arches are affected (`linux-x64` AND `linux-arm64`);
`darwin-*` are `.dylib` and unaffected (which is why it always works on the Mac).

Cause: `.github/workflows/build-pgvector-embedded.yml` builds `linux-x64` on
`ubuntu-latest`, which is now 24.04 (glibc 2.39). Artifacts last rebuilt in PR #1106.

Broken everywhere glibc < 2.38: **Debian 12 bookworm (2.36) — including `node:22-slim`,
the most obvious Docker base — Ubuntu 22.04 LTS (2.35), RHEL/Rocky 9 (2.34),
Amazon Linux 2023 (2.34)**. Works on Debian trixie (2.41) / Ubuntu 24.04 (2.39).

Fix: build the Linux prebuilts on an OLD glibc base (pin `ubuntu-22.04`, or build in a
`debian:bullseye` container), not `ubuntu-latest`. Then gate it: assert the max GLIBC
symbol version in the artifact is <= the declared floor, as a step in that workflow —
a `strings | sort -V | tail -1` check is enough and costs nothing.

## 2. uid 0 (root) — separate, earlier failure

```
You are running this script as root. Postgres does not support running as root.
... set the `createPostgresUser` option to true.
```
`embeddedPgOptions()` (`packages/server/src/embedded-runtime.ts:122`) never sets
`createPostgresUser`. `git grep createPostgresUser origin/main` → nothing outside tests.
Root shells are the default on VPS/WSL/LXC/containers; #2153's reporter was at
`root@sqlserver2025:/my-lobu#`. As root you fail here; as non-root you get past it and
fail on the glibc issue above.

Both are invisible to CI because `cli-smoke` runs on a modern-glibc GitHub runner as a
non-root user. See [[project_published_artifact_has_no_gate]] and
[[project_cli_worker_filename_bun_vs_node]].

name: project_cli_worker_filename_bun_vs_node
description: "2026-07-30 — EVERY agent turn via `lobu run`/`lobu chat` fails with `__filename is not defined`; published @lobu/worker bundle is bun-targeted, CLI users run it under node. Repros on Node 22 AND 26."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project

**`lobu chat` / any agent turn under `lobu run` is broken for every CLI user**, on the
published `@lobu/cli@14.7.1`. Not Node-version-specific — reproduced identically on
**Node 22.22.2 and Node 26.5.0** on macOS (`filename-repro.sh`, both booted OK, both
crashed on the turn).

```
💥 Worker crashed (ReferenceError): __filename is not defined
[worker] Worker execution failed: {"name":"ReferenceError","message":"__filename is not defined"}
```

**Root cause.** `packages/agent-worker/src/embedded/egress-fetch.ts:270` (on `origin/main`):
```ts
undiciPath: createRequire(__filename).resolve("undici"),
```
The file imports `createRequire` from `node:module` but **never defines `__filename`** and
never imports `fileURLToPath`. Compare `packages/server/src/gateway/config/index.ts:21`,
which does it correctly (`const __filename = fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)`).

**Why it was invisible in dev.** The published `@lobu/worker/dist/index.bundle.mjs` (line
3117 carries the same expression) begins:
```
#!/usr/bin/env bun
import { createRequire as __createRequire } from 'module'; const require = __createRequire(import.meta.url);
```
The bundler injected a `require` shim but **not** `__filename`. Verified directly:
`bun t.mjs` → `__filename = /private/tmp/t.mjs`; `node t.mjs` → ReferenceError. The repo runs
everything under bun, so it is green in dev; `npx @lobu/cli` runs it under **node**.
This is the canonical "works from source/bun, broken from the artifact/node" class.

**Trigger path.** `buildEgressFetch()` (`egress-fetch.ts:357`) calls `ensureWorker()` eagerly
`if (httpProxy || httpsProxy)`. A scaffolded project sets `WORKER_ALLOWED_DOMAINS` (allowlist
mode) → gateway sets HTTP_PROXY for the worker → `ensureWorker()` → ReferenceError. So it
fires on the FIRST agent turn of a default `lobu init` project.

**Fix**: one line — `createRequire(import.meta.url)` (accepts a URL directly), or define
`__filename` from `import.meta.url` as the server module does. Then grep the class: any
other bare `__filename`/`__dirname` in ESM-bundled packages.

**UNRESOLVED — why CI is green.** `scripts/cli-smoke.sh:319` DOES run a real worker turn
under `node` (`node "$LOBU_BIN" chat "say the safe word"`), and `:230` DOES set
`WORKER_ALLOWED_DOMAINS=127.0.0.1,localhost`. So the proxy branch should be live there too.
I did not determine the divergence (would need an actual cli-smoke run / full build).
Resolve this BEFORE trusting any new gate — the existing gate looks like it should already
catch this and does not. See [[project_published_artifact_has_no_gate]].

Prod chat is UNAFFECTED (Slack + Telegram both verified replying 2026-07-30) — prod uses the
non-embedded worker deployment, not this embedded egress path.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Is `__filename is not defined` in the agent worker Node-26-specific, or does it
# also hit the supported Node 22 line? Boots the SAME scaffolded project under
# each Node major and sends one chat turn.
set -uo pipefail
PROJ=/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-burakemre-Code-lobu/82368b87-6555-4432-bce4-6459714348f7/scratchpad/e2e/opencode-run/hnwatch
GT=/opt/homebrew/bin/gtimeout

run_case() {
  local label="$1" nodebin="$2" port="$3"
  echo
  echo "########## $label ##########"
  export PATH="$nodebin:/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin:/opt/homebrew/bin"
  hash -r
  echo "node: $(node -v)"
  rm -rf "$PROJ/.lobu"
  cd "$PROJ" || return 1
  PORT="$port" nohup $GT 420 npx -y @lobu/cli@latest run --port "$port" > "/tmp/run-$label.log" 2>&1 &
  local ok=MISS
  for i in $(seq 1 60); do
    sleep 5
    if [ "$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' --max-time 4 "http://localhost:$port/health" 2>/dev/null)" = "200" ]; then ok=OK; break; fi
  done
  echo "BOOT_$label=$ok"
  if [ "$ok" = "OK" ]; then
    echo "--- lobu chat ---"
    $GT 180 npx -y @lobu/cli@latest chat "Reply with exactly: PONG42" 2>&1 | grep -viE '^npm (warn|notice)' | head -25
    echo "CHAT_EXIT_$label=$?"
    echo "--- worker crash lines in run log ---"
    grep -iE "Worker crashed|__filename|ReferenceError" "/tmp/run-$label.log" | head -6
  else

## computer-use
You have a computer-use MCP available (tools named `mcp__computer-use__*`). It lets you take screenshots of the user's desktop and control it with mouse clicks, keyboard input, and scrolling.

**Pick the right tool for the app.** Each tier trades speed/precision against coverage:

1. **Dedicated MCP for the app** — if the task is in an app that has its own MCP (Slack, Gmail, Calendar, Linear, etc.) and that MCP is connected, use it. API-backed tools are fast and precise.
2. **Chrome MCP** (`mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`) — if the target is a web app and there's no dedicated MCP for it, use the browser tools. DOM-aware, much faster than clicking pixels. If the Chrome extension isn't connected, ask the user to install it rather than falling through to computer use.
3. **Computer use** — for native desktop apps (Maps, Notes, Finder, Photos, System Settings, any third-party native app) and cross-app workflows. Computer use IS the right tool here — don't decline a native-app task just because there's no dedicated MCP for it.

This is about what's available, not error handling — if a dedicated MCP tool errors, debug or report it rather than silently retrying via a slower tier.

**Look before you assert.** If the user asks about app state (what's open, what's connected, what an app can do), take a screenshot and check before answering. Don't answer from memory — the user's setup or app version may differ from what you expect. If you're about to say an app doesn't support an action, that claim should be grounded in what you just saw on screen, not general knowledge. Similarly, `list_granted_applications` or a fresh `screenshot` is cheaper than a wrong assertion about what's running.

**Loading via ToolSearch — load in bulk, not one-by-one:** if computer-use tools are in the deferred list, load them ALL in a single ToolSearch call: `{ query: "computer-use", max_results: 30 }`. The keyword search matches the server-name substring in every tool name, so one query returns the entire toolkit. Don't use `select:` for individual tools — that's one round-trip per tool.

**Access flow:** before any computer-use action you must call `request_access` with the list of applications you need. The user approves each application explicitly, and you may need to call it again mid-task if you discover you need another application.

**Tiered apps:** some apps are granted at a restricted tier based on their category — the tier is displayed in the approval dialog and returned in the `request_access` response:
- **Browsers** (Safari, Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Arc, etc.) → tier **"read"**: visible in screenshots, but clicks and typing are blocked. You can read what's already on screen. For navigation, clicking, or form-filling, use the claude-in-chrome MCP (tools named `mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`; load via ToolSearch if deferred).
- **Terminals and IDEs** (Terminal, iTerm, VS Code, JetBrains, etc.) → tier **"click"**: visible and left-clickable, but typing, key presses, right-click, modifier-clicks, and drag-drop are blocked. You can click a Run button or scroll test output, but cannot type into the editor or integrated terminal, cannot right-click (the context menu has Paste), and cannot drag text onto them. For shell commands, use the Bash tool.
- **Everything else** → tier **"full"**: no restrictions.

The tier is enforced by the frontmost-app check: if a tier-"read" app is in front, `left_click` returns an error; if a tier-"click" app is in front, `type` and `right_click` return errors. <!-- Per-repo agent rules loaded into every Claude Code session in this repo. Inlines AGENTS.md (shared project rules) first, then layers local-only notes below. User memory entries live under ~/.claude/projects/.../memory/. Don't add anything here unless it's only relevant to Claude agent specific. If other harnesses like pi or codex need it, modify AGENTS.md -->

@AGENTS.md

content.content:
## Repo map
- Bun workspace under `packages/*`; TS source is in `src`, tests in `__tests__`.
- Main packages: `core` shared types/utils, `plugin-api` native plugin contracts, `plugin-host` deterministic plugin composition, `server` gateway + embedded runtime, `agent-worker` Lobu agent execution, `connectors` built-in connectors, `owletto` frontend submodule.
- Before editing a package, read its nearest `AGENTS.md` if present.
- `docs/GOTCHAS.md` collects the mechanical traps (build, SQL, testing, submodule, browser) that have each cost a debugging session. Skim the section for the surface you are touching before you start, and grep it when something looks inexplicable.

## Hard invariants
- **Never write to `~/Code/lobu` directly — work in a worktree.** Run `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` first, and never `git switch` in the main checkout.
- One branch = one concern (not one file). Tangential task → commit/push/open current work, then branch fresh from `main`. Split only for genuinely independent concerns or an unreviewable diff.
- **Multi-replica correctness is mandatory.** Never put shared required state in an in-memory Map/singleton another replica must read or mutate. If a feature relies on cross-pod visibility, use Postgres-mediated state/signal.
- **`events` is append-only.** Never `DELETE FROM events`; tombstone/supersede instead.
- **Request paths never aggregate history.** No `GROUP BY`, `DISTINCT ON`, per-row `regexp_*`, or leading-wildcard `LIKE` over an append-only / run-history table (`events`, `agent_transcript_snapshot`, `session_calls`, …) on a user-facing read path. History only grows, so read-time aggregation cost grows with it while the answer stays bounded. Materialize the row or counter at WRITE time and read it back by index; run the one-time aggregation in a migration, never per request. Aggregating bounded config tables (`connections`, `watchers`, `agent_users`) is fine.
- **Never bulk-delete prod `organization` rows**, including zero-activity ones — empty-looking orgs are frequently real human signups. Surface them one at a time for confirmation.
- **Workers never receive real credentials.** They may receive only placeholders/proxied access. The only exceptions are device-pinned connectors and short-lived provider-derived credential leases (see `packages/server/AGENTS.md`); a durable stored credential is never one of them.
- Default to static `import`. New dynamic imports require measured cost justification here or in the package AGENTS plus a rationale comment at the call site. Tests may dynamically import after mocks.
  - Node-version gate exceptions: `packages/cli/bin/lobu.js` defers the existing CLI graph without duplicating it, and `packages/server/src/server-entry.ts` adds an 842-byte gate in front of the 4.34 MB server graph (measured 2026-07-24). Both call sites must stay dependency-free until their checks pass.
- Bug fixes require red→fix→green evidence, with both outputs pasted into the PR body. If you cannot reproduce, stop and report the dead end — do not ship a speculative fix.
- Never report done off a green typecheck. Boot it, exercise every branch you touched, clean up test data. If "compiles" is all you ran, say so explicitly.
- Gates are non-negotiable (sequence in "Ship a change" below). `make pre-pr` builds first — that build step is what protects against a stale-dist false green. `make review` is an LLM verdict only: it does NOT run typecheck/knip/tests and is not proof CI will pass.
- The agent-facing product name is **Behavior**; `watcher` is internal engine/DB vocabulary. It must not appear in MCP tool schemas/names/descriptions, ClientSDK discovery metadata, or the connector-sdk public reaction contract — `make pre-pr` fails on it. Internal identifiers (`actingWatcherId`, table/column names, comments) are fine.
- `make review-fix` is the unposted fixer pass and runs BEFORE the first `make review`; verify its diff and commit it. Never iterate `make review` as a find-fix loop — each posted round costs a review + CI cycle.
- Fix the class, not the instance: on the first hit, grep every other instance and fix in one pass — a diff-scoped reviewer only ever finds the next one. Same root cause twice = stop reviewing, grep-enumerate. A class-wide fix is in scope for the branch that found it and does not count as scope creep.
- **Fail closed on durable dispatch/delivery state.** When a durable coordination or delivery operation fails, its caller must not reinterpret the error as proceed/deliver/skip. Propagate a retry, defer, or terminal-failure outcome with a visible log; if the operation may already have succeeded, reconcile idempotently before retrying. Treat lock timeouts, pool errors, and ambiguous or expired rows as failures, not as "nothing changed."
- **Coordination design brake.** A change that needs a second lock, a second retry/deferral budget, or a prose termination argument to explain why it halts is patching a misplaced check — stop and re-derive where the decision belongs before adding mechanism. Find the chokepoint that already serializes the action (e.g. worker dispatch is serialized by `job-router` on the worker-SSE-owner pod) and put the check there; prefer deleting the state transition over coordinating it, and reuse queue-native retry over hand-rolled hold/requeue.
- **Stage by explicit path; never commit the whole tree of a worktree that hosted other work.** A commit is a snapshot — stale file copies silently revert already-merged PRs. After commit/rebase, `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` must equal the task's intended file list; extra files = stop. Verify a "reverts merged work" review finding by diff direction against `origin/main`, never dismiss it as merge-base noise.

## Ship a change
1. `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` → work in `.claude/worktrees/<slug>/`.
2. Reproduce the bug (red) before fixing it. Fix, then prove green.
3. Test: `make test-unit` (no DB) / `make test-integration` (needs `DATABASE_URL` with pgvector). One file: `bun test <path>`, or `cd packages/server && bunx vitest run <path>` for vitest suites.
4. `make pre-pr` — build, typecheck, knip, lint, exposed-surface naming.
5. `make review-fix` on the settled diff and verify what it changed — it edits the working tree, so re-read the files before trusting them.
6. Stage by explicit path (`git add -- <paths>`, never `-A`), commit, then confirm `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` is exactly your intended file list. Extra files = stop.
7. `git push -u origin <branch>` → `gh pr create` (fill `.github/pull_request_template.md`; conventional-commit title, e.g. `fix(server): …`).
8. `make review` **once** on the settled HEAD. It posts the `pi-review` status, which is a REQUIRED check.
9. Merge squash once CI is green: `gh pr merge <n> --squash --admin`. Never `--admin` past a check that has not reported.
10. Prod-visible surface? Verify it live after rollout. Set a self-rescheduling `ScheduleWakeup` (~1500s) carrying the rollout gate: poll the deployed SHA, then `git merge-base --is-ancestor "$MERGE_SHA" "$DEPLOYED_SHA"` with `MERGE_SHA=$(gh pr view <n> --json mergeCommit --jq .mergeCommit.oid)`. Two ways this gate silently never opens — **gate on the squash commit, not your branch head** (a squash merge writes a new commit with no ancestry link to the branch, so the branch head exits 1 forever: PR #2280 has identical trees and still fails), and **keep that argument order** (merge commit first; reversed, it accepts a stale deploy). Run the live check when it lands, and write the result back to memory.

## Agent workflow
- Do only what was asked. Delete ephemeral files you create. Do not create `*.md` unless asked.
- Prefer `bun`; do not use npm/yarn/pnpm for repo work.
- Fix unused params by deleting them, not `_`-prefixing.
- Never `git stash`; use WIP commits and squash later.
- Never resolve merge conflicts in the GitHub web UI (it has silently dropped 1000+ lines of feature work). Rebase locally against `origin/main`, then diff against the last real feature commit before squashing — except on submodule-pointer branches, where you must `git merge` (see `docs/GOTCHAS.md`, "Submodule & cross-repo").
- Run mandated gates automatically; never ask permission to run one.
- Show the diff, not a summary. Before claiming done — on your own work or a dispatched agent's — surface `git status` plus `git diff --stat <base>...HEAD`. An agent's self-report is a claim; the diff is the evidence.
- UI PRs owe before/after screenshots, and `gh` cannot upload images inline. Capture before shots from the unmodified branch and after shots from the same booted app (auth recipe in `docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md`), base64-embed the PNGs into one self-contained HTML comparison page, publish it as a claude.ai artifact, and link it from the PR.
- Any subagent with write access (Edit/Write/Bash) runs in its own worktree; only grep/read agents share the parent. Two writing agents must NEVER share a worktree — they overwrite each other's uncommitted work.
- Dispatch code-writing agents through `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` and brief them with the absolute `.claude/worktrees/<slug>/` path. Only task-setup does the submodule branch pinning, post-init `bun install`, `.env` copy, and port allocation.
- Do repetitive multi-file edits (renames, signature changes, import rewrites) inline or with one script. Reserve subagents for read-only breadth or genuinely isolated parallel work.
- Before adding an env var, grep for the one the codebase already reads. Do not rename existing vars to a "cleaner" convention unasked.
- Deleting code needs structural evidence (dangling import, completed migration, superseded impl). Low prod usage is not a delete signal; trace the workflow, not just the import graph — docs and help text are load-bearing too.
- **Absence is never proven by a grep on a working tree.** To prove code does *not* exist, run `git fetch -q origin && git grep <pattern> origin/main` — the fetch is load-bearing, `origin/main` itself goes stale. Applies to every existence check, including the deletion-evidence rule above.
- Slack link pasted (`slack.com/archives/…?thread_ts=`) → run `scripts/slack-thread-viewer.js "<link>"` first.
- To drive the user's real logged-in browser, use the paired Owletto extension — recipe in `docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md`. Do **not** assume CDP/browser-auth is required.
- Unsure in planning → ask before making conflicting or irreversible choices. Mid-execution, block on a question only for irreversible/destructive actions or decisions that are genuinely the user's; for reversible choices with a clear recommended option, take it and flag the choice in your summary.

## Session efficiency
- Never poll in the foreground (`sleep`/`until`/`while` wait loops, repeated `tail`). Run long waits (dev-server boot, CI, deploys) in the background and act on the completion notification.
- Prefer DOM reads (`get_page_text`, `read_page`, `javascript_tool`) over screenshots; screenshot only when visual layout itself is under test. Screenshots are the #1 context-bloat source.
- Read a file before editing it, and re-read it after any external change (a fixer pass, another agent, a rebase). Blind edits fail and cost a retry round-trip.
- Read PR status compactly: `gh pr view <n> --json number,title,isDraft,mergeStateStatus,reviewDecision` plus `gh pr checks <n> --required`. Never `--json statusCheckRollup` — measured on PR 2280 it is 7520 bytes against 861, 8.7x larger and less legible.
- Batch narrow fixes into one commit, verified once at the end of the batch — not per fix. It never justifies skipping a reproducer or a correctness-critical test. For a one-line or config-only change, take one CI snapshot and move on.

Two ways this gate silently never opens — **gate on the squash commit, not your branch head** (a squash merge writes a new commit with no ancestry link to the branch, so the branch head exits 1 forever: PR #2280 has identical trees and still fails), and **keep that argument order** (merge commit first; reversed, it accepts a stale deploy). Run the live check when it lands, and write the result back to memory.

## Agent workflow
- Do only what was asked. Delete ephemeral files you create. Do not create `*.md` unless asked.
- Prefer `bun`; do not use npm/yarn/pnpm for repo work.
- Fix unused params by deleting them, not `_`-prefixing.
- Never `git stash`; use WIP commits and squash later.
- Never resolve merge conflicts in the GitHub web UI (it has silently dropped 1000+ lines of feature work). Rebase locally against `origin/main`, then diff against the last real feature commit before squashing — except on submodule-pointer branches, where you must `git merge` (see `docs/GOTCHAS.md`, "Submodule & cross-repo").
- Run mandated gates automatically; never ask permission to run one.
- Show the diff, not a summary. Before claiming done — on your own work or a dispatched agent's — surface `git status` plus `git diff --stat <base>...HEAD`. An agent's self-report is a claim; the diff is the evidence.
- UI PRs owe before/after screenshots, and `gh` cannot upload images inline. Capture before shots from the unmodified branch and after shots from the same booted app (auth recipe in `docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md`), base64-embed the PNGs into one self-contained HTML comparison page, publish it as a claude.ai artifact, and link it from the PR.
- Any subagent with write access (Edit/Write/Bash) runs in its own worktree; only grep/read agents share the parent. Two writing agents must NEVER share a worktree — they overwrite each other's uncommitted work.
- Dispatch code-writing agents through `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` and brief them with the absolute `.claude/worktrees/<slug>/` path. Only task-setup does the submodule branch pinning, post-init `bun install`, `.env` copy, and port allocation.
- Do repetitive multi-file edits (renames, signature changes, import rewrites) inline or with one script. Reserve subagents for read-only breadth or genuinely isolated parallel work.
- Before adding an env var, grep for the one the codebase already reads. Do not rename existing vars to a "cleaner" convention unasked.
- Deleting code needs structural evidence (dangling import, completed migration, superseded impl). Low prod usage is not a delete signal; trace the workflow, not just the import graph — docs and help text are load-bearing too.
- **Absence is never proven by a grep on a working tree.** To prove code does *not* exist, run `git fetch -q origin && git grep <pattern> origin/main` — the fetch is load-bearing, `origin/main` itself goes stale. Applies to every existence check, including the deletion-evidence rule above.
- Slack link pasted (`slack.com/archives/…?thread_ts=`) → run `scripts/slack-thread-viewer.js "<link>"` first.
- To drive the user's real logged-in browser, use the paired Owletto extension — recipe in `docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md`. Do **not** assume CDP/browser-auth is required.
- Unsure in planning → ask before making conflicting or irreversible choices. Mid-execution, block on a question only for irreversible/destructive actions or decisions that are genuinely the user's; for reversible choices with a clear recommended option, take it and flag the choice in your summary.

## Session efficiency
- Never poll in the foreground (`sleep`/`until`/`while` wait loops, repeated `tail`). Run long waits (dev-server boot, CI, deploys) in the background and act on the completion notification.
- Prefer DOM reads (`get_page_text`, `read_page`, `javascript_tool`) over screenshots; screenshot only when visual layout itself is under test. Screenshots are the #1 context-bloat source.
- Read a file before editing it, and re-read it after any external change (a fixer pass, another agent, a rebase). Blind edits fail and cost a retry round-trip.
- Read PR status compactly: `gh pr view <n> --json number,title,isDraft,mergeStateStatus,reviewDecision` plus `gh pr checks <n> --required`. Never `--json statusCheckRollup` — measured on PR 2280 it is 7520 bytes against 861, 8.7x larger and less legible.
- Batch narrow fixes into one commit, verified once at the end of the batch — not per fix. It never justifies skipping a reproducer or a correctness-critical test. For a one-line or config-only change, take one CI snapshot and move on.

permissions:

env:
  PGVECTOR_VERSION: ${{ inputs.pgvector_version || 'v0.8.1' }}

jobs:
  build:
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - { platform: darwin-arm64, runner: macos-15 }
          # macos-15-intel is GitHub's x86_64 macOS runner. The old macos-13
          # (Intel) image was retired Dec 2025, so that label queues forever.
          # macos-15-intel runs Intel on macOS 15 (available until ~Aug 2027,
          # the last x86_64 macOS image GitHub will offer).
          - { platform: darwin-x64, runner: macos-15-intel }
          - { platform: linux-x64, runner: ubuntu-latest }
          - { platform: linux-arm64, runner: ubuntu-24.04-arm }
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: 22

      - name: Install PostgreSQL 18 dev (macOS)
        if: runner.os == 'macOS'
        run: |
          brew install postgresql@18
          echo "PG_CONFIG=$(brew --prefix postgresql@18)/bin/pg_config" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      - name: Install PostgreSQL 18 dev (Linux)
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: |
          # Use the official pgdg setup script rather than a hand-rolled
          # curl|gpg --dearmor pipe: the latter intermittently fails on GitHub
          # runners with "gpg: cannot open '/dev/tty'". The script adds the
          # repo + key non-interactively.
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y postgresql-common
          sudo /usr/share/postgresql-common/pgdg/apt.postgresql.org.sh -y
          sudo apt-get install -y postgresql-server-dev-18 build-essential
          echo "PG_CONFIG=/usr/lib/postgresql/18/bin/pg_config" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      - name: Build pgvector artifact
        run: |
          chmod +x packages/pgvector-embedded/scripts/build.sh
          PLATFORM=${{ matrix.platform }} packages/pgvector-embedded/scripts/build.sh

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: pgvector-${{ matrix.platform }}
          # The platform-specific library plus the shared control/SQL (vendored
          # once at the prebuilt root). The least-common-ancestor is `prebuilt/`,
          # so the artifact lays out as `<platform>/vector.*`, `vector.control`,
          # `vector--*.sql`.
          path: |
            packages/pgvector-embedded/prebuilt/${{ matrix.platform }}
            packages/pgvector-embedded/prebuilt/vector.control
            packages/pgvector-embedded/prebuilt/vector--*.sql
          if-no-files-found: error

  open-pr:
    needs: build
    runs-on: blacksmith-4vcpu-ubuntu-2404
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

content.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Build the pgvector artifact for the current platform and stage it under
# prebuilt/<platform>/.
#
# embedded-postgres ships PostgreSQL 18.x with NO pg_config and NO server
# headers, so pgvector cannot be compiled against it directly. Instead we build
# against a separately-installed PostgreSQL of the SAME MAJOR version (18.x) and
# rely on the extension ABI being stable within a major — a library built
# against any 18.x loads into embedded-postgres's 18.x. (Validated locally:
# Homebrew PG 18.1's vector.dylib loaded into embedded-postgres PG 18.3.)
#
# Requirements (provided per CI matrix cell):
#   - pg_config for PostgreSQL 18 on PATH, or PG_CONFIG pointing at it
#   - a C toolchain (make + cc)
#
# Usage:
#   PGVECTOR_VERSION=v0.8.1 packages/pgvector-embedded/scripts/build.sh
set -euo pipefail

PGVECTOR_VERSION="${PGVECTOR_VERSION:-v0.8.1}"
PG_CONFIG="${PG_CONFIG:-pg_config}"

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
PKG_ROOT="$(cd "${SCRIPT_DIR}/.." && pwd)"

# Platform key must match embedded-postgres's package suffix and Node's
# process.platform-process.arch (darwin-arm64, darwin-x64, linux-x64, linux-arm64).
node_platform() { node -e 'process.stdout.write(`${process.platform}-${process.arch}`)'; }
PLATFORM="${PLATFORM:-$(node_platform)}"
OUT_DIR="${PKG_ROOT}/prebuilt/${PLATFORM}"

PG_MAJOR="$("${PG_CONFIG}" --version | sed -E 's/^PostgreSQL ([0-9]+).*/\1/')"
if [[ "${PG_MAJOR}" != "18" ]]; then
  echo "ERROR: pg_config reports PostgreSQL ${PG_MAJOR}, expected 18 (embedded-postgres major). Set PG_CONFIG." >&2
  exit 1
fi

echo "==> pgvector ${PGVECTOR_VERSION} for ${PLATFORM} against $(${PG_CONFIG} --version)"

WORK="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "${WORK}"' EXIT
git clone --depth 1 --branch "${PGVECTOR_VERSION}" https://github.com/pgvector/pgvector.git "${WORK}/pgvector"

# OPTFLAGS="" strips pgvector's default `-march=native`. These artifacts are
# redistributed and loaded on arbitrary user CPUs, so a binary tuned to the CI
# runner's microarchitecture would SIGILL on older hardware. Build for the
# baseline target instead; the perf delta is negligible next to portability.
make -C "${WORK}/pgvector" PG_CONFIG="${PG_CONFIG}" OPTFLAGS=""

PKGLIBDIR="$(${PG_CONFIG} --pkglibdir)"
SHARED_DIR="${PKG_ROOT}/prebuilt"

rm -rf "${OUT_DIR}"
mkdir -p "${OUT_DIR}" "${SHARED_DIR}"

# Stage straight from the build dir — we run `make` but not `make install`, so
# nothing lands in the OS Postgres's pkglibdir/sharedir. The library, control
# file, and generated SQL all sit under the cloned/built pgvector tree.
#
# Compiled extension library is the only PLATFORM-SPECIFIC artifact → goes in
# prebuilt/<platform>/ (name differs per platform via $(DLSUFFIX)).
cp "${WORK}/pgvector/vector"*.so "${OUT_DIR}/" 2>/dev/null || true
cp "${WORK}/pgvector/vector"*.dylib "${OUT_DIR}/" 2>/dev/null || true
# Fall back to an installed copy only if the build dir somehow lacks the lib.
if ! ls "${OUT_DIR}"/vector.* >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  cp "${PKGLIBDIR}/vector".* "${OUT_DIR}/"
fi

# Control + the full-install SQL for the pinned version are byte-identical
# across platforms, so they're vendored ONCE at the prebuilt root (not per
# platform). CREATE EXTENSION at default_version reads vector--<version>.sql
# directly; the vector--A--B.sql upgrade scripts only run on ALTER EXTENSION
# UPDATE, never on a fresh embedded DB, so we don't ship them.
PGVECTOR_SQL_VERSION="${PGVECTOR_VERSION#v}"
cp "${WORK}/pgvector/vector.control" "${SHARED_DIR}/"
cp "${WORK}/pgvector/sql/vector--${PGVECTOR_SQL_VERSION}.sql" "${SHARED_DIR}/"

echo "==> staged $(ls "${OUT_DIR}" | wc -l | tr -d ' ') platform file(s) in ${OUT_DIR}"
ls -1 "${OUT_DIR}" | sed 's/^/    /'

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Build the pgvector artifact for the current platform and stage it under
# prebuilt/<platform>/.
#
# embedded-postgres ships PostgreSQL 18.x with NO pg_config and NO server
# headers, so pgvector cannot be compiled against it directly. Instead we build
# against a separately-installed PostgreSQL of the SAME MAJOR version (18.x) and
# rely on the extension ABI being stable within a major — a library built
# against any 18.x loads into embedded-postgres's 18.x. (Validated locally:
# Homebrew PG 18.1's vector.dylib loaded into embedded-postgres PG 18.3.)
#
# Requirements (provided per CI matrix cell):
#   - pg_config for PostgreSQL 18 on PATH, or PG_CONFIG pointing at it
#   - a C toolchain (make + cc)
#
# Usage:
#   PGVECTOR_VERSION=v0.8.1 packages/pgvector-embedded/scripts/build.sh
set -euo pipefail

PGVECTOR_VERSION="${PGVECTOR_VERSION:-v0.8.1}"
PG_CONFIG="${PG_CONFIG:-pg_config}"

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
PKG_ROOT="$(cd "${SCRIPT_DIR}/.." && pwd)"

# Platform key must match embedded-postgres's package suffix and Node's
# process.platform-process.arch (darwin-arm64, darwin-x64, linux-x64, linux-arm64).
node_platform() { node -e 'process.stdout.write(`${process.platform}-${process.arch}`)'; }
PLATFORM="${PLATFORM:-$(node_platform)}"
OUT_DIR="${PKG_ROOT}/prebuilt/${PLATFORM}"

PG_MAJOR="$("${PG_CONFIG}" --version | sed -E 's/^PostgreSQL ([0-9]+).*/\1/')"
if [[ "${PG_MAJOR}" != "18" ]]; then
  echo "ERROR: pg_config reports PostgreSQL ${PG_MAJOR}, expected 18 (embedded-postgres major). Set PG_CONFIG." >&2
  exit 1
fi

echo "==> pgvector ${PGVECTOR_VERSION} for ${PLATFORM} against $(${PG_CONFIG} --version)"

WORK="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "${WORK}"' EXIT
git clone --depth 1 --branch "${PGVECTOR_VERSION}" https://github.com/pgvector/pgvector.git "${WORK}/pgvector"

# OPTFLAGS="" strips pgvector's default `-march=native`. These artifacts are
# redistributed and loaded on arbitrary user CPUs, so a binary tuned to the CI
# runner's microarchitecture would SIGILL on older hardware. Build for the
# baseline target instead; the perf delta is negligible next to portability.
make -C "${WORK}/pgvector" PG_CONFIG="${PG_CONFIG}" OPTFLAGS=""

PKGLIBDIR="$(${PG_CONFIG} --pkglibdir)"
SHARED_DIR="${PKG_ROOT}/prebuilt"

rm -rf "${OUT_DIR}"
mkdir -p "${OUT_DIR}" "${SHARED_DIR}"

# Stage straight from the build dir — we run `make` but not `make install`, so
# nothing lands in the OS Postgres's pkglibdir/sharedir. The library, control
# file, and generated SQL all sit under the cloned/built pgvector tree.
#
# Compiled extension library is the only PLATFORM-SPECIFIC artifact → goes in
# prebuilt/<platform>/ (name differs per platform via $(DLSUFFIX)).
cp "${WORK}/pgvector/vector"*.so "${OUT_DIR}/" 2>/dev/null || true
cp "${WORK}/pgvector/vector"*.dylib "${OUT_DIR}/" 2>/dev/null || true
# Fall back to an installed copy only if the build dir somehow lacks the lib.
if ! ls "${OUT_DIR}"/vector.* >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  cp "${PKGLIBDIR}/vector".* "${OUT_DIR}/"
fi

# Control + the full-install SQL for the pinned version are byte-identical
# across platforms, so they're vendored ONCE at the prebuilt root (not per
# platform). CREATE EXTENSION at default_version reads vector--<version>.sql
# directly; the vector--A--B.sql upgrade scripts only run on ALTER EXTENSION
# UPDATE, never on a fresh embedded DB, so we don't ship them.
PGVECTOR_SQL_VERSION="${PGVECTOR_VERSION#v}"
cp "${WORK}/pgvector/vector.control" "${SHARED_DIR}/"
cp "${WORK}/pgvector/sql/vector--${PGVECTOR_SQL_VERSION}.sql" "${SHARED_DIR}/"

echo "==> staged $(ls "${OUT_DIR}" | wc -l | tr -d ' ') platform file(s) in ${OUT_DIR}"
ls -1 "${OUT_DIR}" | sed 's/^/    /'
echo "==> staged shared control + SQL in ${SHARED_DIR}"
ls -1 "${SHARED_DIR}"/vector.control "${SHARED_DIR}"/vector--*.sql | sed 's/^/    /'

name: Build pgvector-embedded artifacts

# Rebuilds the prebuilt pgvector artifacts vendored in
# packages/pgvector-embedded/prebuilt/<platform>/ for every platform
# embedded-postgres supports. Run on demand (bump pgvector / PG major) or when
# build.sh changes on main. embedded-postgres ships vanilla PG 18 with no
# pgvector, so each cell compiles pgvector against a same-major PostgreSQL (the
# extension ABI is stable within a major) and uploads the result; a final job
# opens a PR with the regenerated artifacts.
#
# Windows (windows-x64) is intentionally NOT built yet — pgvector on Windows
# needs an MSVC/nmake build the bash script doesn't cover. Follow-up.

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      pgvector_version:
        description: pgvector git tag to build
        default: v0.8.1
  push:
    # Branch-scoped on purpose: a bare `paths` filter also matches tag pushes,
    # and GitHub can't diff a freshly-created ref so it ignores the filter and
    # runs anyway — which meant every release-please tag (`lobu-vX.Y.Z`) kicked
    # off a rebuild and opened a churn PR (the builds aren't byte-reproducible).
    # Restricting to `main` excludes tag refs. Only build.sh affects the
    # artifacts, so the workflow file itself is intentionally not a path here.
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - packages/pgvector-embedded/scripts/build.sh

permissions:
  contents: write
  pull-requests: write

env:
  PGVECTOR_VERSION: ${{ inputs.pgvector_version || 'v0.8.1' }}
