---
name: project_slack_telegram_e2e_verify_2026_07_29
description: 2026-07-29 — ROOT CAUSE FOUND + FIXED (PR #2305, squash 63c7dd519). Chat SDK's pre-dispatch history-cache write silently dropped Telegram/WhatsApp inbound messages; Slack unaffected.
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 05838765-35fd-4133-b449-2ea6731efb06
  modified: 2026-07-29T12:47:43.238Z
---

E2E verification of the chat bots on 2026-07-29 (prod `app.lobu.ai`).

**Slack: WORKING end-to-end.** Sent a live DM to bot `U095U1QTZ7V` (`@lobu`) in workspace
`T09513HDQ77` (lobu-ai.slack.com, connection 390, org `lobu-crm`, agent `crm`).
Round trip 30s. Inbound routing, agent dispatch, and outbound reply all fine.
The reply was a provider error, not a bot failure:
`z.ai returned an error: 429 Weekly/Monthly Limit Exhausted. Your limit will reset at 2026-07-31 04:32:47`
plus a "Manage provider" CTA — i.e. #2280/#2268 error surfacing working as designed
(text traces to `packages/server/src/utils/url-builder.ts:260`).
A 2026-07-27 DM ("naber") got a real 21s Turkish answer + working
"View in Lobu ↗" transcript permalink (#2137), proving the full path when quota is available.

**Real blocker = inference quota, not chat.** `lobu-crm` has NO inference-provider
connection; the model resolves from server-level Z_AI config. Single provider, no failover
→ every agent reply in that org is dead until 2026-07-31 unless a fallback provider is added.
See [[project_agent_model_provider_resolution]] and [[project_inference_providers_feature]].

**Telegram: was implemented but never connected; now connected in `buremba`.**
`packages/connectors/src/telegram.ts` declares `x-lobu-chat-platform: telegram`;
`packages/server/src/gateway/connections/platforms/telegram.ts` is a full 401-line impl
(webhook secret gen/backfill, cloud-mode polling guard, multi-replica lease), registered in
`platforms/index.ts` PLATFORM_REGISTRY. A DB sweep found zero telegram connections anywhere.
On 2026-07-29 I created one in org `buremba`: connection **459**, slug
`agentconn-85045b7a87884eea`, bot `@burembalobubot` (id 8834276769), agent `personal-agent`,
mode `auto` → resolved to webhook `https://app.lobu.ai/lobu/api/v1/webhooks/85045b7a87884eea`
(confirmed via Telegram `getWebhookInfo`).

**TELEGRAM E2E RESULT: INCONCLUSIVE — only ONE real message was ever sent (`/start`), and
its pod is gone. Do NOT record this as "Telegram is broken" without a clean retest.**
Drove the user's real Chrome (Owletto conn 432) to web.telegram.org and opened
`@burembalobubot`. Clicking START sent `/start` at 04:19 (the only genuine send). No reply.
**Correction to an earlier conclusion in this session:** three follow-up "messages"
(`hello, which agent are you?`, `retest 0330`, `ZZMARKER7391`) were NEVER actually sent —
`.message-list-item` contained only `/start`; the text sat in the composer as a draft.
`click_ref` on the send button and a synthetic `KeyboardEvent('Enter')` both failed —
Telegram's React composer ignores untrusted events. Any "no reply" claim based on those
three is void. See [[reference_synthetic_events_dont_send_in_react_composers]].

What IS established:
- Prod runs revision `049ee2ab` and **#2257 IS deployed** (`git merge-base --is-ancestor
  5bc459084 049ee2ab` → true), so the #2230 unrouted-drop fix is live.
- #2257 would not cover this case anyway: it patches the **no-agent-resolved** dead end, but
  conn 459 has `agent_id: personal-agent`, and `resolveAgentId()`
  (`gateway/services/platform-helpers.ts:206`) returns `{source:"connection"}` whenever
  `agentId` is set — so the routed path is taken and the unlinked-notice site is never reached.
- The route works and IS logged: a manual `curl -X POST` to
  `/lobu/api/v1/webhooks/85045b7a87884eea` appeared in pod logs with `res.status: 401`
  (bad secret) — proving requests to that path reach the app and get logged.
- Across 2601 log lines on both live pods there is **no** `/lobu/api/v1/webhooks/` entry from
  Telegram — but both pods are only ~5 min old and the single real `/start` predates them, so
  this proves nothing about that delivery.
- The agent is healthy: `conversations.send({agent_id:"personal-agent"})` → `reply: "pong"` in 3.4s.
- Prod DOES have a live Z_AI 429: repeated `POST /lobu/api/proxy/z-ai/a/personal-agent/
  o/8dc12bdd…/u/watcher_5/chat/completions → 429` in pod logs. So the 429 reaches org
  `buremba` too (via watcher_5), even though direct `conversations.send` succeeded.
### Deep trace (kubectl, prod) — the `/start` delivery DID arrive and returned 200
`POST /lobu/api/v1/webhooks/85045b7a87884eea` from **91.108.5.129** (Telegram IP), valid
secret header, 288-byte body, **HTTP 200**, on pod `frq5m` at 04:34:11 BST. Also confirmed
`[chat-instance-manager] Setting webhook` + `Chat instance started` on `frq5m` ONLY (the
other replica `gtzwv` never started it — fine, since hydration is per-request).

Every layer verified sound by reading the shipped code — **there is NO Chat SDK gap**:
- `@chat-adapter/telegram@4.26.0` `handleWebhook`: verifies secret (timingSafeEqual) → parses
  → `processUpdate` → `handleIncomingMessageUpdate` → `chat.processMessage`. Returns 200.
- `chat/dist` `dispatchToHandlers`: `isDM` → `directMessageHandlers` → Lobu's handler.
- Telegram `isDM(threadId)` = `!chatId.startsWith("-")` → true for a private chat. Correct.
- Lobu registers all three handlers (`message-handler-bridge.ts:428-437`): `onNewMention`,
  `onDirectMessage`, `onSubscribedMessage`. Correct.
- `PROVIDER_QUOTA_EXHAUSTED` is NOT `silent` in AGENT_ERRORS (`core/src/errors.ts:251`); only
  `SESSION_TIMEOUT` is. So a 429 SHOULD post a "Manage provider" card on Telegram too.

**Why no reply: `/start` is not a registered Lobu command and is not a normal message.**
`getMyCommands` returns new/clear/help/status/try/agents/link — **no `/start`**. Telegram's
START button sends exactly `/start`, so it hits the slash-command dispatcher
(`message-handler-bridge.ts:1032`), which has no handler for it. Bare `/start` also fails
`isBotMentioned` (adapter line ~1206 requires `@username` suffix on a bot_command).
`"Processing inbound message"` (the bridge's entry log, :641) never appeared, and 6h of logs
across both pods contain **zero** `platform=telegram` turns.
NOTE: every early return in `chat/dist handleIncomingMessage` (isMe, dedupe) logs at **debug**,
and prod runs at info — so a drop there is invisible. Cannot fully exclude dedupe without
raising LOG_LEVEL.

### CONFIRMED REPRODUCER (05:10 BST, live pods) — ordinary text message IS silently dropped
Sent `KK4477 ping` (plain text, NOT a command) via the browser at 05:10. Verified it really
sent: `.message-list-item` shows `KK4477 ping 05:10` and the draft cleared.
Pod `summaries-app-lobu-app-b99595f9d-66mxl` logged the delivery:
`POST /lobu/api/v1/webhooks/85045b7a87884eea`, `cf-connecting-ip: 91.108.5.129` (Telegram),
valid `x-telegram-bot-api-secret-token`, 279 bytes, **res.status 200**, responseTime 1079ms.
**But NO `"Processing inbound message"` and NO `platform=telegram` anywhere after it.**
The full 90s log window contains only unrelated `watcher_5`/`platform=api` work.
So: adapter accepts + ACKs 200, and the message never reaches
`MessageHandlerBridge.handleMessage`. The drop is inside Chat SDK's
`handleIncomingMessage` → `dispatchToHandlers`, whose early returns (isMe / dedupe /
lock-conflict `handleDrop`) ALL log at **debug** while prod runs at info.
`responseTime: 1079ms` is suspiciously long for a 279-byte parse — consistent with the
`acquireLock`/state-adapter round-trip in `handleDrop`.
PRIME SUSPECT: `handleDrop` lock conflict or the `dedupe:` key in the Postgres state adapter.
NEXT DIAGNOSTIC: raise LOG_LEVEL to debug on the app deploy, resend, and read which early
return fires. Do NOT guess-fix before that line is seen.

**VERDICT: end-to-end is NOT proven, and NOT disproven. `/start` was the wrong test** — it
exercises the command path, not the agent path. No ordinary Telegram text message has ever
reached this bot (synthetic sends failed, see
[[reference_synthetic_events_dont_send_in_react_composers]]).
NEXT: a human sends ordinary text (NOT `/start`) to `@burembalobubot`, then
`kubectl logs -n summaries-prod summaries-app-lobu-app-<pod> --since=5m | grep -aiE "Processing inbound message|platform=telegram"`.
Expect either a turn that 429s (→ Telegram is fine; fix = fallback provider) or a real
drop site. Two candidate gaps to fix regardless:
1. `/start` should be handled (greet + bind), not silently no-op — Telegram's onboarding
   button is the FIRST thing every new user presses.
2. `postToPayloadTarget` (`chat-response-bridge.ts:851`) does `if (target) await target.post()`
   — a null target silently posts nothing, no log, no throw.

### TRAP: `connections.connect()` does NOT start the chat runtime — use `connections.create()`
First attempt used `client.connections.connect({connector_key:"telegram", config})`. It returned
`status: "active"` with `facets.chat: true` and **no error**, but was completely inert:
no webhook registered with Telegram, no `secretToken`, no `chatMetadata`, and
`connections.update({agent_id})` failed with *"agent_id applies only to chat connections
(it sets the chat runtime's fallback agent); this connection has no chat runtime."*
Only `connections.create()` reaches `manage_connections` → `handleCreate`, which checks
`options_schema['x-lobu-chat-platform'] === connector_key` and calls
`upsertByoChatConnection()` (`gateway/connections/chat-connection-service.ts:235`) —
that is what validates the token against the provider, generates `secretToken`, populates
`chatMetadata`, and registers the webhook. `connect()` just writes a DB row.
An `active` chat connection is therefore NOT proof of a running runtime — verify with the
provider (`getWebhookInfo`) or by checking `config.secretToken`/`chatMetadata` exist.
Also: `agent_id` is rejected as an argument to create/connect; set it in a follow-up
`connections.update({connection_id, agent_id})`.

## Gotchas found while verifying
- `channel_messages` has NO `direction` column and stores **inbound only** (`is_bot` was
  false on every one of 10 rows ever). It cannot prove the bot replied — read the Slack
  side (or the conversation transcript) instead.
- `channel_messages` only had rows for workspace `T0BCYB6JV3L` (conn 448); the successful
  conn-390 DM exchange never appeared there. Absence in that table is NOT evidence of failure.
- Two Slack workspaces are live for org `lobu-crm`: conn 390 = `T09513HDQ77` (lobu-ai, the
  one the Slack MCP can reach, bot `U095U1QTZ7V`) and conn 448 = `T0BCYB6JV3L` ("LobuSandbox",
  enterprise install `E0BDSKL1KJL`, bot `U0BECQZCENR`) — the Slack MCP CANNOT reach 448
  (`channel_not_found`).
- Slack/Telegram connections live in org `lobu-crm`, NOT `lobu-team` and NOT `buremba`.
  Use `query_sql` with `org_slug: "lobu-crm"` to see them.
- `client.connections.list()` returns `{connections, total, ...}`, not an array.
- `client.conversations.list()` requires `agent_id`; `limit` is rejected.
- `information_schema` is not in the queryable allowlist; `SELECT *` on a row to learn columns.
- Local dev backend (`:8443`) and the `lobu` CLI (`:8940`) were both down; `.env` here has
  no `DATABASE_URL` and `kubectl` has no cluster access. Lobu MCP `query_sql` was the
  only working DB path.

## RESOLVED — PR #2305 (squash `63c7dd519`), merged 2026-07-29

**Root cause.** Chat SDK writes its message-history cache inside `handleIncomingMessage`
**before** `dispatchToHandlers`, gated only on the adapter's `persistMessageHistory` flag
and with **no try/catch** (`chat/dist/index.js:2966`). `processMessage` catches the throw
and the webhook still answers **200**, so a failing *cache* write silently discards the
user's message. Only **telegram + whatsapp** set that flag (slack/discord/teams/gchat do
not) — exactly why Telegram DMs vanished while Slack worked on the same build. Prod proof:
`POST /lobu/api/v1/webhooks/85045b7a87884eea` from `91.108.5.129`, valid secret, 279 bytes
→ **200** in 1079ms, then NO `"Processing inbound message"` and no `platform=telegram`.

**Fix.** Normalize the flag off in `ChatInstanceManager.createAdapter()` — the single
chokepoint every platform's adapter passes through — via `disableSdkMessageHistory()` in
`gateway/connections/platforms/shared.ts`. Removes a write path, does not add one: nothing
reads that cache (grep `getMessages`/`msg-history` in packages/server/src → zero consumers).
Lobu's durable transcripts are `channel_messages` via `captureChannelMessage` (3 real
consumers: manage_feeds, internal conversations route, read_conversation). Also unpinned the
hardcoded `logger: "warn"` → honours `LOG_LEVEL`; every SDK silent-drop path logs at `debug`,
so the pin made them unreachable at any LOG_LEVEL.
Review: bug_free 96, simplicity 95, slop 0, 0 blockers.

**Do NOT "add persistMessageHistory everywhere".** It is a capability-compensation flag, not
a feature toggle — the SDK's own docstring says to set it only for platforms lacking a
server-side history API (WhatsApp, Telegram). Adding it broadly duplicates stale state.

**Test:** `packages/server/src/gateway/connections/__tests__/inbound-dispatch-parity.test.ts`
drives the REAL Chat SDK through `processMessage`. Red 2 pass/2 fail (both dying at
`chat/dist/index.js:2966`); green 3/3. Mutation-tested (`value: false` → `true` re-breaks it).
One test deliberately pins the raw-SDK drop so the seam can be deleted if upstream fixes it.

**Still open:** ~48 orphaned `msg-history:telegram:6570514069` rows in `chat_state_lists`
(prod db `owletto`) are now permanently dead — safe to delete. Separate consolidation worth
doing: `ConversationStateStore` vs `channel_messages` are two overlapping history stores
(~12 call sites); that is its own branch.

## ✅ PROD E2E VERIFIED (2026-07-29 05:50 UTC, deployed `cc269333e` which contains the fix)

Sent a correctly-signed Telegram webhook to prod. Full trace on
`summaries-app-lobu-app-6cbd9d84bd-*`:
```
[chat-sdk:telegram]   Telegram adapter initialized { botUserId: '8834276769' }
[chat-message-bridge] Processing inbound message          <- NEVER appeared pre-fix
[platform-helpers]    Routing to connection's owning agent
[user-agents-store]   Added agent personal-agent to user telegram/8450689116
[queue-producer]      Enqueued message job 786981, conversation telegram:8450689116
[worker] User prompt: POSTFIX9 verify dispatch...
```
And `channel_messages` now has its FIRST EVER `platform='telegram'` rows — both directions:
- id 69 inbound `POSTFIX9 verify dispatch` (is_bot=false)
- id 70 **agent reply** (is_bot=true) 7s later

Before the fix that same webhook shape returned 200 and produced zero downstream log lines.
Slack re-verified unaffected (`Processing inbound message` 2s after a live DM).
All four prod pages render (connectors/telegram, activity, memory with Person 4358, agents).

Residual (unrelated to this fix): Z_AI quota 429 until 2026-07-31 intermittently fails turns
in BOTH orgs. `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` exists in .env; adding a fallback provider is a prod config
change and was left to the user.

## ✅ REAL-BROWSER E2E VERIFIED 12:46 UTC — plus ONE unexplained drop at 12:31

Deploy at the time: `e89f82c18` (release 14.7.0); `63c7dd519` and `cc269333e` both ancestors.
A genuine human-path send from the user's own Chrome (Owletto conn 432 → web.telegram.org)
of `hey2` round-tripped in **~5s**: webhook 12:46:22 → `Processing inbound message` →
`Routing to connection's owning agent` → `Enqueued message job 793230, conversation
telegram:6570514069` → `Response completed via Chat SDK bridge` 12:46:26.
`channel_messages` 75 (inbound) / 76 (bot reply). So the fix holds for the real user chat
`6570514069`, not just the synthetic `8450689116` used at 05:50.

**The unexplained one:** the user's `hey` at 12:31:25 arrived
(`POST /lobu/api/v1/webhooks/85045b7a87884eea`, 91.108.5.129, valid secret, 271 bytes, **200**,
1134ms) and produced **no** `Processing inbound message` and — decisively — **no
`dedupe:telegram:6570514069:<id>` row in `chat_state_cache`**. Dedupe is written *inside* the
SDK inbound path, so this update never entered it. That is a DIFFERENT drop point from #2305
(which dropped *after* dedupe). It has not reproduced: 3 synthetic replays (plain text, and
`/start`, which now DOES reach `[command-dispatcher] Dispatching command`) and the real browser
send all wrote dedupe rows and processed. The only distinguishing feature of the 12:31 request
is that it was the first hydration of the instance on pod `l56p8` (`Setting webhook` +
`Chat instance started` inside that same request) right as the user was editing the connection
on `/connectors/telegram?tab=settings` — but the 12:36 request on `hfh9w` also cold-hydrated
with `Setting webhook` and processed fine. **Do not write this up as a known bug; it is one
unreproduced loss.** To catch it: the webhook route logs `Inbound platform webhook` but never
what kind of update was dropped — an info-level "update ignored, type=X" in
`chat-instance-manager.handleWebhook` would answer it in one line, since every SDK skip path
logs at debug and prod runs at info.

**Diagnostic recipes that paid off here:**
- `chat_state_cache` (prod db `owletto`, key_prefix `chat-conn`) is the pre/post-dedupe
  tripwire: `dedupe:telegram:<chatId>:<messageId>` present = the SDK inbound path was entered.
  `chat_state_locks` was EMPTY, killing the stale-lock theory.
- Replaying a signed webhook is cheap and safe: POST the update JSON to
  `/lobu/api/v1/webhooks/85045b7a87884eea` with header
  `x-telegram-bot-api-secret-token` (readable from any prior request log line). Use the REAL
  chat id, not an invented one — 05:50's synthetic `8450689116` proved nothing about `6570514069`.
- Payload byte length discriminates update types: `/start` with its `bot_command` entity ≈ 287 B,
  a short plain text ≈ 230–275 B. The 271 B at 12:31 was `hey` (confirmed later from the
  Telegram UI's `.message-list-item`, which is also how you read what the user really sent).
- Bot token is NOT in `connections.config` (it is `secret://connections/<slug>/botToken`), so
  `getWebhookInfo` needs a detour; don't burn time on it.

E2E verification of the chat bots on 2026-07-29 (prod `app.lobu.ai`).

**Slack: WORKING end-to-end.** Sent a live DM to bot `U095U1QTZ7V` (`@lobu`) in workspace
`T09513HDQ77` (lobu-ai.slack.com, connection 390, org `lobu-crm`, agent `crm`).
Round trip 30s. Inbound routing, agent dispatch, and outbound reply all fine.
The reply was a provider error, not a bot failure:
`z.ai returned an error: 429 Weekly/Monthly Limit Exhausted. Your limit will reset at 2026-07-31 04:32:47`
plus a "Manage provider" CTA — i.e. #2280/#2268 error surfacing working as designed
(text traces to `packages/server/src/utils/url-builder.ts:260`).
A 2026-07-27 DM ("naber") got a real 21s Turkish answer + working
"View in Lobu ↗" transcript permalink (#2137), proving the full path when quota is available.

**Real blocker = inference quota, not chat.** `lobu-crm` has NO inference-provider
connection; the model resolves from server-level Z_AI config. Single provider, no failover
→ every agent reply in that org is dead until 2026-07-31 unless a fallback provider is added.
See [[project_agent_model_provider_resolution]] and [[project_inference_providers_feature]].

**Telegram: was implemented but never connected; now connected in `buremba`.**
`packages/connectors/src/telegram.ts` declares `x-lobu-chat-platform: telegram`;
`packages/server/src/gateway/connections/platforms/telegram.ts` is a full 401-line impl
(webhook secret gen/backfill, cloud-mode polling guard, multi-replica lease), registered in
`platforms/index.ts` PLATFORM_REGISTRY. A DB sweep found zero telegram connections anywhere.
On 2026-07-29 I created one in org `buremba`: connection **459**, slug
`agentconn-85045b7a87884eea`, bot `@burembalobubot` (id 8834276769), agent `personal-agent`,
mode `auto` → resolved to webhook `https://app.lobu.ai/lobu/api/v1/webhooks/85045b7a87884eea`
(confirmed via Telegram `getWebhookInfo`).

**TELEGRAM E2E RESULT: INCONCLUSIVE — only ONE real message was ever sent (`/start`), and
its pod is gone. Do NOT record this as "Telegram is broken" without a clean retest.**
Drove the user's real Chrome (Owletto conn 432) to web.telegram.org and opened
`@burembalobubot`. Clicking START sent `/start` at 04:19 (the only genuine send). No reply.
**Correction to an earlier conclusion in this session:** three follow-up "messages"
(`hello, which agent are you?`, `retest 0330`, `ZZMARKER7391`) were NEVER actually sent —
`.message-list-item` contained only `/start`; the text sat in the composer as a draft.
`click_ref` on the send button and a synthetic `KeyboardEvent('Enter')` both failed —
Telegram's React composer ignores untrusted events. Any "no reply" claim based on those
three is void. See [[reference_synthetic_events_dont_send_in_react_composers]].

What IS established:
- Prod runs revision `049ee2ab` and **#2257 IS deployed** (`git merge-base --is-ancestor
  5bc459084 049ee2ab` → true), so the #2230 unrouted-drop fix is live.
- #2257 would not cover this case anyway: it patches the **no-agent-resolved** dead end, but
  conn 459 has `agent_id: personal-agent`, and `resolveAgentId()`
  (`gateway/services/platform-helpers.ts:206`) returns `{source:"connection"}` whenever
  `agentId` is set — so the routed path is taken and the unlinked-notice site is never reached.
- The route works and IS logged: a manual `curl -X POST` to
  `/lobu/api/v1/webhooks/85045b7a87884eea` appeared in pod logs with `res.status: 401`
  (bad secret) — proving requests to that path reach the app and get logged.
- Across 2601 log lines on both live pods there is **no** `/lobu/api/v1/webhooks/` entry from
  Telegram — but both pods are only ~5 min old and the single real `/start` predates them, so
  this proves nothing about that delivery.
- The agent is healthy: `conversations.send({agent_id:"personal-agent"})` → `reply: "pong"` in 3.4s.
- Prod DOES have a live Z_AI 429: repeated `POST /lobu/api/proxy/z-ai/a/personal-agent/
  o/8dc12bdd…/u/watcher_5/chat/completions → 429` in pod logs. So the 429 reaches org
  `buremba` too (via watcher_5), even though direct `conversations.send` succeeded.
### Deep trace (kubectl, prod) — the `/start` delivery DID arrive and returned 200
`POST /lobu/api/v1/webhooks/85045b7a87884eea` from **91.108.5.129** (Telegram IP), valid
secret header, 288-byte body, **HTTP 200**, on pod `frq5m` at 04:34:11 BST. Also confirmed
`[chat-instance-manager] Setting webhook` + `Chat instance started` on `frq5m` ONLY (the
other replica `gtzwv` never started it — fine, since hydration is per-request).

Every layer verified sound by reading the shipped code — **there is NO Chat SDK gap**:
- `@chat-adapter/telegram@4.26.0` `handleWebhook`: verifies secret (timingSafeEqual) → parses
  → `processUpdate` → `handleIncomingMessageUpdate` → `chat.processMessage`. Returns 200.
- `chat/dist` `dispatchToHandlers`: `isDM` → `directMessageHandlers` → Lobu's handler.
- Telegram `isDM(threadId)` = `!chatId.startsWith("-")` → true for a private chat. Correct.
- Lobu registers all three handlers (`message-handler-bridge.ts:428-437`): `onNewMention`,
  `onDirectMessage`, `onSubscribedMessage`. Correct.
- `PROVIDER_QUOTA_EXHAUSTED` is NOT `silent` in AGENT_ERRORS (`core/src/errors.ts:251`); only
  `SESSION_TIMEOUT` is. So a 429 SHOULD post a "Manage provider" card on Telegram too.

**Why no reply: `/start` is not a registered Lobu command and is not a normal message.**
`getMyCommands` returns new/clear/help/status/try/agents/link — **no `/start`**. Telegram's
START button sends exactly `/start`, so it hits the slash-command dispatcher
(`message-handler-bridge.ts:1032`), which has no handler for it. Bare `/start` also fails
`isBotMentioned` (adapter line ~1206 requires `@username` suffix on a bot_command).
`"Processing inbound message"` (the bridge's entry log, :641) never appeared, and 6h of logs
across both pods contain **zero** `platform=telegram` turns.
NOTE: every early return in `chat/dist handleIncomingMessage` (isMe, dedupe) logs at **debug**,
and prod runs at info — so a drop there is invisible. Cannot fully exclude dedupe without
raising LOG_LEVEL.

### CONFIRMED REPRODUCER (05:10 BST, live pods) — ordinary text message IS silently dropped
Sent `KK4477 ping` (plain text, NOT a command) via the browser at 05:10. Verified it really
sent: `.message-list-item` shows `KK4477 ping 05:10` and the draft cleared.
Pod `summaries-app-lobu-app-b99595f9d-66mxl` logged the delivery:
`POST /lobu/api/v1/webhooks/85045b7a87884eea`, `cf-connecting-ip: 91.108.5.129` (Telegram),
valid `x-telegram-bot-api-secret-token`, 279 bytes, **res.status 200**, responseTime 1079ms.
**But NO `"Processing inbound message"` and NO `platform=telegram` anywhere after it.**
The full 90s log window contains only unrelated `watcher_5`/`platform=api` work.
So: adapter accepts + ACKs 200, and the message never reaches
`MessageHandlerBridge.handleMessage`. The drop is inside Chat SDK's
`handleIncomingMessage` → `dispatchToHandlers`, whose early returns (isMe / dedupe /
lock-conflict `handleDrop`) ALL log at **debug** while prod runs at info.
`responseTime: 1079ms` is suspiciously long for a 279-byte parse — consistent with the
`acquireLock`/state-adapter round-trip in `handleDrop`.
PRIME SUSPECT: `handleDrop` lock conflict or the `dedupe:` key in the Postgres state adapter.
NEXT DIAGNOSTIC: raise LOG_LEVEL to debug on the app deploy, resend, and read which early
return fires. Do NOT guess-fix before that line is seen.

**VERDICT: end-to-end is NOT proven, and NOT disproven. `/start` was the wrong test** — it
exercises the command path, not the agent path. No ordinary Telegram text message has ever
reached this bot (synthetic sends failed, see
[[reference_synthetic_events_dont_send_in_react_composers]]).
NEXT: a human sends ordinary text (NOT `/start`) to `@burembalobubot`, then
`kubectl logs -n summaries-prod summaries-app-lobu-app-<pod> --since=5m | grep -aiE "Processing inbound message|platform=telegram"`.
Expect either a turn that 429s (→ Telegram is fine; fix = fallback provider) or a real
drop site. Two candidate gaps to fix regardless:
1. `/start` should be handled (greet + bind), not silently no-op — Telegram's onboarding
   button is the FIRST thing every new user presses.
2. `postToPayloadTarget` (`chat-response-bridge.ts:851`) does `if (target) await target.post()`
   — a null target silently posts nothing, no log, no throw.

### TRAP: `connections.connect()` does NOT start the chat runtime — use `connections.create()`
First attempt used `client.connections.connect({connector_key:"telegram", config})`. It returned
`status: "active"` with `facets.chat: true` and **no error**, but was completely inert:
no webhook registered with Telegram, no `secretToken`, no `chatMetadata`, and
`connections.update({agent_id})` failed with *"agent_id applies only to chat connections
(it sets the chat runtime's fallback agent); this connection has no chat runtime."*
Only `connections.create()` reaches `manage_connections` → `handleCreate`, which checks
`options_schema['x-lobu-chat-platform'] === connector_key` and calls
`upsertByoChatConnection()` (`gateway/connections/chat-connection-service.ts:235`) —
that is what validates the token against the provider, generates `secretToken`, populates
`chatMetadata`, and registers the webhook. `connect()` just writes a DB row.
An `active` chat connection is therefore NOT proof of a running runtime — verify with the
provider (`getWebhookInfo`) or by checking `config.secretToken`/`chatMetadata` exist.
Also: `agent_id` is rejected as an argument to create/connect; set it in a follow-up
`connections.update({connection_id, agent_id})`.

## Gotchas found while verifying
- `channel_messages` has NO `direction` column and stores **inbound only** (`is_bot` was
  false on every one of 10 rows ever). It cannot prove the bot replied — read the Slack
  side (or the conversation transcript) instead.
- `channel_messages` only had rows for workspace `T0BCYB6JV3L` (conn 448); the successful
  conn-390 DM exchange never appeared there. Absence in that table is NOT evidence of failure.
- Two Slack workspaces are live for org `lobu-crm`: conn 390 = `T09513HDQ77` (lobu-ai, the
  one the Slack MCP can reach, bot `U095U1QTZ7V`) and conn 448 = `T0BCYB6JV3L` ("LobuSandbox",
  enterprise install `E0BDSKL1KJL`, bot `U0BECQZCENR`) — the Slack MCP CANNOT reach 448
  (`channel_not_found`).
- Slack/Telegram connections live in org `lobu-crm`, NOT `lobu-team` and NOT `buremba`.
  Use `query_sql` with `org_slug: "lobu-crm"` to see them.
- `client.connections.list()` returns `{connections, total, ...}`, not an array.
- `client.conversations.list()` requires `agent_id`; `limit` is rejected.
- `information_schema` is not in the queryable allowlist; `SELECT *` on a row to learn columns.
- Local dev backend (`:8443`) and the `lobu` CLI (`:8940`) were both down; `.env` here has
  no `DATABASE_URL` and `kubectl` has no cluster access. Lobu MCP `query_sql` was the
  only working DB path.

## RESOLVED — PR #2305 (squash `63c7dd519`), merged 2026-07-29

**Root cause.** Chat SDK writes its message-history cache inside `handleIncomingMessage`
**before** `dispatchToHandlers`, gated only on the adapter's `persistMessageHistory` flag
and with **no try/catch** (`chat/dist/index.js:2966`). `processMessage` catches the throw
and the webhook still answers **200**, so a failing *cache* write silently discards the
user's message. Only **telegram + whatsapp** set that flag (slack/discord/teams/gchat do
not) — exactly why Telegram DMs vanished while Slack worked on the same build. Prod proof:
`POST /lobu/api/v1/webhooks/85045b7a87884eea` from `91.108.5.129`, valid secret, 279 bytes
→ **200** in 1079ms, then NO `"Processing inbound message"` and no `platform=telegram`.

**Fix.** Normalize the flag off in `ChatInstanceManager.createAdapter()` — the single
chokepoint every platform's adapter passes through — via `disableSdkMessageHistory()` in
`gateway/connections/platforms/shared.ts`. Removes a write path, does not add one: nothing
reads that cache (grep `getMessages`/`msg-history` in packages/server/src → zero consumers).
Lobu's durable transcripts are `channel_messages` via `captureChannelMessage` (3 real
consumers: manage_feeds, internal conversations route, read_conversation). Also unpinned the
hardcoded `logger: "warn"` → honours `LOG_LEVEL`; every SDK silent-drop path logs at `debug`,
so the pin made them unreachable at any LOG_LEVEL.
Review: bug_free 96, simplicity 95, slop 0, 0 blockers.

**Do NOT "add persistMessageHistory everywhere".** It is a capability-compensation flag, not
a feature toggle — the SDK's own docstring says to set it only for platforms lacking a
server-side history API (WhatsApp, Telegram). Adding it broadly duplicates stale state.

**Test:** `packages/server/src/gateway/connections/__tests__/inbound-dispatch-parity.test.ts`
drives the REAL Chat SDK through `processMessage`. Red 2 pass/2 fail (both dying at
`chat/dist/index.js:2966`); green 3/3. Mutation-tested (`value: false` → `true` re-breaks it).
One test deliberately pins the raw-SDK drop so the seam can be deleted if upstream fixes it.

**Still open:** ~48 orphaned `msg-history:telegram:6570514069` rows in `chat_state_lists`
(prod db `owletto`) are now permanently dead — safe to delete. Separate consolidation worth
doing: `ConversationStateStore` vs `channel_messages` are two overlapping history stores
(~12 call sites); that is its own branch.

## ✅ PROD E2E VERIFIED (2026-07-29 05:50 UTC, deployed `cc269333e` which contains the fix)

Sent a correctly-signed Telegram webhook to prod. Full trace on
`summaries-app-lobu-app-6cbd9d84bd-*`:
```
[chat-sdk:telegram]   Telegram adapter initialized { botUserId: '8834276769' }
[chat-message-bridge] Processing inbound message          <- NEVER appeared pre-fix
[platform-helpers]    Routing to connection's owning agent
[user-agents-store]   Added agent personal-agent to user telegram/8450689116
[queue-producer]      Enqueued message job 786981, conversation telegram:8450689116
[worker] User prompt: POSTFIX9 verify dispatch...
```
And `channel_messages` now has its FIRST EVER `platform='telegram'` rows — both directions:
- id 69 inbound `POSTFIX9 verify dispatch` (is_bot=false)
- id 70 **agent reply** (is_bot=true) 7s later

Before the fix that same webhook shape returned 200 and produced zero downstream log lines.
Slack re-verified unaffected (`Processing inbound message` 2s after a live DM).
All four prod pages render (connectors/telegram, activity, memory with Person 4358, agents).

Residual (unrelated to this fix): Z_AI quota 429 until 2026-07-31 intermittently fails turns
in BOTH orgs. `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` exists in .env; adding a fallback provider is a prod config
change and was left to the user.

## ✅ REAL-BROWSER E2E VERIFIED 12:46 UTC — plus ONE unexplained drop at 12:31

Deploy at the time: `e89f82c18` (release 14.7.0); `63c7dd519` and `cc269333e` both ancestors.
A genuine human-path send from the user's own Chrome (Owletto conn 432 → web.telegram.org)
of `hey2` round-tripped in **~5s**: webhook 12:46:22 → `Processing inbound message` →
`Routing to connection's owning agent` → `Enqueued message job 793230, conversation
telegram:6570514069` → `Response completed via Chat SDK bridge` 12:46:26.
`channel_messages` 75 (inbound) / 76 (bot reply). So the fix holds for the real user chat
`6570514069`, not just the synthetic `8450689116` used at 05:50.

**The unexplained one:** the user's `hey` at 12:31:25 arrived
(`POST /lobu/api/v1/webhooks/85045b7a87884eea`, 91.108.5.129, valid secret, 271 bytes, **200**,
1134ms) and produced **no** `Processing inbound message` and — decisively — **no
`dedupe:telegram:6570514069:<id>` row in `chat_state_cache`**. Dedupe is written *inside* the
SDK inbound path, so this update never entered it. That is a DIFFERENT drop point from #2305
(which dropped *after* dedupe). It has not reproduced: 3 synthetic replays (plain text, and
`/start`, which now DOES reach `[command-dispatcher] Dispatching command`) and the real browser
send all wrote dedupe rows and processed. The only distinguishing feature of the 12:31 request
is that it was the first hydration of the instance on pod `l56p8` (`Setting webhook` +
`Chat instance started` inside that same request) right as the user was editing the connection
on `/connectors/telegram?tab=settings` — but the 12:36 request on `hfh9w` also cold-hydrated
with `Setting webhook` and processed fine. **Do not write this up as a known bug; it is one
unreproduced loss.** To catch it: the webhook route logs `Inbound platform webhook` but never
what kind of update was dropped — an info-level "update ignored, type=X" in
`chat-instance-manager.handleWebhook` would answer it in one line, since every SDK skip path
logs at debug and prod runs at info.

**Diagnostic recipes that paid off here:**
- `chat_state_cache` (prod db `owletto`, key_prefix `chat-conn`) is the pre/post-dedupe
  tripwire: `dedupe:telegram:<chatId>:<messageId>` present = the SDK inbound path was entered.
  `chat_state_locks` was EMPTY, killing the stale-lock theory.
- Replaying a signed webhook is cheap and safe: POST the update JSON to
  `/lobu/api/v1/webhooks/85045b7a87884eea` with header
  `x-telegram-bot-api-secret-token` (readable from any prior request log line). Use the REAL
  chat id, not an invented one — 05:50's synthetic `8450689116` proved nothing about `6570514069`.
- Payload byte length discriminates update types: `/start` with its `bot_command` entity ≈ 287 B,
  a short plain text ≈ 230–275 B. The 271 B at 12:31 was `hey` (confirmed later from the
  Telegram UI's `.message-list-item`, which is also how you read what the user really sent).
- Bot token is NOT in `connections.config` (it is `secret://connections/<slug>/botToken`), so
  `getWebhookInfo` needs a detour; don't burn time on it.

Both your questions deserve straight answers, and one of them corrects an impression I may have left.

**#2379 now passes** — `tests_adequate: true`, bug_free 88, 0 bugs. Only `integration` left.

## "You had to login, no?" — no, and I wouldn't have

I never entered credentials anywhere; that's a hard line for me. Both paths were **already authenticated**:

- **Slack** — via the Slack MCP connector already attached to your claude.ai account. I sent a live DM to bot `U095U1QTZ7V` in workspace `T09513HDQ77`, round-tripped in 30s.
- **Telegram** — through *your own logged-in Chrome*, driven by the Owletto extension (conn 432) at web.telegram.org.

But here's the part that matters more than the mechanism, and I want to be blunt about it: **that was 2026-07-29, against prod `app.lobu.ai` running release 14.7.0.** That is the *hosted server*. It tells us nothing about the npm tarball we'd be publishing — different artifact, different build, different runtime.

## So: no, pre-publish verification is not complete

Nothing has been published — I asked for your go-ahead and haven't taken it. Here's the actual state, by surface and by *what it was tested against*:

| Surface | Verified? | Against what |
|---|---|---|
| CLI commands | yes | **source tree** — the blind spot that hid all 4 bugs |
| CLI from tarball | **running now** | published artifact, expect red |
| MCP | yes | prod hosted server + in the artifact gate (pending) |
| Slack / Telegram | yes, 2026-07-29 | **prod hosted 14.7.0**, not the tarball |
| UI | 4 pages render, 2026-07-29 | prod hosted |
| Connectors (oauth/api) | **no** | — |

Two gaps I'd call out as genuinely open before a launch: **nothing has been re-verified since the three fixes merged**, and the Slack/UI evidence is two days old against a different artifact.

content.text:
That check changed the picture materially, so let me lead with it.

## The three fixes do **not** affect hosted prod — they're CLI/self-host only

I traced it rather than assumed. `docker/app/Dockerfile:199` copies `packages/agent-worker/` **including `src/`**. The gateway's entrypoint resolution (`gateway/config/index.ts:187-206`) checks `existsSync(<root>/packages/agent-worker/src/index.ts)` first — that's true inside the container, so prod resolves the **`.ts` source**, which `buildWorkerInvocation` spawns under **bun**, where `__filename` is defined.

So `app.lobu.ai` never took the broken path. Same for the other two: pgvector's `vector.so` is the *embedded* Postgres for `lobu run`, and the uid-0 refusal is likewise embedded-Postgres. **All three are `lobu run` / self-hoster bugs.**

Two consequences, one good and one that limits my earlier answer:

- The Slack/Telegram/UI evidence from 07-29 against prod hosted **is still valid**, because none of these fixes touch that path. That's the good half.
- It also means those tests were **never coverage for what we'd publish** — they exercise a different artifact entirely. The npm tarball's story rests on the artifact gate, which is still running.

## Direct answer to "did you do all the MCP/CLI/UI/Slack tests before publishing"

**No — and nothing has been published.** I asked for your go-ahead on the release and haven't taken it, so there's no gap in front of users right now. But if you're asking whether I've earned a "safe to publish": not yet.

What's genuinely missing before publish:

1. **The artifact gate has never completed a green run.** All four cells are still going. Until one passes, the tarball is unverified by anything.
2. **Nothing re-verified since the three fixes merged** — the last end-to-end evidence predates them.
3. **Connectors on oauth/api-key** — no dry-run path exists locally, and I haven't exercised them anywhere.

What I'd argue is *not* missing: a fresh Slack test isn't a publish gate, because publishing `@lobu/cli` doesn't change the hosted server Slack runs on. It becomes relevant when main rolls out to prod, which is a different event.

**Confidence** — the "prod is unaffected" conclusion: **90**, read from the Dockerfile and the resolution logic on `origin/main`; I have not booted the image to watch it pick the entrypoint, and I'd want that before betting the launch on it. Slack/Telegram evidence: **85** for the hosted product as of 07-29, **0** as evidence about the tarball.

**Next, pick from:**
1. Wait for the artifact gate's first verdict — it's the missing precondition for publishing at all.
2. Boot the app image locally and confirm the worker really spawns under bun, upgrading that 90 to fact. Also closes #2183.
3. Re-run the Slack round-trip against current prod, so the launch evidence is hours old rather than two days.
4. Merge #2379 once `integration` finishes.

=== publish-packages triggers ===
name: Publish Packages

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      bump:
        description: "Version bump: patch | minor | major | explicit like 3.1.0 | skip"
        required: false
        default: "skip"
        type: string
      provenance:
        description: "Attach npm provenance (requires trusted publisher configured on npmjs.com)"
        required: false
        default: false
        type: boolean

permissions:
  contents: read
  # Needed for npm trusted publishing (OIDC). Only effective when each
  # package is registered on npmjs.com → Settings → Publishing access →
  # Add trusted publisher → Workflow: .github/workflows/publish-packages.yml,
  # Environment: production.
  id-token: write

jobs:
  publish-packages:
    runs-on: blacksmith-4vcpu-ubuntu-2404
    timeout-minutes: 30
    environment: production
    env:
      # Step-level env is not visible to the same step's `if:` evaluator.
      CLAWHUB_TOKEN_SET: ${{ secrets.CLAWHUB_TOKEN != '' }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup-submodule
        with:
          deploy-key: ${{ secrets.OWLETTO_WEB_DEPLOY_KEY }}

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
=== build-images triggers ===
name: Build and Push Images

# GitHub keeps only one pending run per concurrency group. On 2026-07-28 the
# `lobu-v14.4.0` release queued behind a main build, then a later main push
# evicted it. The version images were not published until a manual rerun. Give
# releases their own group so routine merges cannot evict them.
#
# Pushes deliberately keep the default single-item queue so bursts coalesce to
# the newest commit. `queue: max` is not conditional, so setting it here would
# queue intermediate pushes instead. cancel-in-progress stays false because
# cancelling a running build can leave only some of the shared image tags
# published.
#
# Separate groups let a release and push run in the same second. generate-tag
# therefore appends a zero-padded run number to the timestamp; the timestamp
# preserves Flux ordering across reruns and the run number breaks ties. The
# matching ImagePolicy lives in the owletto submodule and accepts both the old
# two-segment tags and the new three-segment form.
concurrency:
  group: build-images${{ github.event_name == 'release' && '-release' || '' }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  # release-please publishes `lobu-vX.Y.Z`. Building on that too is what gives
  # the images a semver tag and repoints `latest` at a release instead of an
  # arbitrary commit (#2184). Unrelated releases are ignored.
  release:

name: Release Please

on:
  push:

      - main

  contents: write
  pull-requests: write

jobs:
  release-please:
    runs-on: blacksmith-4vcpu-ubuntu-2404
    timeout-minutes: 20
    environment: production
    outputs:
      release_created: ${{ steps.release.outputs.release_created }}
      tag_name: ${{ steps.release.outputs.tag_name }}

generate-tag:
    runs-on: blacksmith-4vcpu-ubuntu-2404
    outputs:
      tag: ${{ steps.tags.outputs.tag }}
      semver: ${{ steps.tags.outputs.semver }}
      is_stable: ${{ steps.tags.outputs.is_stable }}
      should_publish: ${{ steps.tags.outputs.should_publish }}
    steps:
      # Only this job needs the repo; the build jobs check out separately.
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      # Every tag decision lives in scripts/derive-image-tags.mjs so it is
      # covered by scripts/__tests__/derive-image-tags.test.ts. Computed once
      # here so app/worker/embeddings cannot disagree about the tag,
      # eligibility, or version.
      - name: Derive image tags
        id: tags
        env:
          RUN_NUMBER: ${{ github.run_number }}
          EVENT_NAME: ${{ github.event_name }}
          RELEASE_TAG: ${{ github.event_name == 'release' && github.event.release.tag_name || '' }}
          PRERELEASE: ${{ github.event_name == 'release' && github.event.release.prerelease || false }}
        run: node scripts/derive-image-tags.mjs

  # Connector-runtime parity smoke gate (main/deploy side). RUNS the built worker
  # artifact's self-check before any image is pushed, so the packaging/parity
  # drift that broke prod (worker image missing `COPY packages/core` → dangling
  # transitive `@lobu/core` → every feed sync crashed, all CI green) can't ship.
  # `build-worker` depends on this, and `build-app` depends on `build-worker`, so
  # a failing smoke blocks BOTH worker and app pushes — critical because the chart
  # applies one shared tag to app + worker and Flux's ImageUpdateAutomation would
  # otherwise roll the app to a tag whose worker is broken.
  #
  # amd64-only (no QEMU/arm64): a smoke gate, not a release. Reuses the same GHA
  # buildx cache scope as `build-worker` so this doesn't double the build cost.
  connector-parity-smoke:
    runs-on: blacksmith-4vcpu-ubuntu-2404
    needs: [generate-tag]
    if: needs.generate-tag.outputs.should_publish == 'true'

# ===========================================
# Runtime
# ===========================================
FROM node:22-slim AS runtime

WORKDIR /app

# curl for health checks, git/gh for GitHub connector agent tooling, bun for
# tsx-equivalent, Chromium deps for connectors.
#
# bubblewrap is what makes the contributed CLIs REACHABLE: the embedded worker
# registers spawned binaries only when it has an exec sandbox (probeSandbox ->
# bwrap) or an explicit unsandboxed opt-in. Without it `gh` sits in /usr/bin and
# every agent invocation exits 127 — the credential works and the command does
# not.
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
      curl ca-certificates git gh unzip bubblewrap \
      libnss3 libnspr4 libatk1.0-0 libatk-bridge2.0-0 libcups2 libdrm2 libdbus-1-3 \
      libxkbcommon0 libatspi2.0-0 libxcomposite1 libxdamage1 libxfixes3 libxrandr2 \
      libgbm1 libpango-1.0-0 libcairo2 libasound2 libwayland-client0 \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* \
    && curl -fsSL https://bun.sh/install | BUN_INSTALL=/usr/local bash \
    && chmod +x /usr/local/bin/bun

ENV PATH="/usr/local/bin:${PATH}"

# Copy installed deps + source from builder

#
  # Posts to the same Slack webhook the Flux notification-controller's
  # `slack-devops` Provider uses (devops channel) so cluster-side and CI-side
  # deploy failures land in one place. Webhook lives in the SLACK_DEPLOY_WEBHOOK_URL
  # repo secret; if unset the curl is skipped, never failing the job.
  notify-failure:
    runs-on: blacksmith-4vcpu-ubuntu-2404
    needs: [generate-tag, connector-parity-smoke, build-worker, build-embeddings-service, build-app]
    if: >-
      failure()
      && needs.generate-tag.outputs.should_publish == 'true'
      && (github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' || github.event_name == 'release')
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Post failure to Slack devops
        env:
          SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL: ${{ secrets.SLACK_DEPLOY_WEBHOOK_URL }}
          RUN_URL: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
          COMMIT_URL: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/commit/${{ github.sha }}
          RUN_SUMMARY: ${{ github.event.head_commit.message || github.event.release.name || github.ref_name }}
          REF_NAME: ${{ github.ref_name }}
          ACTOR: ${{ github.actor }}
          SHA_SHORT: ${{ github.sha }}
        run: |
          if [ -z "$SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL" ]; then
            echo "SLACK_DEPLOY_WEBHOOK_URL not set; skipping notification."
            exit 0
          fi
          # First line of commit/release summary only, JSON-escaped via jq.
          first_line=$(printf '%s' "$RUN_SUMMARY" | head -n1)
          payload=$(jq -nc \
            --arg text "<@U09513HH1N1> :rotating_light: build-images failed on \`${REF_NAME}\` — sibling image tags may be incomplete. <${RUN_URL}|run> · <${COMMIT_URL}|${SHA_SHORT:0:7}> by ${ACTOR}\n> ${first_line}" \
            '{text: $text}')
          curl -sS -X POST -H 'Content-type: application/json' --data "$payload" "$SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL"

input.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# App-image smoke: BOOT the lobu-app image that was just pushed and exercise the
# surfaces a user actually touches — HTTP health, the web UI and every asset it
# references, the MCP mount, the in-container `lobu` CLI, and the connector
# runtime.
#
# Why this exists, and why building the image is not enough.
#
# `build-images.yml` builds and pushes app/worker/embeddings, and Flux rolls the
# tag out. Nothing in that path ever RUNS the app image. The whole "image builds
# green, container is broken" class was therefore invisible:
#
#   #2231   no `lobu` on PATH inside the image — the CLI shipped, unreachable
#   #2183   app image serves 404s for assets the built SPA references
#   #430    server bundle could not bind named imports against CJS dist barrels
#
# `connector-parity-smoke` already learned this lesson for the WORKER image (it
# `docker run`s the self-check rather than trusting the build). This is the same
# move for the APP image, which is the one users and the browser talk to.
#
# It runs AFTER `build-app` has pushed, deliberately: a failure here must not
# block the push or Flux's rollout, but it does fail the workflow — so main goes
# red and a release cannot be cut on a broken image.
#
# Keyless: needs only a Postgres with pgvector. No provider key, no secrets.
#
# Usage: app-image-smoke.sh <image-ref>
# Env:   DATABASE_URL  postgres with pgvector (required)
#        APP_PORT      host port to bind (default 8787)

set -uo pipefail

IMAGE="${1:?usage: app-image-smoke.sh <image-ref>}"
APP_PORT="${APP_PORT:-8787}"
: "${DATABASE_URL:?DATABASE_URL must point at a pgvector-enabled Postgres}"

BASE="http://127.0.0.1:${APP_PORT}"
CID=""
PASS=0
FAIL=0

note() { echo ""; echo "== $* =="; }
ok()   { echo "  ok   — $*"; PASS=$((PASS + 1)); }
bad()  { echo "  FAIL — $*"; FAIL=$((FAIL + 1)); }

cleanup() {
  if [ -n "$CID" ]; then
    echo ""
    echo "---- container logs (tail) ----"
    docker logs --tail 120 "$CID" 2>&1 || true
    docker rm -f "$CID" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  fi
}
trap cleanup EXIT

echo "================================================================"
echo " app-image smoke"
echo "   image: ${IMAGE}"
echo "================================================================"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Boot. --network host so the container reaches the Postgres service on
#    127.0.0.1 and publishes 8787 on the runner without port-mapping games.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
note "boot"
CID=$(docker run -d --network host \
  -e "DATABASE_URL=${DATABASE_URL}" \
  -e "JWT_SECRET=app-image-smoke-not-a-real-secret" \
  -e "ALLOW_DB_CREATE=1" \
  -e "PORT=${APP_PORT}" \
  "$IMAGE")
echo "  container ${CID:0:12}"

# Migrations run at start, so allow a generous window. Poll /health rather than
# sleeping: a fixed sleep either wastes time or flakes.
booted=false
for _ in $(seq 1 90); do
  if curl -fsS --max-time 3 "${BASE}/health" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    booted=true
    break
  fi
  if [ -z "$(docker ps -q --filter "id=${CID}")" ]; then
    bad "container exited before serving /health"
    break
  fi
  sleep 2
done

if [ "$booted" != true ]; then
  bad "/health never became ready"
  echo ""
  echo "RESULT: app-image smoke FAILED (boot)"
  exit 1
fi
ok "/health responded"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. The in-container CLI (#2231). It shipped but was not on PATH, so
#    `docker exec <container> lobu ...` — the documented self-host recipe —
#    failed for every self-hoster while every build stayed green.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
note "in-container CLI"
if docker exec "$CID" lobu --version >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  ok "\`lobu --version\` resolves on PATH"
else
  bad "\`lobu\` is not runnable inside the image (#2231 regression)"
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Worker-entrypoint invariant.
#
#    `gateway/config/index.ts` picks the worker entrypoint by probing for

fi

if [ "$FAIL" -ne 0 ]; then
  echo "RESULT: app-image smoke FAILED"
  exit 1
fi

<!-- Per-repo agent rules loaded into every Claude Code session in this repo. Inlines AGENTS.md (shared project rules) first, then layers local-only notes below. User memory entries live under ~/.claude/projects/.../memory/. Don't add anything here unless it's only relevant to Claude agent specific. If other harnesses like pi or codex need it, modify AGENTS.md -->

@AGENTS.md

content.content:
## Repo map
- Bun workspace under `packages/*`; TS source is in `src`, tests in `__tests__`.
- Main packages: `core` shared types/utils, `plugin-api` native plugin contracts, `plugin-host` deterministic plugin composition, `server` gateway + embedded runtime, `agent-worker` Lobu agent execution, `connectors` built-in connectors, `owletto` frontend submodule.
- Before editing a package, read its nearest `AGENTS.md` if present.
- `docs/GOTCHAS.md` collects the mechanical traps (build, SQL, testing, submodule, browser) that have each cost a debugging session. Skim the section for the surface you are touching before you start, and grep it when something looks inexplicable.

## Hard invariants
- **Never write to `~/Code/lobu` directly — work in a worktree.** Run `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` first, and never `git switch` in the main checkout.
- One branch = one concern (not one file). Tangential task → commit/push/open current work, then branch fresh from `main`. Split only for genuinely independent concerns or an unreviewable diff.
- **Multi-replica correctness is mandatory.** Never put shared required state in an in-memory Map/singleton another replica must read or mutate. If a feature relies on cross-pod visibility, use Postgres-mediated state/signal.
- **`events` is append-only.** Never `DELETE FROM events`; tombstone/supersede instead.
- **Request paths never aggregate history.** No `GROUP BY`, `DISTINCT ON`, per-row `regexp_*`, or leading-wildcard `LIKE` over an append-only / run-history table (`events`, `agent_transcript_snapshot`, `session_calls`, …) on a user-facing read path. History only grows, so read-time aggregation cost grows with it while the answer stays bounded. Materialize the row or counter at WRITE time and read it back by index; run the one-time aggregation in a migration, never per request. Aggregating bounded config tables (`connections`, `watchers`, `agent_users`) is fine.
- **Never bulk-delete prod `organization` rows**, including zero-activity ones — empty-looking orgs are frequently real human signups. Surface them one at a time for confirmation.
- **Workers never receive real credentials.** They may receive only placeholders/proxied access. The only exceptions are device-pinned connectors and short-lived provider-derived credential leases (see `packages/server/AGENTS.md`); a durable stored credential is never one of them.
- Default to static `import`. New dynamic imports require measured cost justification here or in the package AGENTS plus a rationale comment at the call site. Tests may dynamically import after mocks.
  - Node-version gate exceptions: `packages/cli/bin/lobu.js` defers the existing CLI graph without duplicating it, and `packages/server/src/server-entry.ts` adds an 842-byte gate in front of the 4.34 MB server graph (measured 2026-07-24). Both call sites must stay dependency-free until their checks pass.
- Bug fixes require red→fix→green evidence, with both outputs pasted into the PR body. If you cannot reproduce, stop and report the dead end — do not ship a speculative fix.
- Never report done off a green typecheck. Boot it, exercise every branch you touched, clean up test data. If "compiles" is all you ran, say so explicitly.
- Gates are non-negotiable (sequence in "Ship a change" below). `make pre-pr` builds first — that build step is what protects against a stale-dist false green. `make review` is an LLM verdict only: it does NOT run typecheck/knip/tests and is not proof CI will pass.
- The agent-facing product name is **Behavior**; `watcher` is internal engine/DB vocabulary. It must not appear in MCP tool schemas/names/descriptions, ClientSDK discovery metadata, or the connector-sdk public reaction contract — `make pre-pr` fails on it. Internal identifiers (`actingWatcherId`, table/column names, comments) are fine.
- `make review-fix` is the unposted fixer pass and runs BEFORE the first `make review`; verify its diff and commit it. Never iterate `make review` as a find-fix loop — each posted round costs a review + CI cycle.
- Fix the class, not the instance: on the first hit, grep every other instance and fix in one pass — a diff-scoped reviewer only ever finds the next one. Same root cause twice = stop reviewing, grep-enumerate. A class-wide fix is in scope for the branch that found it and does not count as scope creep.
- **Fail closed on durable dispatch/delivery state.** When a durable coordination or delivery operation fails, its caller must not reinterpret the error as proceed/deliver/skip. Propagate a retry, defer, or terminal-failure outcome with a visible log; if the operation may already have succeeded, reconcile idempotently before retrying. Treat lock timeouts, pool errors, and ambiguous or expired rows as failures, not as "nothing changed."
- **Coordination design brake.** A change that needs a second lock, a second retry/deferral budget, or a prose termination argument to explain why it halts is patching a misplaced check — stop and re-derive where the decision belongs before adding mechanism. Find the chokepoint that already serializes the action (e.g. worker dispatch is serialized by `job-router` on the worker-SSE-owner pod) and put the check there; prefer deleting the state transition over coordinating it, and reuse queue-native retry over hand-rolled hold/requeue.
- **Stage by explicit path; never commit the whole tree of a worktree that hosted other work.** A commit is a snapshot — stale file copies silently revert already-merged PRs. After commit/rebase, `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` must equal the task's intended file list; extra files = stop. Verify a "reverts merged work" review finding by diff direction against `origin/main`, never dismiss it as merge-base noise.

## Ship a change
1. `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` → work in `.claude/worktrees/<slug>/`.
2. Reproduce the bug (red) before fixing it. Fix, then prove green.
3. Test: `make test-unit` (no DB) / `make test-integration` (needs `DATABASE_URL` with pgvector). One file: `bun test <path>`, or `cd packages/server && bunx vitest run <path>` for vitest suites.
4. `make pre-pr` — build, typecheck, knip, lint, exposed-surface naming.
5. `make review-fix` on the settled diff and verify what it changed — it edits the working tree, so re-read the files before trusting them.
6. Stage by explicit path (`git add -- <paths>`, never `-A`), commit, then confirm `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` is exactly your intended file list. Extra files = stop.
7. `git push -u origin <branch>` → `gh pr create` (fill `.github/pull_request_template.md`; conventional-commit title, e.g. `fix(server): …`).
8. `make review` **once** on the settled HEAD. It posts the `pi-review` status, which is a REQUIRED check.
9. Merge squash once CI is green: `gh pr merge <n> --squash --admin`. Never `--admin` past a check that has not reported.
10. Prod-visible surface? Verify it live after rollout. Set a self-rescheduling `ScheduleWakeup` (~1500s) carrying the rollout gate: poll the deployed SHA, then `git merge-base --is-ancestor "$MERGE_SHA" "$DEPLOYED_SHA"` with `MERGE_SHA=$(gh pr view <n> --json mergeCommit --jq .mergeCommit.oid)`. Two ways this gate silently never opens — **gate on the squash commit, not your branch head** (a squash merge writes a new commit with no ancestry link to the branch, so the branch head exits 1 forever: PR #2280 has identical trees and still fails), and **keep that argument order** (merge commit first; reversed, it accepts a stale deploy). Run the live check when it lands, and write the result back to memory.

## Agent workflow
- Do only what was asked. Delete ephemeral files you create. Do not create `*.md` unless asked.
- Prefer `bun`; do not use npm/yarn/pnpm for repo work.
- Fix unused params by deleting them, not `_`-prefixing.
- Never `git stash`; use WIP commits and squash later.
- Never resolve merge conflicts in the GitHub web UI (it has silently dropped 1000+ lines of feature work). Rebase locally against `origin/main`, then diff against the last real feature commit before squashing — except on submodule-pointer branches, where you must `git merge` (see `docs/GOTCHAS.md`, "Submodule & cross-repo").
- Run mandated gates automatically; never ask permission to run one.
- Show the diff, not a summary. Before claiming done — on your own work or a dispatched agent's — surface `git status` plus `git diff --stat <base>...HEAD`. An agent's self-report is a claim; the diff is the evidence.
- UI PRs owe before/after screenshots, and `gh` cannot upload images inline. Capture before shots from the unmodified branch and after shots from the same booted app (auth recipe in `docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md`), base64-embed the PNGs into one self-contained HTML comparison page, publish it as a claude.ai artifact, and link it from the PR.
- Any subagent with write access (Edit/Write/Bash) runs in its own worktree; only grep/read agents share the parent. Two writing agents must NEVER share a worktree — they overwrite each other's uncommitted work.
- Dispatch code-writing agents through `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` and brief them with the absolute `.claude/worktrees/<slug>/` path. Only task-setup does the submodule branch pinning, post-init `bun install`, `.env` copy, and port allocation.
- Do repetitive multi-file edits (renames, signature changes, import rewrites) inline or with one script. Reserve subagents for read-only breadth or genuinely isolated parallel work.
- Before adding an env var, grep for the one the codebase already reads. Do not rename existing vars to a "cleaner" convention unasked.
- Deleting code needs structural evidence (dangling import, completed migration, superseded impl). Low prod usage is not a delete signal; trace the workflow, not just the import graph — docs and help text are load-bearing too.
- **Absence is never proven by a grep on a working tree.** To prove code does *not* exist, run `git fetch -q origin && git grep <pattern> origin/main` — the fetch is load-bearing, `origin/main` itself goes stale. Applies to every existence check, including the deletion-evidence rule above.
- Slack link pasted (`slack.com/archives/…?thread_ts=`) → run `scripts/slack-thread-viewer.js "<link>"` first.
- To drive the user's real logged-in browser, use the paired Owletto extension — recipe in `docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md`. Do **not** assume CDP/browser-auth is required.
- Unsure in planning → ask before making conflicting or irreversible choices. Mid-execution, block on a question only for irreversible/destructive actions or decisions that are genuinely the user's; for reversible choices with a clear recommended option, take it and flag the choice in your summary.

## Session efficiency
- Never poll in the foreground (`sleep`/`until`/`while` wait loops, repeated `tail`). Run long waits (dev-server boot, CI, deploys) in the background and act on the completion notification.
- Prefer DOM reads (`get_page_text`, `read_page`, `javascript_tool`) over screenshots; screenshot only when visual layout itself is under test. Screenshots are the #1 context-bloat source.
- Read a file before editing it, and re-read it after any external change (a fixer pass, another agent, a rebase). Blind edits fail and cost a retry round-trip.
- Read PR status compactly: `gh pr view <n> --json number,title,isDraft,mergeStateStatus,reviewDecision` plus `gh pr checks <n> --required`. Never `--json statusCheckRollup` — measured on PR 2280 it is 7520 bytes against 861, 8.7x larger and less legible.
- Batch narrow fixes into one commit, verified once at the end of the batch — not per fix. It never justifies skipping a reproducer or a correctness-critical test. For a one-line or config-only change, take one CI snapshot and move on.

<!-- Project rules for agents (Claude, pi, codex). CLAUDE.md inlines this into every session — keep this file lean. Put package-specific detail in the nearest package AGENTS.md. -->

## Repo map
- Bun workspace under `packages/*`; TS source is in `src`, tests in `__tests__`.
- Main packages: `core` shared types/utils, `plugin-api` native plugin contracts, `plugin-host` deterministic plugin composition, `server` gateway + embedded runtime, `agent-worker` Lobu agent execution, `connectors` built-in connectors, `owletto` frontend submodule.
- Before editing a package, read its nearest `AGENTS.md` if present.
- `docs/GOTCHAS.md` collects the mechanical traps (build, SQL, testing, submodule, browser) that have each cost a debugging session. Skim the section for the surface you are touching before you start, and grep it when something looks inexplicable.

## Hard invariants
- **Never write to `~/Code/lobu` directly — work in a worktree.** Run `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` first, and never `git switch` in the main checkout.
- One branch = one concern (not one file). Tangential task → commit/push/open current work, then branch fresh from `main`. Split only for genuinely independent concerns or an unreviewable diff.
- **Multi-replica correctness is mandatory.** Never put shared required state in an in-memory Map/singleton another replica must read or mutate. If a feature relies on cross-pod visibility, use Postgres-mediated state/signal.
- **`events` is append-only.** Never `DELETE FROM events`; tombstone/supersede instead.
- **Request paths never aggregate history.** No `GROUP BY`, `DISTINCT ON`, per-row `regexp_*`, or leading-wildcard `LIKE` over an append-only / run-history table (`events`, `agent_transcript_snapshot`, `session_calls`, …) on a user-facing read path. History only grows, so read-time aggregation cost grows with it while the answer stays bounded. Materialize the row or counter at WRITE time and read it back by index; run the one-time aggregation in a migration, never per request. Aggregating bounded config tables (`connections`, `watchers`, `agent_users`) is fine.
- **Never bulk-delete prod `organization` rows**, including zero-activity ones — empty-looking orgs are frequently real human signups. Surface them one at a time for confirmation.
- **Workers never receive real credentials.** They may receive only placeholders/proxied access. The only exceptions are device-pinned connectors and short-lived provider-derived credential leases (see `packages/server/AGENTS.md`); a durable stored credential is never one of them.
- Default to static `import`. New dynamic imports require measured cost justification here or in the package AGENTS plus a rationale comment at the call site. Tests may dynamically import after mocks.
  - Node-version gate exceptions: `packages/cli/bin/lobu.js` defers the existing CLI graph without duplicating it, and `packages/server/src/server-entry.ts` adds an 842-byte gate in front of the 4.34 MB server graph (measured 2026-07-24). Both call sites must stay dependency-free until their checks pass.
- Bug fixes require red→fix→green evidence, with both outputs pasted into the PR body. If you cannot reproduce, stop and report the dead end — do not ship a speculative fix.
- Never report done off a green typecheck. Boot it, exercise every branch you touched, clean up test data. If "compiles" is all you ran, say so explicitly.
- Gates are non-negotiable (sequence in "Ship a change" below). `make pre-pr` builds first — that build step is what protects against a stale-dist false green. `make review` is an LLM verdict only: it does NOT run typecheck/knip/tests and is not proof CI will pass.
- The agent-facing product name is **Behavior**; `watcher` is internal engine/DB vocabulary. It must not appear in MCP tool schemas/names/descriptions, ClientSDK discovery metadata, or the connector-sdk public reaction contract — `make pre-pr` fails on it. Internal identifiers (`actingWatcherId`, table/column names, comments) are fine.
- `make review-fix` is the unposted fixer pass and runs BEFORE the first `make review`; verify its diff and commit it. Never iterate `make review` as a find-fix loop — each posted round costs a review + CI cycle.
- Fix the class, not the instance: on the first hit, grep every other instance and fix in one pass — a diff-scoped reviewer only ever finds the next one. Same root cause twice = stop reviewing, grep-enumerate. A class-wide fix is in scope for the branch that found it and does not count as scope creep.
- **Fail closed on durable dispatch/delivery state.** When a durable coordination or delivery operation fails, its caller must not reinterpret the error as proceed/deliver/skip. Propagate a retry, defer, or terminal-failure outcome with a visible log; if the operation may already have succeeded, reconcile idempotently before retrying. Treat lock timeouts, pool errors, and ambiguous or expired rows as failures, not as "nothing changed."
- **Coordination design brake.** A change that needs a second lock, a second retry/deferral budget, or a prose termination argument to explain why it halts is patching a misplaced check — stop and re-derive where the decision belongs before adding mechanism. Find the chokepoint that already serializes the action (e.g. worker dispatch is serialized by `job-router` on the worker-SSE-owner pod) and put the check there; prefer deleting the state transition over coordinating it, and reuse queue-native retry over hand-rolled hold/requeue.
- **Stage by explicit path; never commit the whole tree of a worktree that hosted other work.** A commit is a snapshot — stale file copies silently revert already-merged PRs. After commit/rebase, `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` must equal the task's intended file list; extra files = stop. Verify a "reverts merged work" review finding by diff direction against `origin/main`, never dismiss it as merge-base noise.

## Ship a change
1. `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` → work in `.claude/worktrees/<slug>/`.
2. Reproduce the bug (red) before fixing it. Fix, then prove green.
3. Test: `make test-unit` (no DB) / `make test-integration` (needs `DATABASE_URL` with pgvector). One file: `bun test <path>`, or `cd packages/server && bunx vitest run <path>` for vitest suites.
4. `make pre-pr` — build, typecheck, knip, lint, exposed-surface naming.
5. `make review-fix` on the settled diff and verify what it changed — it edits the working tree, so re-read the files before trusting them.
6. Stage by explicit path (`git add -- <paths>`, never `-A`), commit, then confirm `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` is exactly your intended file list. Extra files = stop.
7. `git push -u origin <branch>` → `gh pr create` (fill `.github/pull_request_template.md`; conventional-commit title, e.g. `fix(server): …`).
8. `make review` **once** on the settled HEAD. It posts the `pi-review` status, which is a REQUIRED check.
9. Merge squash once CI is green: `gh pr merge <n> --squash --admin`. Never `--admin` past a check that has not reported.
10. Prod-visible surface? Verify it live after rollout. Set a self-rescheduling `ScheduleWakeup` (~1500s) carrying the rollout gate: poll the deployed SHA, then `git merge-base --is-ancestor "$MERGE_SHA" "$DEPLOYED_SHA"` with `MERGE_SHA=$(gh pr view <n> --json mergeCommit --jq .mergeCommit.oid)`. Two ways this gate silently never opens — **gate on the squash commit, not your branch head** (a squash merge writes a new commit with no ancestry link to the branch, so the branch head exits 1 forever: PR #2280 has identical trees and still fails), and **keep that argument order** (merge commit first; reversed, it accepts a stale deploy). Run the live check when it lands, and write the result back to memory.

## Agent workflow
- Do only what was asked. Delete ephemeral files you create. Do not create `*.md` unless asked.
- Prefer `bun`; do not use npm/yarn/pnpm for repo work.
- Fix unused params by deleting them, not `_`-prefixing.
- Never `git stash`; use WIP commits and squash later.
- Never resolve merge conflicts in the GitHub web UI (it has silently dropped 1000+ lines of feature work). Rebase locally against `origin/main`, then diff against the last real feature commit before squashing — except on submodule-pointer branches, where you must `git merge` (see `docs/GOTCHAS.md`, "Submodule & cross-repo").
- Run mandated gates automatically; never ask permission to run one.
- Show the diff, not a summary. Before claiming done — on your own work or a dispatched agent's — surface `git status` plus `git diff --stat <base>...HEAD`. An agent's self-report is a claim; the diff is the evidence.
- UI PRs owe before/after screenshots, and `gh` cannot upload images inline. Capture before shots from the unmodified branch and after shots from the same booted app (auth recipe in `docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md`), base64-embed the PNGs into one self-contained HTML comparison page, publish it as a claude.ai artifact, and link it from the PR.
- Any subagent with write access (Edit/Write/Bash) runs in its own worktree; only grep/read agents share the parent. Two writing agents must NEVER share a worktree — they overwrite each other's uncommitted work.
- Dispatch code-writing agents through `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` and brief them with the absolute `.claude/worktrees/<slug>/` path. Only task-setup does the submodule branch pinning, post-init `bun install`, `.env` copy, and port allocation.
- Do repetitive multi-file edits (renames, signature changes, import rewrites) inline or with one script. Reserve subagents for read-only breadth or genuinely isolated parallel work.
- Before adding an env var, grep for the one the codebase already reads. Do not rename existing vars to a "cleaner" convention unasked.
- Deleting code needs structural evidence (dangling import, completed migration, superseded impl). Low prod usage is not a delete signal; trace the workflow, not just the import graph — docs and help text are load-bearing too.
- **Absence is never proven by a grep on a working tree.** To prove code does *not* exist, run `git fetch -q origin && git grep <pattern> origin/main` — the fetch is load-bearing, `origin/main` itself goes stale. Applies to every existence check, including the deletion-evidence rule above.
- Slack link pasted (`slack.com/archives/…?thread_ts=`) → run `scripts/slack-thread-viewer.js "<link>"` first.
- To drive the user's real logged-in browser, use the paired Owletto extension — recipe in `docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md`. Do **not** assume CDP/browser-auth is required.
- Unsure in planning → ask before making conflicting or irreversible choices. Mid-execution, block on a question only for irreversible/destructive actions or decisions that are genuinely the user's; for reversible choices with a clear recommended option, take it and flag the choice in your summary.

## Session efficiency
- Never poll in the foreground (`sleep`/`until`/`while` wait loops, repeated `tail`). Run long waits (dev-server boot, CI, deploys) in the background and act on the completion notification.
- Prefer DOM reads (`get_page_text`, `read_page`, `javascript_tool`) over screenshots; screenshot only when visual layout itself is under test. Screenshots are the #1 context-bloat source.
- Read a file before editing it, and re-read it after any external change (a fixer pass, another agent, a rebase). Blind edits fail and cost a retry round-trip.
- Read PR status compactly: `gh pr view <n> --json number,title,isDraft,mergeStateStatus,reviewDecision` plus `gh pr checks <n> --required`. Never `--json statusCheckRollup` — measured on PR 2280 it is 7520 bytes against 861, 8.7x larger and less legible.
- Batch narrow fixes into one commit, verified once at the end of the batch — not per fix. It never justifies skipping a reproducer or a correctness-critical test. For a one-line or config-only change, take one CI snapshot and move on.

      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@v2

          bun-version: 1.3.5

steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      # Refuse to publish off a commit whose post-merge image smoke is red.
      #
      # `app-image-smoke` (in build-images.yml) BOOTS the app image built from
      # this exact commit. If that is failing, the tree is known-broken at
      # runtime and a release would ship it — every bug this guards against
      # (#2231, #2183, __filename, GLIBC_2.38, uid-0) was green on every check
      # that does not run the artifact.
      #
      # Deliberately NOT gated on "Published-artifact smoke": that one installs
      # `@lobu/cli@latest` from npm, i.e. the PREVIOUS release. It is red
      # precisely when a fix is waiting to be published, so gating on it would
      # deadlock the release that repairs it. Its job is to alert on what users
      # can install right now, and to verify the new version after publishing.
      - name: Require a green app-image smoke for this commit
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          sha="$(git rev-parse HEAD)"
          echo "publishing from ${sha}"

          # Newest run of build-images for this SHA. `head_sha` filters server
          # side so a busy main can't push ours off the first page.
          conclusion=$(gh api \
            "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/workflows/build-images.yml/runs?head_sha=${sha}&per_page=1" \
            --jq '.workflow_runs[0].conclusion // "missing"')
          echo "build-images conclusion: ${conclusion}"

          case "$conclusion" in
            success)
              echo "app-image smoke green for ${sha} — proceeding."
              ;;
            missing)
              echo "::error::No build-images run for ${sha}. The app image for this commit has never been built or smoked; publish would ship an unverified tree."
              exit 1
              ;;
            *)
              echo "::error::build-images for ${sha} concluded '${conclusion}'. The app image smoke is not green — fix main before releasing."
              exit 1
              ;;
          esac

      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup-submodule
