**PR #2395** is up: https://github.com/lobu-ai/lobu/pull/2395 — `make review` running now (Fable; codex is still quota-blocked until Aug 5).

## The diff, as ground truth

```
 .github/workflows/ci.yml                           |  51 ++++++
 packages/agent-worker/src/__tests__/exec-sandbox.test.ts |  69 ++++++++
 packages/agent-worker/src/embedded/exec-sandbox.ts       | 195 +++++++++++++----
 3 files changed, 281 insertions(+), 34 deletions(-)
```

`git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` is exactly those three files — no stale-tree contamination from the other work this worktree hosted.

## Red→green, redone properly

My first attempt at this mutation silently didn't run — I `cd`'d into a directory I was already in, the `&&` chain short-circuited, and the "restore" step executed against an unmutated file. It would have reported green and proved nothing. Redone with absolute paths:

```
RED   Expected to contain: "setting up uid map: Permission denied"
      Received: "...Install bubblewrap (Linux) or check sandbox-exec (macOS)..."
      36 pass | 1 fail
GREEN 37 pass | 0 fail
```

The mutation puts back exactly the sentence this PR removes, so the failing assertion is the defect itself.

That's twice now in this programme that a mutation quietly failed to apply. The tell both times was a count that didn't move — worth making the assert-then-verify step routine rather than incidental.

## One thing I'd flag on the CI job

It probes `kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns` alongside the older Debian `unprivileged_userns_clone`, because on Ubuntu 24.04 the latter doesn't exist and the AppArmor knob is what actually governs userns. If the probe comes back saying `systemd-run --user` works on Blacksmith runners, that's a real alternative backend worth a follow-up — but it stays `continue-on-error` until something reads it.

**Confidence:** 90 — 37 tests green, defect mutation-verified red→green with the mutation confirmed applied, `pre-pr` exit 0, file list verified against `origin/main`. Not higher because the CI job's actual output is unknowable until it runs on a real runner, and the macOS `Inconsistent probe` branch is asserted but has never fired in the wild.

**Next:**
1. Merge #2395 when CI + `pi-review` report (I won't `--admin` past a pending check).
2. Read the probe's step summary on the first run — it either opens a `systemd-run` follow-up or closes the question.
3. Prod-verify wakeup for #2393 (`d8a22a96`) — still owed, gated on the squash commit.
4. Optional: make `dry_run` reachable from the ClientSDK/REST `feeds.trigger` path — currently only `manage_feeds` can set it.

=== Dockerfile ===
168-# tsx-equivalent, Chromium deps for connectors.
169-#
170:# bubblewrap is what makes the contributed CLIs REACHABLE: the embedded worker
171-# registers spawned binaries only when it has an exec sandbox (probeSandbox ->
172:# bwrap) or an explicit unsandboxed opt-in. Without it `gh` sits in /usr/bin and
173-# every agent invocation exits 127 — the credential works and the command does
174-# not.
175-RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
176:      curl ca-certificates git gh unzip bubblewrap \
177-      libnss3 libnspr4 libatk1.0-0 libatk-bridge2.0-0 libcups2 libdrm2 libdbus-1-3 \
178-      libxkbcommon0 libatspi2.0-0 libxcomposite1 libxdamage1 libxfixes3 libxrandr2 \
179-      libgbm1 libpango-1.0-0 libcairo2 libasound2 libwayland-client0 \
180-    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* \

=== values.yaml ===
    preStopSleepSeconds: 5

  # Container-level hardening. runAsNonRoot is left unset because the app image
  # currently has no non-root USER (docker/app/Dockerfile) — enable it once the
  # image ships a non-root user. The defaults below are safe to apply even as
  # root and drop a meaningful amount of attack surface.
  # NOTE on connector-contributed CLIs (e.g. `gh`): the embedded worker registers
  # spawned binaries ONLY when it has a working per-exec sandbox. bubblewrap
  # needs `unshare(CLONE_NEWUSER)`, which the RuntimeDefault profile below
  # filters on most runtimes — so as shipped, probeSandboxStrategy reports
  # "none" and a contributed CLI exits 127.
  #
  # That is the SAFE default and is deliberate. Every worker and the gateway
  # share this container as the same user, so without a per-exec sandbox a
  # shell-capable CLI can read sibling `workspaces/{agentId}` directories and
  # the gateway's environment — verified, not theoretical. The pod boundary is
  # per-POD, and the tenants are inside it.
  #
  # MEASURED on this cluster (k3s v1.32.8, containerd 2.0.5, Ubuntu 24.04 /
  # kernel 6.8): bubblewrap CANNOT be enabled by any securityContext change.
  # `unshare --user` succeeds once SYS_ADMIN is added, but bwrap then fails at
  #
  #     bwrap: setting up uid map: Operation not permitted
  #
  # which still failed with SETUID+SETGID+SYS_CHROOT+MKNOD+DAC_OVERRIDE added,
  # allowPrivilegeEscalation: true, AND seccomp removed entirely. Writing
  # /proc/self/uid_map is restricted by the container runtime, not by seccomp or
  # capabilities, so no chart-level knob reaches it.
  #
  # Consequence: connector-contributed CLIs (`gh`) exit 127 on this cluster, by
  # design, and that is the SAFE outcome — see the isolation note above.
  # Enabling them needs a runtime-level change, not a values.yaml edit. Also
  # measured: this cluster declares `crun` and `gvisor` RuntimeClasses, but
  # neither handler is installed on the nodes ("no runtime for \"crun\" is
  # configured" / "...\"runsc\"..."), so switching runtimeClassName is not an
  # available workaround here either.
  #
  # Verify on any cluster before assuming otherwise:
  #   kubectl exec <app-pod> -- bwrap --unshare-user --unshare-pid --ro-bind \
  #     /usr /usr --proc /proc --dev /dev -- /usr/bin/true
  # Exit 0 means contributed CLIs will register; anything else means 127.
  # Do NOT "fix" a non-zero result with LOBU_ALLOW_UNSANDBOXED_EXEC: workers and
  # the gateway share this container, and /proc/1/environ is readable from it.
  #
  # Do NOT reach for `type: Unconfined` (drops the whole filter) or for
  # LOBU_ALLOW_UNSANDBOXED_EXEC (skips the sandbox AND unlocks full
  # interpreters); the latter is a per-agent decision for trusted agents.
  containerSecurityContext:
    allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
    capabilities:
      drop:
        - ALL
    seccompProfile:

An assert would be red by design. Instead REPORT the values.yaml probe result (bwrap --unshare-user --unshare-pid --ro-bind /usr /usr --proc /proc --dev /dev -- /usr/bin/true) so a change either way is visible. fix(agent-worker): apply the same diagnosis to the explicit-override throw

Review on #2395 found the second instance of the defect this branch fixes:
`LOBU_EXEC_SANDBOX=bwrap` on a host that cannot honour it threw "Install
bubblewrap and ensure kernel.unprivileged_userns_clone=1" regardless of
cause. That is worse there than in the passive warning — an operator who
sets the override is deliberately asking why the sandbox is off, and on the
managed cluster the answer is neither a missing package nor that sysctl,
which does not exist on Ubuntu 24.04.

Both sites now route through `explainBwrapUnavailable`, so only a genuinely
absent bwrap ever recommends installing anything.

Also collapses the probe. The previous commit kept `bwrapDeliversIsolation`
as the selection predicate and added `probeBwrap` beside it, sharing an args
constant so the two could not describe different flag sets. Deleting the
predicate outright is the better answer: one function cannot drift from
itself, and the shared constant existed only to police the duplication.
`probeBwrap` now returns the resolved path on success, so selection reads it
directly, and the auto path passes its probe result into `describeNoSandbox`
instead of spawning bwrap a second time to ask the same question.

The module header claimed `--unshare-user` requires
`kernel.unprivileged_userns_clone=1`. That is the Debian knob; Ubuntu 24.04
governs userns through AppArmor and a container runtime can restrict uid_map
regardless of either — which is why the probe is a real spawn and not a
sysctl read.
EOF

Follow-up commit `10c9f6a4` — acting on the review's "pre-existing, untouched" note about `exec-sandbox.ts:221`.

That note found the **second instance of the same defect**, which is exactly the case AGENTS.md's "fix the class, not the instance" rule covers: a diff-scoped reviewer only ever finds the next one. `git grep` on `origin/main` confirms there were exactly two in code (the CI install steps and `scripts/install-bubblewrap.sh` are real installers, correctly untouched).

**1. The override throw now gets the same diagnosis.** `LOBU_EXEC_SANDBOX=bwrap` on an unusable host prescribed "Install bubblewrap and ensure `kernel.unprivileged_userns_clone=1`" for both causes. Worse there than in the passive warning: an operator who sets that override is deliberately asking *why* the sandbox is off. Both sites now route through `explainBwrapUnavailable`, so only a genuinely absent bwrap recommends installing anything.

**2. The probe is collapsed to one function.** The first commit kept `bwrapDeliversIsolation` as the selection predicate and added `probeBwrap` beside it, with a shared args constant so the two couldn't describe different flag sets. Deleting the predicate is the better answer — one function cannot drift from itself, and the constant existed only to police the duplication. `probeBwrap` returns the resolved path on success, and the auto path hands its result to `describeNoSandbox` rather than spawning bwrap a second time to ask the same question.

**3. A stale claim in the module header.** It said `--unshare-user` requires `kernel.unprivileged_userns_clone=1`. That's the Debian knob — it doesn't exist on Ubuntu 24.04, where AppArmor governs userns, and a container runtime can restrict `uid_map` regardless of either. That's *why* the probe is a real spawn rather than a sysctl read.

### Red → green

Mutation: restore the old override message.

```
RED
  (fail) probeSandboxStrategy > explicit override fails closed when backend unavailable
  (fail) formatBwrapOverrideError > still fails closed and names the override requested
  (fail) formatBwrapOverrideError > a userns refusal does not tell the operator to install anything
  (fail) formatBwrapOverrideError > a missing bubblewrap is still allowed to say install it
   36 pass | 12 skip | 4 fail

GREEN (restored)
   40 pass | 12 skip | 0 fail
```

`make pre-pr` clean on the settled diff.

### One deliberate test change

The pre-existing `explicit override fails closed` test pinned the old wording and is darwin-only. It now asserts only that an unhonourable override **throws** rather than degrading to `kind:"none"` — the part that genuinely needs the real code path. Wording is asserted by `formatBwrapOverrideError`, which runs on every host; leaving message assertions in a darwin-gated test would make the production branch (a Linux userns refusal) untestable anywhere but a Linux box that also blocks userns.

content.text:
While that builds — the bubblewrap answer:

## Where bubblewrap is actually used

One call site, three layers around it.

**The call site** is `just-bash-bootstrap.ts:64`. When an embedded agent's just-bash script spawns a binary — `gh`, `git`, `lobu`, anything from `/nix/store` — the invocation goes through `wrapInvocation` first, which prepends `bwrap` plus bind mounts (or `sandbox-exec` plus an SBPL profile on macOS).

**The Dockerfile installs it** (`docker/app/Dockerfile:170`) with a comment that states the real stake:

> bubblewrap is what makes the contributed CLIs REACHABLE

That's the part worth understanding. The embedded worker **registers spawned binaries only when it has a working sandbox**. No sandbox means `gh` sits in `/usr/bin`, unregistered, and every agent invocation exits 127 — *"the credential works and the command does not."*

**The chart explains why it's off in prod anyway** (`charts/lobu/values.yaml:96-108`), and this is the thing my PR is really about. Someone already measured it properly on k3s v1.32.8 / Ubuntu 24.04:

```
bwrap: setting up uid map: Operation not permitted
```

That persisted with `SYS_ADMIN`, with `SETUID+SETGID+SYS_CHROOT+MKNOD+DAC_OVERRIDE`, with `allowPrivilegeEscalation: true`, and **with seccomp removed entirely**. Writing `/proc/self/uid_map` is restricted by the container runtime, so no chart-level knob reaches it. They also checked the escape hatches: the cluster declares `crun` and `gvisor` RuntimeClasses but neither handler is installed on the nodes.

## Why 127 is the correct outcome, not a bug

This is the bit that makes the whole design cohere. Every worker *and* the gateway share one container as the same user. Without a per-exec sandbox, a shell-capable CLI can read sibling `workspaces/{agentId}` directories and the gateway's environment — the chart notes this was **verified, not theoretical**. The pod boundary is per-pod; the tenants are inside it.

So the sandbox isn't hardening around a trust boundary — it *is* the trust boundary. That's why `LOBU_ALLOW_UNSANDBOXED_EXEC` is explicitly called out as the wrong fix: `/proc/1/environ` is readable from that container.

## How this connects to the PR

The system behaves correctly and the operator-facing story was the only broken part. A correct, deliberate refusal was reported as *"Install bubblewrap"* — advice pointing at a package that's already in the image, for a restriction no package can lift, citing a sysctl that doesn't exist on the distro in question. Now the log carries the kernel's own `uid_map` refusal and the `values.yaml` pointer to the measurement.

The macOS `sandbox-exec` path is the same idea for local `lobu run` — weaker (allow-default with denies, since that's what SBPL gives you) but it covers the dev machine where the workspace sits under `/Users`.

content.content: @AGENTS.md
content.rawContent:
<!-- Per-repo agent rules loaded into every Claude Code session in this repo. Inlines AGENTS.md (shared project rules) first, then layers local-only notes below. User memory entries live under ~/.claude/projects/.../memory/. Don't add anything here unless it's only relevant to Claude agent specific. If other harnesses like pi or codex need it, modify AGENTS.md -->

@AGENTS.md

content.content:
## Repo map
- Bun workspace under `packages/*`; TS source is in `src`, tests in `__tests__`.
- Main packages: `core` shared types/utils, `plugin-api` native plugin contracts, `plugin-host` deterministic plugin composition, `server` gateway + embedded runtime, `agent-worker` Lobu agent execution, `connectors` built-in connectors, `owletto` frontend submodule.
- Before editing a package, read its nearest `AGENTS.md` if present.
- `docs/GOTCHAS.md` collects the mechanical traps (build, SQL, testing, submodule, browser) that have each cost a debugging session. Skim the section for the surface you are touching before you start, and grep it when something looks inexplicable.

## Hard invariants
- **Never write to `~/Code/lobu` directly — work in a worktree.** Run `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` first, and never `git switch` in the main checkout.
- One branch = one concern (not one file). Tangential task → commit/push/open current work, then branch fresh from `main`. Split only for genuinely independent concerns or an unreviewable diff.
- **Multi-replica correctness is mandatory.** Never put shared required state in an in-memory Map/singleton another replica must read or mutate. If a feature relies on cross-pod visibility, use Postgres-mediated state/signal.
- **`events` is append-only.** Never `DELETE FROM events`; tombstone/supersede instead.
- **Request paths never aggregate history.** No `GROUP BY`, `DISTINCT ON`, per-row `regexp_*`, or leading-wildcard `LIKE` over an append-only / run-history table (`events`, `agent_transcript_snapshot`, `session_calls`, …) on a user-facing read path. History only grows, so read-time aggregation cost grows with it while the answer stays bounded. Materialize the row or counter at WRITE time and read it back by index; run the one-time aggregation in a migration, never per request. Aggregating bounded config tables (`connections`, `watchers`, `agent_users`) is fine.
- **Never bulk-delete prod `organization` rows**, including zero-activity ones — empty-looking orgs are frequently real human signups. Surface them one at a time for confirmation.
- **Workers never receive real credentials.** They may receive only placeholders/proxied access. The only exceptions are device-pinned connectors and short-lived provider-derived credential leases (see `packages/server/AGENTS.md`); a durable stored credential is never one of them.
- Default to static `import`. New dynamic imports require measured cost justification here or in the package AGENTS plus a rationale comment at the call site. Tests may dynamically import after mocks.
  - Node-version gate exceptions: `packages/cli/bin/lobu.js` defers the existing CLI graph without duplicating it, and `packages/server/src/server-entry.ts` adds an 842-byte gate in front of the 4.34 MB server graph (measured 2026-07-24). Both call sites must stay dependency-free until their checks pass.
- Bug fixes require red→fix→green evidence, with both outputs pasted into the PR body. If you cannot reproduce, stop and report the dead end — do not ship a speculative fix.
- Never report done off a green typecheck. Boot it, exercise every branch you touched, clean up test data. If "compiles" is all you ran, say so explicitly.
- Gates are non-negotiable (sequence in "Ship a change" below). `make pre-pr` builds first — that build step is what protects against a stale-dist false green. `make review` is an LLM verdict only: it does NOT run typecheck/knip/tests and is not proof CI will pass.
- The agent-facing product name is **Behavior**; `watcher` is internal engine/DB vocabulary. It must not appear in MCP tool schemas/names/descriptions, ClientSDK discovery metadata, or the connector-sdk public reaction contract — `make pre-pr` fails on it. Internal identifiers (`actingWatcherId`, table/column names, comments) are fine.
- `make review-fix` is the unposted fixer pass and runs BEFORE the first `make review`; verify its diff and commit it. Never iterate `make review` as a find-fix loop — each posted round costs a review + CI cycle.
- Fix the class, not the instance: on the first hit, grep every other instance and fix in one pass — a diff-scoped reviewer only ever finds the next one. An assert would be red by design. Instead REPORT the values.yaml probe result (bwrap --unshare-user --unshare-pid --ro-bind /usr /usr --proc /proc --dev /dev -- /usr/bin/true) so a change either way is visible. See memory reference_contributed_clis_exit_127_by_design. The systemd-run --user probe half stands unchanged.

content.text:
Three PRs open. Here's where things stand.

## What I found doing item 4 — the premise was wrong

I had this tracked as *"`dry_run` is unreachable from the ClientSDK because `feeds.trigger` calls `createSyncRun` without options."* Both halves were wrong.

`feeds.trigger` never calls `createSyncRun`. It forwards its input verbatim through `createActionCaller` to the `trigger_feed` action, whose TypeBox schema has accepted `dry_run` since #2390. And scripts are transpiled by esbuild, which strips types without checking them — so the narrow declared type never blocked anything at runtime either.

I proved it rather than reasoning about it. The new test passes against **completely unmodified source**:

```
=== source reverted; only the new test file present ===
?? src/__tests__/integration/feeds-sdk-trigger-dry-run.test.ts
=== run against UNMODIFIED source ===
 ✓ feeds-sdk-trigger-dry-run.test.ts (3 tests)  Tests  3 passed (3)
```

So #4 is a **type + discoverability** change, not a plumbing one: `FeedsNamespace.trigger` now declares `dry_run?: boolean`, and `method-metadata.ts` documents it so `search_sdk` actually tells agents it exists. That last part was the real gap — an agent had no way to discover a flag that already worked.

The test is the load-bearing artifact here, since "widening a type to match behaviour" and "adding behaviour" look identical in a diff.

## The blocker was never mine

`check-drift` fails on #2395 — and on every other open PR. owletto#669 merged without the parent submodule bump. CI prescribes fixing it as a separate PR, so **#2396** does that.

One thing worth knowing: `make task-setup NAME=owletto-pointer-bump` silently **reused a July 28 worktree** whose commit pinned `260a9861` — now *behind* main. Pushing it would have walked the pointer backwards and reverted merged work. I branched fresh from `origin/main` and asserted direction explicitly:

```
$ git -C packages/owletto merge-base --is-ancestor 21fc1c33 fdcb39ff && echo ok
ok
```

Reused task-setup names are a live footgun for exactly the failure mode AGENTS.md warns about.

## Status

| PR | what | state |
|---|---|---|
| #2395 | exec-sandbox diagnosis + CI probe | 2 commits; blocked on #2396 only |
| #2396 | owletto pointer bump | pre-pr clean, unblocks everything |
| #4 | SDK `dry_run` type + discovery | pre-pr clean, `review-fix` running |

On #2395 I also acted on the review's "pre-existing, untouched" note — it had found the **second** instance of the same defect (the `LOBU_EXEC_SANDBOX=bwrap` throw). Per the fix-the-class rule I grepped `origin/main`, confirmed exactly two in code, fixed both, and collapsed `bwrapDeliversIsolation` into `probeBwrap` — one function can't drift from itself, which made the shared-args-constant guard unnecessary. Mutation-verified 4-fail → 0-fail.

**Confidence:** #2396 **95** (pointer-only, ancestry asserted) · #2395 **90** (mutation-verified both instances, pre-pr clean; CI probe output still unknown until it runs) · item 4 **92** (3 integration tests green, pre-existing behaviour proven by revert-and-rerun; `review-fix` not yet read).

**Next:** merge #2396 first to unblock the queue, then #2395 once check-drift reruns green, then PR item 4. Prod-verify for #2393 is still owed.

content.text:
Holding the merge. Here's the situation:

## #2396 is not safe to merge — it breaks a test for real

```
FAIL device-connector-manifests.test.ts
  > accepts the actual Owletto Mac manifests
AssertionError: expected null not to be null
Test Files  1 failed | 367 passed (368)
```

That test loads the **real** manifests out of `packages/owletto/apps/mac/Owletto/ConnectorManifests/`, so bumping the pointer pulls in owletto#669's new `os_shell.json` — and afterwards `apple.screen_time`, `apple.computer_use`, and `local.directory` all come back null. The device poll returned 200, so the manifests were accepted and then *nothing installed*, which points at batch-level rejection rather than one bad entry.

`os_shell.json` is the only new manifest and the only one with an empty `feeds_schema: {}` plus an `actions_schema`. That's my leading hypothesis, not a conclusion — the local repro is still building.

**This is exactly why the pointer bump is a separate PR.** Merging it with `--admin` would have put a red integration suite on main and broken device-connector installs for every Mac user. And it wasn't a flake — I checked before assuming.

## Everything else is green

| PR | verdict | required checks |
|---|---|---|
| **#2395** exec-sandbox | 91 / 80 / slop 10 / **0 bugs, 0 blockers** | all pass **except** check-drift, which needs #2396 |
| **#2396** pointer bump | 92 / 100 / slop 0 / 0 bugs | **integration fails** ← real |
| item 4 SDK dry_run | pre-pr clean, review-fix done | not yet PR'd |

So there's a genuine dependency knot: #2395 can't go green until the pointer bump lands, and the pointer bump can't land until the manifest break is fixed.

## What I'd do

Fix the manifest rejection in the same PR as the bump — it's the same concern (making the parent accept the current submodule), and neither half is mergeable alone. If the fix turns out to belong on the owletto side instead, that's an owletto PR first, then re-bump.

I'm not merging anything until I've reproduced the failure locally and know which of the three definitions dies and why. Want me to proceed with that, or would you rather look at `os_shell.json` yourself first — given it ships a `requiresApproval` shell-exec action, it may deserve a design look independent of the test break?

content.text:
Root cause confirmed, and it's worse than a test failure. Full chain:

1. owletto#669 ships `os_shell.json` with key `os.shell`
2. `connectorKeyAllowedForPlatform('macos', 'os.shell')` → **false** — the allowlist is `apple.*`, `local.directory`, `whatsapp.local` (`device-manifests.ts:267`)
3. That manifest throws → caught → **`accepted = false`** for the whole payload
4. `poll.ts:271` then sets `connectorManifestMap = null` and writes `{}`

Step 4 is deliberate and correct — the comment says a rejected payload must not replace the last good inventory. But it means **one unknown key drops every manifest on the device**. A Mac on the new build would lose screen time, calendar, photos and WhatsApp too, not just `os.shell`. That's a production regression waiting on the Mac release, not just red CI.

```
"err":"connector key 'os.shell' is not allowed for platform 'macos'"
× accepts the actual Owletto Mac manifests → expected null not to be null
```

The decisive detail: `os.shell` is **already** in `OS_CAPABILITIES` and `PLATFORM_ALLOWLIST.macos` already spreads it (`packages/core/src/capabilities.ts:28-60`). So the capability is authorized for macOS — only the coarser *key* namespace check was never updated. The two lists drifted.

/**
 * Coarse namespace check on the connector KEY. The real gate is the
 * `required_capability` check in the caller, which authorizes against
 * PLATFORM_ALLOWLIST in @lobu/core — a key admitted here still cannot install
 * unless its capability is allowlisted for the platform.
 *
 * Keep the `os.` namespace in sync with OS_CAPABILITIES. It is admitted as a
 * prefix rather than one key at a time because the cost of an omission is not
 * confined to the offending manifest: a single unrecognised key throws, sets
 * `accepted = false` for the WHOLE payload, and the caller then declines to
 * replace the device's inventory (poll.ts) — deliberately, so a malformed poll
 * cannot look like removal. The result is that one unknown key silently drops
 * every OTHER connector on that device. `os.shell` (owletto#669) did exactly
 * that: it was already authorized as a capability in @lobu/core, but this list
 * had not been updated, so a Mac on that build lost screen time, calendar,
 * photos and WhatsApp along with it.
 */
function connectorKeyAllowedForPlatform(platform: string, key: string): boolean {
  if (platform === 'macos') {
    return (
      key.startsWith('apple.') ||
      key.startsWith('os.') ||
      key === 'local.directory' ||
      key === 'whatsapp.local'
    );
  }

<!-- Per-repo agent rules loaded into every Claude Code session in this repo. Inlines AGENTS.md (shared project rules) first, then layers local-only notes below. content.content:
## Repo map
- Bun workspace under `packages/*`; TS source is in `src`, tests in `__tests__`.
- Main packages: `core` shared types/utils, `plugin-api` native plugin contracts, `plugin-host` deterministic plugin composition, `server` gateway + embedded runtime, `agent-worker` Lobu agent execution, `connectors` built-in connectors, `owletto` frontend submodule.
- Before editing a package, read its nearest `AGENTS.md` if present.
- `docs/GOTCHAS.md` collects the mechanical traps (build, SQL, testing, submodule, browser) that have each cost a debugging session. Skim the section for the surface you are touching before you start, and grep it when something looks inexplicable.

## Hard invariants
- **Never write to `~/Code/lobu` directly — work in a worktree.** Run `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` first, and never `git switch` in the main checkout.
- One branch = one concern (not one file). Tangential task → commit/push/open current work, then branch fresh from `main`. Split only for genuinely independent concerns or an unreviewable diff.
- **Multi-replica correctness is mandatory.** Never put shared required state in an in-memory Map/singleton another replica must read or mutate. If a feature relies on cross-pod visibility, use Postgres-mediated state/signal.
- **`events` is append-only.** Never `DELETE FROM events`; tombstone/supersede instead.
- **Request paths never aggregate history.** No `GROUP BY`, `DISTINCT ON`, per-row `regexp_*`, or leading-wildcard `LIKE` over an append-only / run-history table (`events`, `agent_transcript_snapshot`, `session_calls`, …) on a user-facing read path. History only grows, so read-time aggregation cost grows with it while the answer stays bounded. Materialize the row or counter at WRITE time and read it back by index; run the one-time aggregation in a migration, never per request. Aggregating bounded config tables (`connections`, `watchers`, `agent_users`) is fine.
- **Never bulk-delete prod `organization` rows**, including zero-activity ones — empty-looking orgs are frequently real human signups. Surface them one at a time for confirmation.
- **Workers never receive real credentials.** They may receive only placeholders/proxied access. The only exceptions are device-pinned connectors and short-lived provider-derived credential leases (see `packages/server/AGENTS.md`); a durable stored credential is never one of them.
- Default to static `import`. New dynamic imports require measured cost justification here or in the package AGENTS plus a rationale comment at the call site. Tests may dynamically import after mocks.
  - Node-version gate exceptions: `packages/cli/bin/lobu.js` defers the existing CLI graph without duplicating it, and `packages/server/src/server-entry.ts` adds an 842-byte gate in front of the 4.34 MB server graph (measured 2026-07-24). Both call sites must stay dependency-free until their checks pass.
- Bug fixes require red→fix→green evidence, with both outputs pasted into the PR body. If you cannot reproduce, stop and report the dead end — do not ship a speculative fix.
- Never report done off a green typecheck. Boot it, exercise every branch you touched, clean up test data. If "compiles" is all you ran, say so explicitly.
- Gates are non-negotiable (sequence in "Ship a change" below). `make pre-pr` builds first — that build step is what protects against a stale-dist false green. `make review` is an LLM verdict only: it does NOT run typecheck/knip/tests and is not proof CI will pass.
- The agent-facing product name is **Behavior**; `watcher` is internal engine/DB vocabulary. It must not appear in MCP tool schemas/names/descriptions, ClientSDK discovery metadata, or the connector-sdk public reaction contract — `make pre-pr` fails on it. Internal identifiers (`actingWatcherId`, table/column names, comments) are fine.
- `make review-fix` is the unposted fixer pass and runs BEFORE the first `make review`; verify its diff and commit it. Never iterate `make review` as a find-fix loop — each posted round costs a review + CI cycle.
- Fix the class, not the instance: on the first hit, grep every other instance and fix in one pass — a diff-scoped reviewer only ever finds the next one. Same root cause twice = stop reviewing, grep-enumerate. A class-wide fix is in scope for the branch that found it and does not count as scope creep.
- **Fail closed on durable dispatch/delivery state.** When a durable coordination or delivery operation fails, its caller must not reinterpret the error as proceed/deliver/skip. Propagate a retry, defer, or terminal-failure outcome with a visible log; if the operation may already have succeeded, reconcile idempotently before retrying. Treat lock timeouts, pool errors, and ambiguous or expired rows as failures, not as "nothing changed."
- **Coordination design brake.** A change that needs a second lock, a second retry/deferral budget, or a prose termination argument to explain why it halts is patching a misplaced check — stop and re-derive where the decision belongs before adding mechanism. - **Stage by explicit path; never commit the whole tree of a worktree that hosted other work.** A commit is a snapshot — stale file copies silently revert already-merged PRs. ## Ship a change
1. `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` → work in `.claude/worktrees/<slug>/`.
2. Reproduce the bug (red) before fixing it. Fix, then prove green.
3. Test: `make test-unit` (no DB) / `make test-integration` (needs `DATABASE_URL` with pgvector). One file: `bun test <path>`, or `cd packages/server && bunx vitest run <path>` for vitest suites.
4. `make pre-pr` — build, typecheck, knip, lint, exposed-surface naming.
5. `make review-fix` on the settled diff and verify what it changed — it edits the working tree, so re-read the files before trusting them.
6. Stage by explicit path (`git add -- <paths>`, never `-A`), commit, then confirm `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` is exactly your intended file list. Extra files = stop.
7. `git push -u origin <branch>` → `gh pr create` (fill `.github/pull_request_template.md`; conventional-commit title, e.g. `fix(server): …`).
8. `make review` **once** on the settled HEAD. It posts the `pi-review` status, which is a REQUIRED check.
9. Merge squash once CI is green: `gh pr merge <n> --squash --admin`. Never `--admin` past a check that has not reported.
10. Prod-visible surface? Verify it live after rollout. - Do only what was asked. Delete ephemeral files you create. Do not create `*.md` unless asked.
- Prefer `bun`; do not use npm/yarn/pnpm for repo work.
- Fix unused params by deleting them, not `_`-prefixing.

- Show the diff, not a summary. Before claiming done — on your own work or a dispatched agent's — surface `git status` plus `git diff --stat <base>...HEAD`. An agent's self-report is a claim; the diff is the evidence.
- UI PRs owe before/after screenshots, and `gh` cannot upload images inline. Capture before shots from the unmodified branch and after shots from the same booted app (auth recipe in `docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md`), base64-embed the PNGs into one self-contained HTML comparison page, publish it as a claude.ai artifact, and link it from the PR.
- Any subagent with write access (Edit/Write/Bash) runs in its own worktree; only grep/read agents share the parent. Two writing agents must NEVER share a worktree — they overwrite each other's uncommitted work.
- Dispatch code-writing agents through `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` and brief them with the absolute `.claude/worktrees/<slug>/` path. Only task-setup does the submodule branch pinning, post-init `bun install`, `.env` copy, and port allocation.
- Do repetitive multi-file edits (renames, signature changes, import rewrites) inline or with one script. Reserve subagents for read-only breadth or genuinely isolated parallel work.
- Before adding an env var, grep for the one the codebase already reads. Do not rename existing vars to a "cleaner" convention unasked.
- Deleting code needs structural evidence (dangling import, completed migration, superseded impl). Low prod usage is not a delete signal; trace the workflow, not just the import graph — docs and help text are load-bearing too.
- **Absence is never proven by a grep on a working tree.** To prove code does *not* exist, run `git fetch -q origin && git grep <pattern> origin/main` — the fetch is load-bearing, `origin/main` itself goes stale. Applies to every existence check, including the deletion-evidence rule above.
- Slack link pasted (`slack.com/archives/…?thread_ts=`) → run `scripts/slack-thread-viewer.js "<link>"` first.
- To drive the user's real logged-in browser, use the paired Owletto extension — recipe in `docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md`. Do **not** assume CDP/browser-auth is required.
- Unsure in planning → ask before making conflicting or irreversible choices. Mid-execution, block on a question only for irreversible/destructive actions or decisions that are genuinely the user's; for reversible choices with a clear recommended option, take it and flag the choice in your summary.

## Session efficiency
- Never poll in the foreground (`sleep`/`until`/`while` wait loops, repeated `tail`). Run long waits (dev-server boot, CI, deploys) in the background and act on the completion notification.
- Prefer DOM reads (`get_page_text`, `read_page`, `javascript_tool`) over screenshots; screenshot only when visual layout itself is under test. Screenshots are the #1 context-bloat source.
- Read a file before editing it, and re-read it after any external change (a fixer pass, another agent, a rebase). Blind edits fail and cost a retry round-trip.
- Read PR status compactly: `gh pr view <n> --json number,title,isDraft,mergeStateStatus,reviewDecision` plus `gh pr checks <n> --required`. Never `--json statusCheckRollup` — measured on PR 2280 it is 7520 bytes against 861, 8.7x larger and less legible.
- Batch narrow fixes into one commit, verified once at the end of the batch — not per fix. It never justifies skipping a reproducer or a correctness-critical test. For a one-line or config-only change, take one CI snapshot and move on.

I found a real bug, so I'm not merging yet. Here's the call I need from you.

## What the pointer bump exposed

Reproduced locally, exact cause:

```
"err":"connector key 'os.shell' is not allowed for platform 'macos'"
× accepts the actual Owletto Mac manifests → expected null not to be null
```

`connectorKeyAllowedForPlatform` admits `apple.*`, `local.directory`, `whatsapp.local` — not `os.shell`. That single unknown key throws, sets **`accepted = false` for the whole payload**, and `poll.ts:271` then refuses to replace the device's inventory at all.

That refusal is deliberate and right — a malformed poll must not look like removal. But the consequence is that **one unrecognised key silently drops every other connector on that Mac**: screen time, calendar, photos, WhatsApp. This is a production regression waiting on the Mac release, not just red CI.

## The fix, and why I think it's the right shape

`os.shell` is **already** in `OS_CAPABILITIES`, and `PLATFORM_ALLOWLIST.macos` already spreads it (`packages/core/src/capabilities.ts:28-60`). So the capability was authorized all along — only the coarser *key* namespace check drifted. I admitted `os.` as a prefix (matching how `apple.` works) rather than one key at a time, because `os.files` and `os.notifications` are also already in `OS_CAPABILITIES` and would each hit this same whole-payload failure later.

Mutation-verified: remove the line → **2 fail** (my guard + the real-manifest test); restore → **14 pass**.

## The decision that's yours

This authorizes a connector that runs **arbitrary shell commands as the signed-in user** via `zsh -l -c`. The manifest self-describes as `requiresApproval: true`, `destructiveHint: true`, `openWorldHint: true`, and *"Same trust tier as computer use."*

I lean toward shipping it: core already allowlisted the capability, owletto#669 is already merged, and the alternative leaves main red and Mac manifests broken. But "gateway now accepts a shell-exec connector" deserves your explicit yes rather than my inference from `capabilities.ts`.

Worth noting the two lists can drift precisely because they're maintained separately — the capability allowlist lives in `core`, the key allowlist in `server`. A follow-up could derive one from the other.

**Confidence:** 93 on the diagnosis and fix (reproduced red, mutation-verified, 14/14 green locally); pre-pr still running.

Say the word and I'll commit, re-review, and merge #2396 → #2395 → item 4 in order. If you'd rather `os.shell` not be enabled server-side yet, the alternative is reverting owletto#669's manifest instead — that keeps the gateway unchanged but needs an owletto PR first.

git push -q origin chore/owletto-pointer-bump-0731 && echo PUSHED && gh pr edit 2396 --title "fix(server): admit os.* device connector keys, and bump the owletto pointer" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary

Two commits, one concern: **make the parent accept the current owletto main.** Neither half is mergeable alone — the bump without the fix breaks device connectors; the fix without the bump has nothing to fix.

**1. Pointer bump.** owletto#669 merged without it, so `check-drift` (a required check) fails on every open PR. Pinned `21fc1c33` → `fdcb39ff`, verified forward-only:

```
$ git -C packages/owletto merge-base --is-ancestor 21fc1c33 fdcb39ff && echo ok
ok
```

**2. `os.*` key namespace.** The bump turned `device-connector-manifests.test.ts` red. `connectorKeyAllowedForPlatform` admitted `apple.*`, `local.directory`, `whatsapp.local` — not `os.shell`, which owletto#669 ships.

The capability side was never the problem: `os.shell` is already in `OS_CAPABILITIES` and `PLATFORM_ALLOWLIST.macos` already spreads it. The two lists drifted, and only the coarse key check rejected it.

### Why this is worse than a failing test

An unrecognised key throws → `accepted = false` for the **entire payload** → the caller declines to replace the device's inventory at all (`poll.ts:271`). That refusal is deliberate and correct (a malformed poll must not look like removal), but it means **one unknown key drops every other connector on that Mac**. A device on the new build would lose screen time, calendar, photos and WhatsApp too — a production regression waiting on the Mac release, not just red CI.

Admitted as an `os.` **prefix** rather than one key at a time: `os.files` and `os.notifications` are also already in `OS_CAPABILITIES` and would each hit this identical whole-payload failure later. The prefix is a namespace check, **not** an authorization — `required_capability` is still authorized independently against `@lobu/core`, so a key admitted here cannot install unless its capability is allowlisted too.

## Test plan
- [x] `make pre-pr` clean (build + typecheck + knip + lint + exposed-surface naming)
- [x] Tests run: `bunx vitest run src/__tests__/integration/device-connector-manifests.test.ts` — 14 passed
- [x] Bug fix: red→fix→green below
- [ ] If bot behavior: n/a

### Red → green

RED (reproduced locally with the pointer bumped, before the fix):

```
warn: "connector key 'os.shell' is not allowed for platform 'macos'"
      [device-manifests] dropped invalid manifest
× accepts the actual Owletto Mac manifests and installs their connector definitions
  → expected null not to be null
   Tests  1 failed | 12 passed (13)
```

GREEN:

```
   Tests  14 passed (14)
```

Mutation (drop `key.startsWith('os.')`) — confirms both guards are load-bearing:

```
× admits the os.* namespace on macOS and does not let one unknown key drop its siblings
× accepts the actual Owletto Mac manifests and installs their connector definitions
   Tests  2 failed | 12 passed (14)
```

## Notes

### Security surface — flagging explicitly

This admits a connector that runs **arbitrary shell commands as the signed-in user** (`zsh -l -c`). The manifest self-describes as `requiresApproval: true`, `destructiveHint: true`, `openWorldHint: true`, *"same trust tier as computer use."* The capability was already allowlisted in `@lobu/core`, so this PR does not widen the trust model — it aligns the key check with a decision already made there — but it is the change that makes the connector reachable, and it should be read as such.

### Why the new test uses synthetic keys

The first version asserted on `apple.screen_time` and **passed alone but failed in the full file**: that key also exists in the bundled device-connector catalog, which puts it on a different reconcile path and makes the outcome depend on catalog state rather than on the allowlist under test. It also deliberately does not assert that `os.shell`'s own definition materializes — it declares no feeds, and what reconcile does with a feedless device connector is a separate question.

### Drift is structural

The capability allowlist lives in `packages/core`, the key allowlist in `packages/server`. They are maintained separately, which is why they drifted. Deriving one from the other is a reasonable follow-up; not attempted here to keep this PR to the break it fixes.
EOF

test(server): pin the sibling-drop blast radius of an unknown manifest key

The real-manifest parity test now asserts os.shell installs, which covers
the fix only for as long as owletto happens to ship os_shell.json. This
pins the property that made the bug expensive, with synthetic keys that do
not depend on what any repo ships.

The property: an unrecognised key does not merely drop itself. It sets
accepted=false for the whole payload, and the caller then declines to
replace the device's inventory at all — so every OTHER connector on that
device disappears with it. That is why the allowlist must not lag behind
the manifests, and it is the assertion that would have caught owletto#669
before the pointer bump reached CI.

Synthetic keys are deliberate. An earlier version asserted on
apple.screen_time and passed alone but failed in the full file: that key
also exists in the bundled device-connector catalog, so it takes a
different reconcile path and the outcome tracks catalog state rather than
the allowlist under test.

Primes the module-level materialize cooldown the same way this file's first
test does. Without that the test failed about 2 runs in 7 (singleFork +
isolate:false makes it depend on whether a preceding poll left the cooldown
hot); with it, 6 consecutive clean runs.

content.text:
I stopped short of merging, and I'd rather you decide the last bit. Three things happened worth reporting.

## The Codesmith bot beat me to the fix — and its version was better

While I was working, the bot pushed to my branch (my push was rejected non-fast-forward). It had reached the identical diagnosis independently, including the whole-payload blast radius.

Its fix was narrower than mine: `key === 'os.shell'` where I'd written `key.startsWith('os.')`. Its comment carried the argument that changed my mind:

> a new on-device connector **must land here in the same change that ships its manifest**

That reframes the allowlist as a deliberate per-connector opt-in — a review checkpoint — not a filter that drifted by accident. My prefix would have removed that checkpoint on a shell-execution surface, and pre-authorized `os.files` and `os.notifications` while I was at it. I dropped my version and took the bot's.

I did **not** force-push over it.

## My own test was flaky and I nearly shipped it

After adopting the bot's fix I re-ran the suite repeatedly instead of accepting one green:

```
run1: 1 failed | 13 passed   ← mine
run2: 14 passed
run3: 14 passed
```

Measured both ways, same 10 real manifests:

**Without the fix** (a Mac on the new build hitting today's gateway):
```
SHIPPED:   apple.calendar, apple.computer_use, apple.health, apple.photos,
           apple.reminders, apple.screen_time, apple.system_audio,
           local.directory, os.shell, whatsapp.local
INSTALLED: (NONE)
```

**With the fix:**
```
INSTALLED: all 10, including apple.computer_use
```

## Answering directly

**Yes, computer use breaks** — but not because of anything computer use did. One unrecognised key (`os.shell`) makes the gateway reject the *entire* poll payload, so all ten connectors install as zero. Calendar, health, photos, reminders, screen time, system audio, WhatsApp, local directory — all gone with it.

**`os.shell` is not computer use.** They're separate connectors: `apple.computer_use` already existed; `os.shell` is new from owletto#669. The confusion is fair — the manifest describes itself as *"same trust tier as computer use"*, but that's a comparison of how dangerous it is, not a statement that it's the same feature. Computer use drives the UI; `os.shell` runs `zsh -l -c` directly.

**The fix doesn't break anything — it prevents a break.** What breaks is merging the pointer bump *without* it. And since `check-drift` is failing on every open PR until the pointer bump lands, the bump isn't really optional.

## So the actual decision is narrower than I framed it

I said this was "authorize shell exec, yes or no." That was imprecise. `os.shell` is already merged in owletto and already capability-allowlisted in `@lobu/core` — it ships on the next Mac release regardless. The gateway-side choice is only:

- **Merge as-is** → all 10 connectors work, `os.shell` among them.
- **Don't** → all 10 break the moment that Mac build lands, including computer use.

There's no variant where `os.shell` stays off *and* the other nine keep working — the payload is all-or-nothing by design.

If you want `os.shell` genuinely disabled, that has to happen in owletto (drop `os_shell.json`) or by removing the capability from `@lobu/core`, not by withholding the key.

**Confidence:** 97 — measured directly on the real manifests, both directions, rather than inferred.

`createTestConnectorDefinition` defaults to `organization_id: null` (the global catalog row), but `resolveActiveConnectorVersion` resolves on `(connector_key, org)`. content.text:
The blocker was legitimate and I'm glad the merge waited on it.

## What the reviewer caught that I missed

My test was flaky, and **my fix for it was wrong**. I attributed the flake to the module-level materialize cooldown and added a primer poll. Real cause:

Both synthetic manifests inherited `name: 'Device Manifest Test'` from the helper. `ensureDeviceConnectorWired` runs per-key under `Promise.allSettled` with an advisory lock keyed on `(userId, connectorKey)` — so two same-named manifests race `ensureUniqueConnectionSlug`, one connection INSERT loses on `connections_org_slug_unique`, and `allSettled` **swallows** it. The definition never lands.

I verified the correction is causal rather than trusting another green streak:

| | result |
|---|---|
| without distinct name | **1 / 8 failed** |
| with distinct name | **8 / 8 passed** |

Reviewer independently measured 3/8 and 5/5. My earlier "6/6 with the primer" sits comfortably inside chance at that failure rate — it was never evidence. I removed the primer *and* its comment, since shipping a confident wrong explanation is worse than shipping nothing.

That's the third time today a first green misled me. The pattern is consistent: single runs and short streaks don't establish anything about a race.

## A real bug fell out of it

The reviewer's aside is worth more than the test fix: **two same-named device-manifest connectors wired in one reconcile pass can lose a connection INSERT in production.** It self-heals on the next poll via slug suffixing, and today's real manifests all have distinct names, so it's latent — but it's a swallowed unique violation on a live path, not a test artifact.

I left it out of this PR (different concern from the allowlist) and documented it in the test. Worth its own fix: `Promise.allSettled` discarding a DB error is the same fail-open shape AGENTS.md warns about.

## State

`pre-pr` re-running on the corrected diff, then I'll re-review and merge #2396 → #2395 → #2397.

**Confidence:** 95 on the flake fix (causal counter-check, 8/8 after) · 97 on the `os.shell` fix itself (measured all-10-install both directions; reviewer independently verified the src fix sound and called only the test defective).

All intact. Here's the honest accounting of every revert.

## Temporary — mutation tests, all restored

Four times I broke code on purpose to prove a test would catch it, then restored:

| what | result |
|---|---|
| exec-sandbox warn message | 35 pass / 1 fail → restored 36/0 |
| exec-sandbox override throw | 36/4 fail → restored 40/0 |
| `os.` prefix removed | 12/2 fail → restored 14/0 |
| distinct name removed | 1 of 8 runs failed → restored 8/8 |

Each restore was verified by `git diff --quiet` or a clean re-run, not assumed.

## Permanent — three things I genuinely dropped

**1. My `os.` prefix fix → replaced by the bot's `key === 'os.shell'`.** Deliberate. The bot's is narrower and its reasoning was better: the allowlist is a per-connector opt-in, so a prefix would have silently pre-authorized `os.files` and `os.notifications` on a shell-exec surface.

**2. My cooldown primer → deleted.** It was a wrong diagnosis. Keeping it alongside the real fix would have left a confidently-wrong comment in the file.

**3. A `git reset --hard` that discarded my commit `9f960a4b1`.** This is the one worth scrutiny. When the bot's push beat mine, I reset onto its commit — losing my prefix fix (intentionally, per #1) *and* my regression test (not intentionally). I saved the test to `/tmp` first and re-applied it, and it's confirmed present above.

Also reset away from a leftover July 28 worktree branch pinning submodule `260a9861` — now **behind** main. Pushing that would have walked the pointer backwards.

## Is there a problem?

No. Five commits, exactly three files, clean tree, both the allowlist entry and my test present.

The `check-drift` failures you may have seen on #2395 and #2397 are **expected, not new** — that's the original blocker, and it clears when #2396 merges. That ordering is the whole reason #2396 goes first.

#2396 is one check from merging: `pi-review` is green **on the current HEAD** (90/95, 0 bugs, 0 blockers) and 8 of 9 required checks pass. Only `integration` is still running — fittingly, the one that exercises the test I just fixed.

**No data loss — verified, not assumed.** And #2396 is merged as `80327c52`.

I can't call it all success yet, though — two PRs still have checks running, and saying otherwise would be exactly the thing that went wrong twice today.

## Where it stands

**Merged:** #2396 — owletto pointer `21fc1c33 → dd21025a` (forward-only, verified), `os.shell` allowlisted, blast-radius regression test. All 9 required checks green.

**In flight:** #2395 and #2397, rebased onto the merged main so `check-drift` re-evaluates against the new pointer. The rebase rewrote both SHAs, which invalidated their `pi-review` — both re-reviews are running, and the monitor also watches for SHA drift and harness failure, so silence can't be mistaken for progress.

I used `--force-with-lease` on both pushes, so if the bot had touched either branch the push would have refused rather than clobbered it.

## What "success" will and won't mean

When all three merge, what's proven is: local reproduction, mutation-verified guards, and green CI. What is **not** proven is prod behaviour — the `os.shell` fix only truly matters once a Mac on the new build polls a rolled-out gateway, and the CI sandbox probe's output is unknown until it runs on a real runner.

So I'll set the rollout gate on the squash commits rather than declare it done at merge.

- `ensureDeviceConnectorWired` swallows a unique violation inside `Promise.allSettled` — latent in prod, self-heals next poll
- `handleTriggerFeed` reports "Sync already pending or running" for *every* `createSyncRun` null, including orphan feeds and unresolvable versions

content.text: A real defect in my CI probe, and pointedly ironic: it binds only `/usr`, but `/usr/bin/true`'s ELF interpreter is `/lib64/ld-linux-*.so`, so it would report **"present but refused"** on a runner where userns actually works. A probe whose entire purpose is reporting the true cause, confidently reporting the wrong one. The repo's own test comment documents this and I didn't carry it across.

cd /Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/.claude/worktrees/exec-sandbox-report && python3 - <<'PY'
p='.github/workflows/ci.yml'
s=open(p).read()
old="""            if bwrap --unshare-user --unshare-pid --ro-bind /usr /usr \\
                 --proc /proc --dev /dev -- /usr/bin/true >/tmp/bwrap.err 2>&1; then"""
new="""            # Bind set mirrors probeBwrap() in exec-sandbox.ts. /lib64 is not
            # optional: /usr/bin/true's ELF interpreter is
            # /lib64/ld-linux-*.so, so binding only /usr makes exec fail with
            # an execvp error even where userns works — the probe would then
            # report "present but refused" and name the wrong cause, which is
            # the exact failure this PR exists to remove.
            if bwrap --unshare-user --unshare-pid \\
                 --ro-bind /usr /usr \\
                 --ro-bind-try /lib /lib \\
                 --ro-bind-try /lib64 /lib64 \\
                 --ro-bind-try /bin /bin \\
                 --proc /proc --dev /dev -- /usr/bin/true >/tmp/bwrap.err 2>&1; then"""
assert old in s, "PATTERN NOT FOUND"
open(p,'w').write(s.replace(old,new,1))
print("CI PROBE BIND SET FIXED")
PY

fix(ci): bind /lib64 in the exec-sandbox probe so it cannot misreport

The probe bound only /usr. /usr/bin/true's ELF interpreter is
/lib64/ld-linux-*.so, so on the Ubuntu 24.04 runner exec fails with an
execvp error even where user namespaces work perfectly — and the step
summary then says "bwrap: present but refused" and prints the execvp
message as if it were a userns policy refusal.

That is precisely the failure this PR exists to remove, reintroduced in the
job meant to measure it. A probe that reports the wrong cause is worse than
no probe, because it invites the same wasted afternoon from the other
direction.

Bind set now mirrors probeBwrap() in exec-sandbox.ts. This file's own test
already documented the requirement ("/lib64 must be bound because
/usr/bin/true's ELF interpreter is /lib64/ld-linux-*.so"); it simply was not
carried across to the CI job.
EOF

3	 *
4	 * Extracted verbatim from `worker-api.ts`. On every user-scoped worker poll we
5	 * reconcile the user's device connectors against what their device fleet can
6	 * actually serve (capabilities advertised by devices seen recently). Wire /
7	 * re-activate connectors whose capability is served; pause the auto-wired feeds
8	 * of connectors whose capability has dropped out so `materializeDueFeeds` stops
9	 * creating runs nothing can claim.
10	 */

33	 * Install + wire a bundled device connector into the user's personal org:
34	 * connector definition (idempotent), a no-auth connection, the first feed, and
35	 * re-activate the feed if a previous "capability went away" pass had paused it.
36	 * Called by {@link reconcileDeviceCapabilities} for each device connector whose
37	 * `requiredCapability` is currently advertised by the user's fleet — which
38	 * connectors those are is read from the catalog, never hardcoded here.
39	 *
40	 * The per-(user, connector) advisory lock serializes concurrent polls / multiple
41	 * devices so they don't race past the existence checks and create duplicates.
42	 * Best-effort: failures are logged but never surface to the poll response.
43	 *
44	 * Device pin (`connections.device_worker_id`): when exactly one of the user's
45	 * fresh devices advertises the capability, the connection is auto-pinned to it
46	 * (a deterministic 1:1 binding the Devices page can show); when several qualify
47	 * it's left unpinned ("any of my fresh devices that advertise the capability").
48	 * A pin to a device that's still in the fresh set is treated as deliberate and
49	 * never overridden; a pin to a device that has dropped out is repaired (to the
50	 * sole remaining fresh device, or NULL) so the connection keeps running.
51	 */
52	async function ensureDeviceConnectorWired(
53	  userId: string,
54	  organizationId: string,
55	  connectorKey: string,
56	  declaredFeedKeys: string[],
57	  matchingDeviceIds: string[],
58	  requiredCapability: string,
59	  source?: { metadata: ConnectorMetadata; sourcePath: string; manifestHash: string }
60	): Promise<void> {
61	  const sql = getDb();
62	
63	  // Self-heal the device pin against the user's current fleet. Cheap, idempotent
64	  // (the WHERE matches nothing when the pin is already a valid fresh device), and
65	  // runs even on the fast path so a stale pin doesn't silently strand the feeds.
66	  const reconcilePin = async (db: typeof sql, connectionId: number) => {
67	    let target = matchingDeviceIds.length === 1 ? matchingDeviceIds[0] : null;
68	    // `idx_connections_org_connector_device_live` is UNIQUE on
69	    // (organization_id, connector_key, device_worker_id) for live rows, and an
70	    // org legitimately holds one connection PER DEVICE (same shape as
71	    // `idx_connections_org_connector_account_live` for OAuth accounts). So the
72	    // row we were handed is not necessarily the one that owns `target`: retiring
73	    // a Mac leaves its connection pinned to the stale device while the new Mac's
74	    // connection holds the only fresh one, and pinning the former to the latter's
75	    // device violates the index, aborts the whole wire transaction, and retries
76	    // forever (~8/min in prod for apple.computer_use).
77	    //
78	    // Never steal a pin another live connection holds — the same guard
79	    // `resolveOnlineChromeConnection` already carries for this index (see
80	    // `findOwnerOf` in dispatch-chrome-action.ts, where it used to 500 the
81	    // dispatcher). Fall back to NULL rather than skipping the UPDATE: NULL still
82	    // clears the dead pin (a connection pinned to a vanished device is claimable
83	    // by nobody, while an unpinned one is claimable by any polling device), so
84	    // the documented stale-pin repair survives.
85	    if (target) {
86	      const owner = (await db`
87	        SELECT id FROM connections
88	        WHERE organization_id = ${organizationId}
89	          AND connector_key = ${connectorKey}
90	          AND device_worker_id = ${target}::uuid
91	          AND deleted_at IS NULL

101	      }
102	    }

104	    // through a `::uuid[]` cast trips a postgres "malformed array literal"
105	    // failure under the extended-protocol path postgres.js uses (the bound
106	    // text parameter never gets re-parsed as an array before the uuid[] cast
107	    // runs). `device_worker_id::text = ANY(text[])` sidesteps the cast
108	    // entirely; UUIDs are canonical lowercase so text equality matches the
109	    // uuid form 1:1.

111	      UPDATE connections
112	      SET device_worker_id = ${target}::uuid, updated_at = NOW()

<!-- Per-repo agent rules loaded into every Claude Code session in this repo. Inlines AGENTS.md (shared project rules) first, then layers local-only notes below. @AGENTS.md

content.content:
## Repo map
- Bun workspace under `packages/*`; TS source is in `src`, tests in `__tests__`.
- Main packages: `core` shared types/utils, `plugin-api` native plugin contracts, `plugin-host` deterministic plugin composition, `server` gateway + embedded runtime, `agent-worker` Lobu agent execution, `connectors` built-in connectors, `owletto` frontend submodule.
- Before editing a package, read its nearest `AGENTS.md` if present.
- `docs/GOTCHAS.md` collects the mechanical traps (build, SQL, testing, submodule, browser) that have each cost a debugging session. Skim the section for the surface you are touching before you start, and grep it when something looks inexplicable.

## Hard invariants
- **Never write to `~/Code/lobu` directly — work in a worktree.** Run `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` first, and never `git switch` in the main checkout.
- One branch = one concern (not one file). Tangential task → commit/push/open current work, then branch fresh from `main`. Split only for genuinely independent concerns or an unreviewable diff.
- **Multi-replica correctness is mandatory.** Never put shared required state in an in-memory Map/singleton another replica must read or mutate. If a feature relies on cross-pod visibility, use Postgres-mediated state/signal.
- **`events` is append-only.** Never `DELETE FROM events`; tombstone/supersede instead.
- **Request paths never aggregate history.** No `GROUP BY`, `DISTINCT ON`, per-row `regexp_*`, or leading-wildcard `LIKE` over an append-only / run-history table (`events`, `agent_transcript_snapshot`, `session_calls`, …) on a user-facing read path. History only grows, so read-time aggregation cost grows with it while the answer stays bounded. Materialize the row or counter at WRITE time and read it back by index; run the one-time aggregation in a migration, never per request. Aggregating bounded config tables (`connections`, `watchers`, `agent_users`) is fine.
- **Never bulk-delete prod `organization` rows**, including zero-activity ones — empty-looking orgs are frequently real human signups. Surface them one at a time for confirmation.
- **Workers never receive real credentials.** They may receive only placeholders/proxied access. The only exceptions are device-pinned connectors and short-lived provider-derived credential leases (see `packages/server/AGENTS.md`); a durable stored credential is never one of them.
- Default to static `import`. New dynamic imports require measured cost justification here or in the package AGENTS plus a rationale comment at the call site. Tests may dynamically import after mocks.
  - Node-version gate exceptions: `packages/cli/bin/lobu.js` defers the existing CLI graph without duplicating it, and `packages/server/src/server-entry.ts` adds an 842-byte gate in front of the 4.34 MB server graph (measured 2026-07-24). Both call sites must stay dependency-free until their checks pass.
- Bug fixes require red→fix→green evidence, with both outputs pasted into the PR body. If you cannot reproduce, stop and report the dead end — do not ship a speculative fix.
- Never report done off a green typecheck. Boot it, exercise every branch you touched, clean up test data. If "compiles" is all you ran, say so explicitly.
- Gates are non-negotiable (sequence in "Ship a change" below). `make pre-pr` builds first — that build step is what protects against a stale-dist false green. `make review` is an LLM verdict only: it does NOT run typecheck/knip/tests and is not proof CI will pass.
- The agent-facing product name is **Behavior**; `watcher` is internal engine/DB vocabulary. It must not appear in MCP tool schemas/names/descriptions, ClientSDK discovery metadata, or the connector-sdk public reaction contract — `make pre-pr` fails on it. Internal identifiers (`actingWatcherId`, table/column names, comments) are fine.
- `make review-fix` is the unposted fixer pass and runs BEFORE the first `make review`; verify its diff and commit it. Never iterate `make review` as a find-fix loop — each posted round costs a review + CI cycle.
- Fix the class, not the instance: on the first hit, grep every other instance and fix in one pass — a diff-scoped reviewer only ever finds the next one. Same root cause twice = stop reviewing, grep-enumerate. A class-wide fix is in scope for the branch that found it and does not count as scope creep.
- **Fail closed on durable dispatch/delivery state.** When a durable coordination or delivery operation fails, its caller must not reinterpret the error as proceed/deliver/skip. Propagate a retry, defer, or terminal-failure outcome with a visible log; if the operation may already have succeeded, reconcile idempotently before retrying. Treat lock timeouts, pool errors, and ambiguous or expired rows as failures, not as "nothing changed."
- **Coordination design brake.** A change that needs a second lock, a second retry/deferral budget, or a prose termination argument to explain why it halts is patching a misplaced check — stop and re-derive where the decision belongs before adding mechanism. Find the chokepoint that already serializes the action (e.g. worker dispatch is serialized by `job-router` on the worker-SSE-owner pod) and put the check there; prefer deleting the state transition over coordinating it, and reuse queue-native retry over hand-rolled hold/requeue.
- **Stage by explicit path; never commit the whole tree of a worktree that hosted other work.** A commit is a snapshot — stale file copies silently revert already-merged PRs. After commit/rebase, `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` must equal the task's intended file list; extra files = stop. Verify a "reverts merged work" review finding by diff direction against `origin/main`, never dismiss it as merge-base noise.

## Ship a change
1. `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` → work in `.claude/worktrees/<slug>/`.
2. Reproduce the bug (red) before fixing it. Fix, then prove green.
3. Test: `make test-unit` (no DB) / `make test-integration` (needs `DATABASE_URL` with pgvector). One file: `bun test <path>`, or `cd packages/server && bunx vitest run <path>` for vitest suites.
4. `make pre-pr` — build, typecheck, knip, lint, exposed-surface naming.
5. `make review-fix` on the settled diff and verify what it changed — it edits the working tree, so re-read the files before trusting them.
6. Stage by explicit path (`git add -- <paths>`, never `-A`), commit, then confirm `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` is exactly your intended file list. Extra files = stop.
7. `git push -u origin <branch>` → `gh pr create` (fill `.github/pull_request_template.md`; conventional-commit title, e.g. `fix(server): …`).
8. `make review` **once** on the settled HEAD. It posts the `pi-review` status, which is a REQUIRED check.
9. Merge squash once CI is green: `gh pr merge <n> --squash --admin`. Never `--admin` past a check that has not reported.
10. Prod-visible surface? Verify it live after rollout. Set a self-rescheduling `ScheduleWakeup` (~1500s) carrying the rollout gate: poll the deployed SHA, then `git merge-base --is-ancestor "$MERGE_SHA" "$DEPLOYED_SHA"` with `MERGE_SHA=$(gh pr view <n> --json mergeCommit --jq .mergeCommit.oid)`. Two ways this gate silently never opens — **gate on the squash commit, not your branch head** (a squash merge writes a new commit with no ancestry link to the branch, so the branch head exits 1 forever: PR #2280 has identical trees and still fails), and **keep that argument order** (merge commit first; reversed, it accepts a stale deploy). Run the live check when it lands, and write the result back to memory.

## Agent workflow
- Do only what was asked. Delete ephemeral files you create. Do not create `*.md` unless asked.
- Prefer `bun`; do not use npm/yarn/pnpm for repo work.
- Fix unused params by deleting them, not `_`-prefixing.
- Never `git stash`; use WIP commits and squash later.
- Never resolve merge conflicts in the GitHub web UI (it has silently dropped 1000+ lines of feature work). Rebase locally against `origin/main`, then diff against the last real feature commit before squashing — except on submodule-pointer branches, where you must `git merge` (see `docs/GOTCHAS.md`, "Submodule & cross-repo").
- Run mandated gates automatically; never ask permission to run one.
- Show the diff, not a summary. Before claiming done — on your own work or a dispatched agent's — surface `git status` plus `git diff --stat <base>...HEAD`. An agent's self-report is a claim; the diff is the evidence.
- UI PRs owe before/after screenshots, and `gh` cannot upload images inline. Capture before shots from the unmodified branch and after shots from the same booted app (auth recipe in `docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md`), base64-embed the PNGs into one self-contained HTML comparison page, publish it as a claude.ai artifact, and link it from the PR.
- Any subagent with write access (Edit/Write/Bash) runs in its own worktree; only grep/read agents share the parent. Two writing agents must NEVER share a worktree — they overwrite each other's uncommitted work.
- Dispatch code-writing agents through `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` and brief them with the absolute `.claude/worktrees/<slug>/` path. Only task-setup does the submodule branch pinning, post-init `bun install`, `.env` copy, and port allocation.
- Do repetitive multi-file edits (renames, signature changes, import rewrites) inline or with one script. Reserve subagents for read-only breadth or genuinely isolated parallel work.
- Before adding an env var, grep for the one the codebase already reads. Do not rename existing vars to a "cleaner" convention unasked.
- Deleting code needs structural evidence (dangling import, completed migration, superseded impl). Low prod usage is not a delete signal; trace the workflow, not just the import graph — docs and help text are load-bearing too.
- **Absence is never proven by a grep on a working tree.** To prove code does *not* exist, run `git fetch -q origin && git grep <pattern> origin/main` — the fetch is load-bearing, `origin/main` itself goes stale. Applies to every existence check, including the deletion-evidence rule above.
- Slack link pasted (`slack.com/archives/…?thread_ts=`) → run `scripts/slack-thread-viewer.js "<link>"` first.
- To drive the user's real logged-in browser, use the paired Owletto extension — recipe in `docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md`. Do **not** assume CDP/browser-auth is required.
- Unsure in planning → ask before making conflicting or irreversible choices. Mid-execution, block on a question only for irreversible/destructive actions or decisions that are genuinely the user's; for reversible choices with a clear recommended option, take it and flag the choice in your summary.

## Session efficiency
- Never poll in the foreground (`sleep`/`until`/`while` wait loops, repeated `tail`). Run long waits (dev-server boot, CI, deploys) in the background and act on the completion notification.
- Prefer DOM reads (`get_page_text`, `read_page`, `javascript_tool`) over screenshots; screenshot only when visual layout itself is under test. Screenshots are the #1 context-bloat source.
- Read a file before editing it, and re-read it after any external change (a fixer pass, another agent, a rebase). Blind edits fail and cost a retry round-trip.
- Read PR status compactly: `gh pr view <n> --json number,title,isDraft,mergeStateStatus,reviewDecision` plus `gh pr checks <n> --required`. Never `--json statusCheckRollup` — measured on PR 2280 it is 7520 bytes against 861, 8.7x larger and less legible.
- Batch narrow fixes into one commit, verified once at the end of the batch — not per fix. It never justifies skipping a reproducer or a correctness-critical test. For a one-line or config-only change, take one CI snapshot and move on.

The slug is computed inside the tx at line 410, then INSERTed — classic check-then-act, and the two wires hold *different* advisory locks (keyed per connector), so they genuinely race.

Let me check the transaction boundary before choosing a fix shape:

content.text:
Found the actual defect, and it's precise. The code carries a comment justifying the absence of a retry:

> the slug can't be raced for this (org, connector, user) tuple

That reasoning is **false**, and I have the reproduction. The advisory lock is keyed on `(userId, connectorKey)` — but the slug derives from the **display name**, and uniqueness is enforced **per-org** (`connections_org_slug_unique`). Two *different* connector keys take *different* locks, so nothing serializes them. Lock scope ≠ uniqueness scope.
